guides.title: Replace the crankshaft rear oil seal by engine variant
guides.summary: Renew the rear crankshaft oil seal using the correct retainer-sealing or seal-installation method for the fitted engine.
guides.introduction: The rear crankshaft seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft exits toward the transmission. Access is behind the flywheel or flexplate. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures include sealing a retainer joint, while the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures use tools to remove and seat the seal in its bore.
guides.why: A clean sealing surface and correctly seated seal are essential to containing oil. Retainer installation must preserve the applied silicone bead and meet its assembly deadline. The V8 crankshaft sensor ring needs careful handling, and the 5.2L seal has its own installation orientation.
searchTerms: oil leak at rear of engine

when.summary: When repair calls for replacement of the crankshaft rear oil seal after the leak source is established.
notes: Choose the engine branch before ordering parts or arranging installation tools.
Plan access through the applicable flywheel or flexplate procedure and its support requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare retainer-service materials
prepare.detail: For 2.3L and 3.7L work, obtain Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357 and follow the sealing-surface preparation procedure. RTV means room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone. The 2.3L also needs installer 303-328, oil-drain equipment, a new oil filter and the specified engine oil.

prepare.title: Provide the V8 seal tools
prepare.detail: The 5.0L uses remover 303-519 with slide hammer 100-001. The 5.2L uses a universal seal puller. Both use installer 303-1250 with handle 205-153. Confirm replacement parts against engine identification.

prepare.title: Use the correct assembly lubricant
prepare.detail: The 3.7L specifies clean SAE 5W-20 synthetic-blend oil for the seal. The 5.0L specifies clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil.

prepare.title: Arrange the required scan-tool completion
prepare.detail: On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the specified misfire-monitor profile-correction routine. Flywheel or flexplate restoration includes this electronic completion step; a road test is a separate check.

steps.title: Expose the rear seal
steps.body: Remove the applicable flywheel or flexplate on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L; remove the flywheel on the 5.2L. For the 3.7L and both V8s, remove the crankshaft sensor ring and engine-to-transmission spacer plate. Inspect the V8 sensor ring and discard it if dropped or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Remove the seal using the engine's method
steps.body: On the 3.7L, first disconnect and remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, then remove the oil-pan-to-rear-seal bolts. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, unbolt and remove the rear-seal assembly and discard the seal; complete [RTV surface preparation](#/document/G1692003). On the 5.0L, use its specified remover and slide hammer. On the 5.2L, use a universal seal puller. Discard the removed seal in every branch.

steps.title: 2.3L: seal and install the retainer
steps.body: Follow [the 2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660464): apply a 3 mm silicone bead to the oil-pan surface and 5 mm beads at the T-joints. Fit installer 303-328. Introduce the retainer at an angle above the pan flange, then tilt it onto the block without scraping away sealant. Seat the seal, tighten the bolts in the illustrated sequence and remove the tool. Secure the assembly within 10 minutes; otherwise remove the sealant, clean and restart.

steps.title: 3.7L: complete its separate retainer procedure
steps.body: Follow [the 3.7L bead paths](#/document/G1681514) for the separate 5 mm and 3 mm silicone beads. Lubricate the seal with specified oil. Angle the retainer above the pan flange and tilt it onto the block, installing and tightening it within 10 minutes of sealant application. Tighten the retainer bolts in sequence and the oil-pan bolts through their torque-and-angle stages. Reinstall and reconnect the CKP sensor.

steps.title: 5.0L: install the lubricated seal
steps.body: Lubricate the seal bore and lips with clean engine oil. Position installer 303-1250 on the crankshaft, slide the new seal onto it and use handle 205-153 to install it through [the 5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685316).

steps.title: 5.2L: preserve the unique seal orientation
steps.body: Lubricate the retaining-plate bore and seal lips with specified 5W-50 oil. Position installer 303-1250, check the seal orientation in [the 5.2L installation detail](#/document/G1800269), and slide on the new seal. Install it using the specified handle and installer.

steps.title: Complete oil service and reassembly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, drain the oil after seal installation, refit the drain plug, discard the filter and fit a new filter with its seal lubricated. Follow the stated tightening instructions and refill using [2.3L oil specifications](#/document/G1660452). Restore the sensor ring and spacer plate on the applicable engines, then reinstall the correct flywheel or flexplate.

steps.title: Complete the engine-specific misfire-monitor routine
steps.body: After restoring the flywheel or flexplate, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with a diagnostic scan tool on the 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, use the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine. Follow the relevant flywheel or flexplate procedure for that engine; do not transfer this requirement to the 2.3L branch.

steps.title: Road test after assembly and required electronic completion
steps.body: Perform the road test required by the selected rear-seal procedure after reassembly and any applicable profile-correction routine. Record the result separately from the scan-tool operation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect silicone on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Use the specified Motorcraft sealant. The procedure warns that unsuitable sealant can cause excessive oil foaming and serious engine damage.

watchFor.title: Sealant scraped from the joint
watchFor.body: Preserve the angled retainer approach on the 2.3L and 3.7L so the oil-pan flange does not wipe away the bead.

notes: Use the tightening sequences and seal illustrations for the selected engine. The 5.2L seal orientation is unique to its procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L crankshaft sensor ring was dropped or shows visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The ring is unsuitable for reuse under the stated inspection rule.
diagnostics.next: Discard it and install a replacement during reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm branch completion
verification.body: Confirm seal installation and surrounding reassembly against the selected procedure. Record completion of the required oil and filter change on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record the applicable profile correction
verification.body: For the 3.7L and 5.0L, record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. For the 5.2L, record the PCM Misfire Monitor Profile Correction result. Keep that record distinct from the subsequent road-test result.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Perform the required road test after reassembly and record the repair outcome and any remaining concern.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L rear-seal retainer replacement, silicone application and subsequent oil/filter service.
3.7L rear-seal retainer replacement, CKP access and silicone-sealed reassembly.
5.0L rear-seal extraction and installation with the specified tools.
5.2L rear-seal replacement, lubrication and unique seal orientation.
RTV sealing-surface cleaning and preparation for retainer installation.
2.3L engine-oil specifications for the required refill.
3.7L flexplate removal and installation for rear-seal access Includes the required engine-specific scan-tool misfire-monitor profile correction.
3.7L flywheel removal and installation for rear-seal access Includes the required engine-specific scan-tool misfire-monitor profile correction.
5.0L flexplate removal and installation for rear-seal access Includes the required engine-specific scan-tool misfire-monitor profile correction.
5.0L flywheel removal and installation for rear-seal access Includes the required engine-specific scan-tool misfire-monitor profile correction.
5.2L flywheel removal and installation for rear-seal access Includes the required engine-specific scan-tool misfire-monitor profile correction.

authoring.method: Codex review of engine-specific linked completion requirements

guides.title: Remove and replace the brake master cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the brake master cylinder, renew its mounting nuts and complete the bleeding branch appropriate to replacement or temporary removal.
guides.introduction: The brake master cylinder converts brake-pedal input into hydraulic pressure for the braking system. Its reservoir supplies fluid, and manual-transmission vehicles also have a clutch supply connection that must be addressed during removal. The job changes or temporarily removes the cylinder, opens hydraulic connections and therefore requires the appropriate bleeding work before completion.
guides.why: Air introduced into a hydraulic circuit can compress instead of transmitting pedal movement effectively. That makes bleeding part of the repair, not an optional final task. Sealing open connections protects the system from contamination, and the cylinder’s mounting nuts must be replaced after removal.

when.summary: When the master cylinder requires replacement or must be removed to reach another component.
notes: Choose the bleeding route according to whether a new cylinder is installed or the original cylinder is refitted.
Manual-transmission vehicles also require clutch bleeding.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Have the applicable bleeding procedures and equipment ready before opening the system. For manual-transmission vehicles, provide a suitable suction device for emptying the reservoir.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement nuts and closures
prepare.detail: Obtain new master-cylinder mounting nuts, suitable closures for hydraulic openings, and torque tools for the mounting nuts and brake-tube fittings.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, wash the affected area immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Disconnect the manual-transmission supply branch
steps.body: On manual-transmission vehicles, remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid with a suitable suction device. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder tube and detach its bracket from the master-cylinder studs.

steps.title: Release the electrical and brake connections
steps.body: On all vehicles, disconnect the fluid-level sensor connector and detach the harness retainer from the reservoir. Disconnect the two brake-tube fittings, ensuring all openings are sealed.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder and discard its nuts
steps.body: Remove the two mounting nuts and the brake master cylinder. Discard both nuts; the [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692560) requires replacement fasteners.

steps.title: Reinstall the cylinder and connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using new mounting nuts. Tighten the nuts to 23 Nm and the brake-tube fittings to 27.5 Nm. Restore the sensor connector, harness retainer and, where applicable, the clutch tube, bracket and reservoir cap.

steps.title: Complete the correct bleeding operations
steps.body: For a new cylinder, follow [Component Bleeding](#/document/G1694693) to bleed the master cylinder. If the original cylinder was removed for access and refitted, follow Brake System Pressure Bleeding. Manual-transmission vehicles additionally require clutch bleeding.

steps.title: Complete the replacement check
steps.body: When a new master cylinder has been installed, road-test the vehicle after the required bleeding work is complete. Record that result separately from the hydraulic assembly work.

watchFor.title: Open hydraulic ports
watchFor.body: Keep all disconnected openings sealed. Leaving them exposed defeats the contamination precaution required during removal.

watchFor.title: Reused mounting nuts
watchFor.body: Do not reinstall the discarded cylinder mounting nuts.

notes: Manual-transmission vehicles need clutch bleeding after the hydraulic supply has been opened. The linked procedure is used by both MT82 and 3160 installation instructions; follow it with the fitted gearbox’s restoration requirements.
Use the complete named Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure when refitting a cylinder removed for access; no substitute bleeding sequence is given here.

diagnostics.finding: A new master cylinder is being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement branch requires master-cylinder bleeding and a road test.
diagnostics.next: Complete Component Bleeding, any applicable clutch bleeding and the road test.

diagnostics.finding: The original cylinder is being refitted after access work.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure directs brake-system pressure bleeding.
diagnostics.next: Complete that bleeding route and clutch bleeding if the vehicle has a manual transmission.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm new mounting nuts, tightened tube fittings, restored electrical connections and the applicable clutch supply attachments.

verification.title: Record the hydraulic completion route
verification.body: Record whether the cylinder was renewed or reused, which bleeding operations were completed, and the road-test result when replacement required it.

procedures.purpose: Master cylinder removal and installation, including manual-transmission preparation and conditional bleeding and road-test requirements.
Master-cylinder bleeding when a new cylinder is installed.
Required clutch-system bleeding after the manual-transmission clutch supply is restored.

authoring.method: Codex review of engine-specific linked completion requirements

guides.title: Replace a front brake disc with 2-, 4- or 6-piston calipers
guides.summary: Replace the front brake disc while supporting the caliper, renewing its mounting bolts and cleaning the disc mating surfaces.
guides.introduction: The front brake disc rotates with the wheel. When the caliper presses the brake pads against it, friction slows the vehicle and produces heat. Replacing the disc requires moving the caliper and pads aside to expose it. Identify the fitted brake package first: the two-piston assembly uses an anchor bracket, while the larger calipers have their own mounting arrangement. The removed mounting bolts are renewed in all three branches.
guides.why: A caliper is too heavy to leave hanging from its flexible brake hose: doing so can damage the hose. Clean mating surfaces help the disc sit properly against its mounting face. Correct bolt handling and the final brake-pedal check are essential parts of completing the repair.

when.summary: When a front brake disc has been identified for replacement or must be removed for related service.
notes: Identify the fitted caliper before starting so the correct replacement fasteners are available.

prepare.title: Wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Provide safe vehicle support for wheel removal and a means of supporting the caliper independently of its hose. Follow the linked Wheel and Tire procedure.

prepare.title: Cleaning and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have a wire brush, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner PM-4-A or PM-4-B, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench. Obtain new mounting bolts for the fitted two-, four- or six-piston brake assembly.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and identify the brake branch
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to expose the brake. Select the matching caliper branch in [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784) so the correct mounting points and replacement hardware are identified.

steps.title: Move the caliper and pads aside
steps.body: Remove and discard the two mounting bolts, then position the caliper and pads aside with their weight supported. For the two-piston assembly these are the caliper-anchor bolts, not the separate guide-pin bolts. The four- and six-piston caliper mounting bolts are also discarded.

steps.title: Remove the disc
steps.body: With the caliper clear, remove the brake disc. Keep the supported caliper from loading the hose while working around the exposed mounting area.

steps.title: Prepare the mating surfaces and fit the disc
steps.body: Clean the brake disc mating surfaces with the wire brush and specified brake cleaner. Refit the disc as part of reversing the removal sequence, ensuring the cleaned mating surfaces come together properly.

steps.title: Reassemble the brake and wheel
steps.body: Reposition the caliper and pads. Install new mounting bolts and tighten them to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) for the selected disc-service branch. Reinstall the wheel using its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight on the hose
watchFor.body: Stop and restore independent support if the caliper starts hanging from the brake hose.

watchFor.title: Discarded bolts returning to service
watchFor.body: Keep all removed anchor or caliper mounting bolts separate from the new installation hardware. Do not confuse the two-piston anchor attachments with the separate caliper guide-pin fasteners.

notes: Use the wheel procedure for wheel-fastener requirements; the caliper bolt torque applies only to the caliper attachment.

verification.title: Check brake operation
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake system operation before considering the work complete.

verification.title: Record the fastening check
verification.body: Record the fitted caliper branch, required bolt renewal and completed caliper-bolt torque check.

procedures.purpose: Front brake-disc removal and installation with the exact two-, four- or six-piston mounting arrangement.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for access to the front brake.
Two-piston anchor-plate mounting and the requirement to discard and renew its bolts.

authoring.method: Codex independent original-image and linked-prerequisite review

guides.title: Replace and configure the electric power steering gear
guides.summary: Remove the electric steering gear, rebuild its tie-rod and boot connections, and complete configuration and front-toe adjustment.
guides.introduction: The electric power-assisted steering (EPAS) gear converts steering input into sideways rack movement, while an electric motor reduces the driver's effort. Its power steering control module (PSCM), motor and torque sensor are serviced together as an assembly. Replacement combines mechanical steering work with electronic configuration; the separately serviceable tie rods and bellows boots also require careful assembly.
guides.why: An incorrectly centered gear can damage the steering gear or clockspring when the column is connected. Reused column bolts can allow shaft detachment, and poorly sealed bellows can draw water into the gear during steering movement. Correct configuration makes the replacement module match the vehicle, while front-toe adjustment addresses the wheel alignment disturbed by tie-rod work.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the steering gear assembly requires removal or replacement.
notes: Heavy steering or a warning message does not, by itself, prove that the gear has failed.
Follow the engine, transmission, convertible-bracket and underbody-equipment branches that match the vehicle.

prepare.title: Arrange mechanical and electronic capability
prepare.detail: Provide safe underside access, a steering-wheel holding device, rack holding tool 204-816, a suitable crowfoot or open-end wrench, torque equipment and boot-clamp pliers. A replacement gear requires a configuration-capable scan tool; front-toe measurement and adjustment are also needed.

prepare.title: Have the replacement hardware ready
prepare.detail: Renew the removed inner tie rods, steering stops, bellows boots and clamps, both main gear bolts and the column shaft bolt. Renew the coupler bolt if removed for a new gear. Replacement gears have a separate kit containing inner rods, boots, clamps and jam nuts for installation after the gear is mounted.

prepare.title: Prepare branch-specific materials
prepare.detail: The 2.3L operation requires oil-drain equipment, a new oil filter and the specified engine oil. Boot mating surfaces require Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-E1 meeting ESA-M1C75-B.

prepare.title: Plan battery isolation after saving configuration
prepare.detail: Retrieve the required PSCM configuration before disconnection. Then follow Battery Disconnect and Connect before steering-linkage work; battery-ground isolation is required by the tie-rod-end procedure and must already be complete before the 3.7L starter-cable work.

steps.title: Save configuration and release the dash seal
steps.body: Before removing a gear being replaced, connect the scan tool and retrieve PSCM configuration. Follow the [complete steering gear procedure](#/document/G1686680). Remove the dash-seal nuts, loosen the seal, and hand-start the nuts again. Preserve its foam and brackets. After saving configuration, disconnect the battery ground cable through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Hold the steering wheel straight ahead, remove both tie-rod ends, and remove applicable shields, support brackets and V-brace.

steps.title: Disconnect the column and strip the inner rods
steps.body: Discard the column shaft bolt, separate the shaft from the lower coupler without hammering or prying, and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Disconnect EPAS wiring and release its retainers. Remove and discard both boots' clamps; move the boots and stops aside. Move the rack fully left and use tool 204-816 on the left side to hold it while removing both inner rods. Reverse the tool for the right-hand rod. Discard the rods and stops.

steps.title: Clear the applicable engine equipment
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove and discard the oil filter and, with automatic transmission, move the cooler tubes aside through their bracket fasteners. On the 3.7L, follow the starter-solenoid battery-cable, solenoid-wire and engine-ground disconnections. Follow the transmission-specific bracket branch for the wiring and cooler tubes. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, release the specified oil-pan wiring retainers; the 5.2L also requires moving the oxygen-sensor harness.

steps.title: Remove the gear through the available clearance
steps.body: Remove and discard the left- and right-hand gear bolts and remove the convertible support bracket if fitted. Set the rack end flush with the right-hand side of the case. Slide the gear left, then rotate it and lower its right-hand side to extract it. When fitting a new gear, remove the coupler from the old assembly and discard its bolt.

steps.title: Mount the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the transferred coupler with a new bolt when applicable. Raise the gear's left side and slide it left, then raise the right side and slide the assembly into position. Finger-tighten the convertible bracket bolt if fitted and both new main gear bolts. Tighten the bracket, right-hand gear bolt and left-hand gear bolt as directed.

steps.title: Restore engine-specific connections
steps.body: Refit the disturbed wiring retainers and transmission brackets. On the 3.7L, restore the engine ground, solenoid wire and battery cable, then close the cable cover. On the 2.3L automatic, restore the cooler-tube brackets; install a new oil filter using its specified tightening stages. Keep these oil and starter operations within their own engine branches.

steps.title: Install the inner rods and airtight bellows
steps.body: Position new stops and move the rack fully left. Hold the rack with tool 204-816 while tightening the new inner rods, reversing the tool for the right side. Seat each stop by hand until it clicks and cannot be pulled off by hand. Apply the specified grease to the boot mating surfaces. Fit new boots over the housing beads and rod grooves, install new inner and outer clamps, and thread on the jam nuts.

steps.title: Center the gear before joining the column
steps.body: Reconnect and secure the EPAS harness. Turn the gear input fully right, then fully left, and return it to center before connecting the held steering column. Fit a new column shaft bolt without forcing the joint. Carry out the Steering Column Collapsed Check before completing reassembly.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding structure
steps.body: Reinstall the applicable V-brace, shields and support brackets, then both tie-rod ends. Position the dash seal and tighten its nuts. Turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock to ensure the steering stops are fully seated.

steps.title: Complete oil restoration, configuration and alignment
steps.body: Complete the linked reassembly and battery-connection procedure once the mechanical and electrical connections are restored. For the 2.3L, fill with clean engine oil using its engine specifications. Configure a new gear using the previously retrieved information or vehicle As-Built data, following scan-tool instructions. Finally, check and, if needed, adjust front toe through Front Toe Adjustment (204-00).

watchFor.title: Column force or seal damage
watchFor.body: The dash seal must be loosened before lower-coupler work. Forcing the shaft can damage steering components; damaged seal foam or separated brackets can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

watchFor.title: Water entering the bellows
watchFor.body: Use new boots and proper clamps. Zip ties cannot provide the required airtight seal, and water contamination can damage the inner-joint grease.

watchFor.title: Rack position serving different purposes
watchFor.body: Full-left rack travel provides tie-rod tool clearance; a rack end flush with the right-hand case provides extraction clearance. Centering is required later, before column connection.

notes: The 2.3L oil specification in this operation is SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend, WSS-M2C946-B1. Do not apply this branch's oil instructions to the other engines.
If module programming occurs during installation, follow scan-tool key-cycling instructions and clear communication faults caused by programming.

diagnostics.finding: Steering assistance is reduced and steering feels heavier.
diagnostics.meaning: The PSCM can reduce assistance for low voltage, high voltage or over-temperature conditions.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the recorded condition before deciding that the gear assembly requires replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Electrical assistance is absent.
diagnostics.meaning: A critical detected concern can place EPAS in manual steering mode, leaving mechanical steering with heavy effort.
diagnostics.next: Use the stored diagnostic trouble codes and system diagnosis to establish the cause.

diagnostics.finding: The identified defect is confined to a tie rod or bellows boot.
diagnostics.meaning: These parts are separately serviceable, whereas the PSCM, motor and torque sensor form the serviced gear assembly.
diagnostics.next: Select the repair scope that matches the established fault.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical checks
verification.body: Complete the lower-shaft collapsed check, verify each stop's hand-retention check, and perform the final lock-to-lock seating operation.

verification.title: Confirm electronic completion
verification.body: For a new gear, record successful scan-tool configuration using saved configuration or As-Built data.

verification.title: Record alignment and fluid completion
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment. On the 2.3L, confirm completion of the specified oil refill.

procedures.purpose: Complete steering gear removal and installation, including engine and equipment branches, rack positioning, new hardware and final checks.
Retrieve and restore PSCM configuration through programmable module installation and As-Built data when directed.
Remove and reinstall the outer tie-rod ends on both sides.
Inspect the steering column lower shaft after gear reconnection.
Apply the 2.3L engine specifications during the required oil refill.
Disconnect battery ground before steering-linkage and starter-cable work, then reconnect through the specified completion procedure.

guides.title: Overhaul the 2.3L EcoBoost engine
guides.summary: Remove, inspect and rebuild the 2.3L EcoBoost engine, then reinstall it and complete the required checks and misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: This turbocharged, direct-injection engine uses overhead camshafts to operate the valves and a pressure-fed lubrication system to protect its bearings, timing components and turbocharger. An overhaul opens these systems for inspection and measured rebuilding. It combines vehicle removal, precision bench work, engine timing and final commissioning; each phase depends on the preceding work being correct.
guides.why: The crankshaft pulley and timing sprocket rely on friction rather than locating keys. Loosening the pulley bolt releases that relationship, so incorrect positioning can damage valves and pistons. Cleanliness, bearing selection and controlled assembly also matter: debris or an incorrect clearance can undermine an otherwise careful rebuild.

when.summary: When internal damage or measured wear justifies engine removal, inspection and rebuilding.
notes: Confirm engine identification before ordering parts; build revisions affect the crankshaft sprocket and timing-chain tensioner.
Choose the transmission branch throughout removal, bench work and installation.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and precision assembly capability
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, engine crane and lifting brackets, mounting stand, transmission support, measuring equipment, torque-and-angle tools, piston ring compressor, timing tools and the specified seal and injector tools. A compatible diagnostic scan tool is needed at completion.

prepare.title: Make the vehicle and fuel system ready
prepare.detail: Follow the lifting procedure with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Use the specified lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Release fuel pressure, disconnect the battery ground and drain the cooling system and engine oil in the removal sequence. Plan the matching fuel-system restoration and leak checks before any commissioning step starts the engine.

prepare.title: Organize parts and replacement supplies
prepare.detail: Provide clean, identified storage for bearings, caps, tappets and shims. Prepare the specified sealants and every replacement required by the discard instructions, including fasteners, seals, gaskets, the high-pressure fuel tube, cylinder-head temperature sensor and turbocharger oil supply filter.

steps.title: Remove the engine with the transmission supported
steps.body: Follow [engine removal](#/document/G1660475). Mark the hood position, remove the access components and disconnect the cooling, intake, fuel, vacuum and electrical connections. Support the air-conditioning compressor aside. For the 6R80, mark a converter stud against the flexplate and discard the converter nuts, rotating the crankshaft only clockwise. Fit the lifting brackets and crane, support the transmission bellhousing with the jack and wooden block, then release the remaining mounting connections in sequence and lift out the engine.

steps.title: Mount the engine and strip its external systems
steps.body: Use [engine disassembly](#/document/G1660477). Remove the automatic flexplate or manual clutch and flywheel before mounting the engine on its stand. Discard the specified fasteners; loosen the clutch pressure plate evenly and control friction dust without compressed air. Remove the harness, manifolds, turbocharger, cooling parts and accessories in order. When opening the high-pressure fuel tube, wrap the pump flare nut with a shop towel to catch residual fuel; discard the tube. Extract injectors along their axes with the specified tools.

steps.title: Secure timing before opening the valve train
steps.body: Establish top dead center using the crankshaft timing peg and camshaft alignment tool before loosening the pulley bolt. Follow the alignment retry sequence if the camshaft tool will not fit. Hold the pulley with the strap wrench and use the specified impact equipment for removal; discard its bolt and washer. Remove the timing drive and variable camshaft timing units. Record camshaft lobe positions, cap orientation and tappet locations, then release the camshaft caps progressively in the illustrated sequence before removing the head.

steps.title: Expose and inspect the lower engine
steps.body: Remove the sump, pickup, rear seal and oil-pump drive. Index the balance shaft assembly at top dead center and preserve its shim positions; do not dismantle the assembly. Identify connecting rods, caps and bearings before removing the pistons and crankshaft. Protect cylinder walls and journals throughout. Inspect pistons and check cylinder-head and block distortion through the referenced procedures. Clean head-gasket faces with a plastic scraper, clear bolt holes and keep debris out of oil and coolant passages.

steps.title: Measure and assemble the crankshaft, pistons and balancer
steps.body: Follow [engine assembly](#/document/G1660482). Record journal and housing measurements and use its charts to select bearings. Original bearing-beam and connecting-rod bolts are used for the prescribed measuring stages, then discarded before final assembly with new bolts. Lubricate bearings, retain any reused bearing positions and perform the crankshaft fore-and-aft positioning before tightening the beam. Measure end play. Install correctly oriented pistons with the specified ring-gap arrangement and verify smooth crankshaft rotation after each rod cap. Refit the indexed balancer and shims, check gear meshing and measure backlash at every specified crankshaft position.

steps.title: Build the lubrication system and cylinder head
steps.body: Return the crankshaft to the prescribed timing position. Prime the oil pump with clean engine oil and turn it by hand before installation. Assemble its drive using the correct sprocket-and-washer branch, then fit the rear seal, pickup with a new gasket and aligned oil pan. Install the head with a new gasket and new torque-to-yield bolts. If the head, valves, tappets or camshafts are new, follow the complete piston-positioning and valve-clearance sequence, record each clearance and select tappets accordingly. Original reused parts follow the separate assembly branch.

steps.title: Complete camshaft timing and front sealing
steps.body: Install lubricated camshafts in their recorded orientation, applying the prescribed rear-cap sealant and progressive tightening sequence. Fit the alignment tool, new variable camshaft timing unit bolts and timing drive. Reset the fitted tensioner by its own procedure and release its pin only after tightening its bolts. Counterhold the camshafts with a wrench when tightening the timing units. Seal the front cover, install the front seal and align the pulley. Keep the crankshaft at top dead center while tightening its new bolt and washer with hand tools and a universal pulley holder. Align the crankshaft position sensor with its specified tool.

steps.title: Restore fuel delivery and external assemblies
steps.body: Fit new injector seals using the installation and sizing tools. Keep lower Teflon seals dry and install injectors within 15 minutes of sizing; seat the rail by hand without impact and use new rail bolts. Fit the high-pressure pump drive at zero cam lift, inspect its tappet, and install the pump with a new O-ring, new bolts and new fuel tube. Restore the separator, correctly oriented knock sensors, covers, new cylinder-head temperature sensor, vacuum pump, cooling system, accessories and turbocharger. Renew discarded turbocharger hardware, filter and seals; fully seat oil tubes before tightening and fit the lower coolant inlet tube first. Finish the intake, harness and transmission-specific flywheel/clutch or flexplate assembly using the specified special fasteners.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the engine
steps.body: Follow [engine installation](#/document/G1660484), including lubrication of the automatic converter pilot or manual input shaft. Align the marked automatic converter stud with the flexplate. Transfer support between crane, transmission support and the prescribed engine support as directed while securing mounts and transmission attachments. Renew converter nuts where applicable and the catalytic-converter gasket and nuts. Restore grounds, starter, supported compressor, hoses, fuel couplings, wiring, intake connections and hood using its index marks.

steps.title: Fill and commission the completed assembly
steps.body: Install a new oil filter, reconnect the battery and fill with the engine oil specified for this engine. Before any engine-running cooling-system or commissioning step, complete [fuel-system restoration](#/document/G1671508): reconnect the fuel pump driver module (FPDM), restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for fuel leaks before starting. Start only after that check and check again for fuel leaks while running. Complete the cooling-system vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure and restore the underbody shield in its specified sequence. Check the exhaust for leaks. Run the Powertrain Control Module misfire monitor profile correction routine with the diagnostic scan tool, then road-test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Alignment tools cannot substitute for counterholding
watchFor.body: The camshaft alignment tool is for positioning only. The crankshaft peg prevents travel past top dead center in one direction but does not prevent reverse rotation. Follow the separate pulley removal and installation holding methods.

watchFor.title: Sprocket and tensioner revisions
watchFor.body: Flat-faced sprockets require diamond washers on both sides; inspect and reuse undamaged washers. Laser-etched sprockets must never have them. Replacing an early sprocket means fitting the laser-etched service part and discarding its diamond washers. A cast-iron tensioner requiring replacement becomes an aluminum unit with new bolts.

watchFor.title: Different tensioner reset mechanisms
watchFor.body: For an aluminum tensioner, spread the ratchet wire clip, compress the plunger in a soft-jawed vise and pin the body. The cast-iron procedure separately compresses the plunger and releases and retracts the ratchet before pinning; never compress its ratchet assembly.

watchFor.title: Sealant timing and contamination
watchFor.body: The oil pan, front cover, valve cover and sealed rear camshaft caps have 10-minute securing requirements. Follow the specified cleaning and reapplication instructions if a window is missed. Keep sealant out of bearing journals and remove excess from pump mounting faces.

notes: Maintain a replacement checklist through disassembly: clutch/flywheel or flexplate fasteners, bearing bolts, head bolts, timing-unit bolts, pulley hardware, fuel-system consumables, discarded turbocharger hardware, crankshaft seals and specified gaskets must not be returned to service.
Some gaskets and O-rings are inspection-dependent rather than automatic replacements. Follow each assembly instruction, including the valve-cover solenoid seals and intake-manifold gaskets.
Do not clean injector tips with compressed air or the injector-bore brush. Replace the fuel rail pressure sensor if it is removed from the rail.

diagnostics.finding: Crankshaft end play is outside the specified range.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembled crankshaft does not meet the required axial-clearance check.
diagnostics.next: Record the measurement and install new parts as necessary before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Balance shaft damage, rough rotation or unacceptable gear backlash is found.
diagnostics.meaning: A damaged assembly requires replacement; an incorrect backlash measurement requires the dedicated adjustment procedure.
diagnostics.next: Do not dismantle the balancer. Use the Balance Shaft Backlash procedure when the measured clearance is outside specification.

diagnostics.finding: The high-pressure fuel pump tappet has flat spots or scoring.
diagnostics.meaning: The contacting pump and drive-lobe components also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the pump and tappet drive lobe and replace damaged components as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is present in the intake manifold following upper-engine failure.
diagnostics.meaning: Retained debris can damage the rebuilt engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold.

verification.title: Keep a measured assembly record
verification.body: Record bearing-selection measurements, crankshaft end play, all specified balancer backlash readings and valve clearances when that branch applies. Resolve unacceptable results before closing the engine.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical assembly checks
verification.body: Confirm smooth rotation after each connecting-rod cap and correct balancer gear meshing. Account for removal of timing and alignment tools and completion of the specified tightening sequences.

verification.title: Record commissioning results
verification.body: Record restoration of the FPDM connection and both the pre-start and running fuel-leak checks. Also record the exhaust leak check, completion of the misfire monitor profile correction routine and the road-test result.

guides.title: Replace a coupe rear quarter panel
guides.summary: Restore body dimensions, section and weld in the replacement outer quarter panel, then restore sealing, paint and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The coupe quarter panel forms the outer rear body side around the wheel opening and sail-panel area. This mild-steel outer panel is joined to the surrounding body through welded and bonded areas. Replacement is a specialist collision repair involving body measurement, controlled cutting, several joining methods and full finishing work.
guides.why: Cutting only the outer panel protects the underlying structure, which contains different steel grades. Adhesive, expanding foam and seam sealer serve separate purposes: bonding, noise and vibration treatment, and joint sealing. Each must be restored in its designated locations.
searchTerms: quarter panel rocker and sail panel sectioning

when.summary: When quarter-panel damage requires outer-panel replacement, with body dimensions restored first if necessary.
notes: Establish the required dimensional correction before using the replacement panel to close the repair.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair equipment and capability
prepare.detail: This work requires resistance spotwelding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, locking pliers, a spherical cutter, air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit and hot air gun.

prepare.title: Prepare joining and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Select the listed metal bonding adhesive, flexible foam repair material and seam sealer. Arrange a Ford-approved paint system and corrosion-protection work. Establish the prescribed cut, adhesive, foam and weld locations before starting.

prepare.title: Provide a new left-side filler-door assembly
prepare.detail: When left-side access requires removing the fuel filler door assembly, obtain a new assembly before reassembly. Its removal releases clips by damaging the housing, so the removed assembly cannot be returned to service.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions
steps.body: If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Use the applicable coupe and shared body measurements; convertible-specific dimensions do not define this repair.

steps.title: Remove surrounding components
steps.body: Remove the front door, luggage-compartment lid, rocker moulding, fixed glass, coupe loadspace trim, rear quarter trim, rear bumper and rear lamp assembly. On the left side, remove the fuel filler door assembly and applicable filler pipe, treating the door assembly as a required replacement. Remove the affected door striker and position the carpet and wiring harness aside.

steps.title: Separate the damaged outer panel
steps.body: Follow the illustrated rocker and sail-panel cuts in the [quarter-panel procedure](#/document/G1687585), cutting through the outer panel only. Complete both spot-weld drilling stages, then remove the panel. A hot air gun may soften adhesive and noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam, but applied heat must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement panel
steps.body: Cut the service panel to fit using the specified spherical cutter and air body saw. Drill the prescribed plug-weld holes with an 8 mm drill bit. Follow the installation locations rather than devising a general hole pattern.

steps.title: Apply materials and establish the panel position
steps.body: Apply NVH expanding foam and metal bonding adhesive to the indicated areas. Install and clamp the quarter panel in position, then perform the specified seam welding with MIG/MAG equipment.

steps.title: Complete the remaining weld stages
steps.body: Perform the resistance spotwelding stage, followed by the separate MIG welding stages in the installation sequence. Use locking pliers where directed. Each joining operation must follow its designated locations in the panel procedure.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired areas, seal all areas to production level and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection through the dedicated [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Reassemble the body
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness and install the door striker. Reinstall the removed closures, glass, trim, bumper and lighting through their individual procedures. For left-side work, install a new fuel filler door assembly and restore the applicable filler pipe; do not reuse the assembly damaged during removal.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying structure
watchFor.body: The sectioning instruction applies only to the outer panel. Keep the rocker and sail-panel cuts within that layer.

watchFor.title: Incomplete finishing
watchFor.body: Complete production-level sealing and corrosion protection as well as the visible paint finish.

diagnostics.finding: Body measurements show accident-related dimensional displacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding body needs restoration before panel replacement proceeds.
diagnostics.next: Restore pre-accident dimensions using the applicable body measurements before fitting the new quarter panel.

verification.title: Record body fit
verification.body: Record the applicable body-side and rear-panel margins and flushness against Body and Frame specifications, including the adjacent door, luggage-compartment lid, lamp and fuel door where relevant.

verification.title: Confirm repair completion
verification.body: Confirm completion of the specified joining stages, production-level sealing, refinishing, corrosion protection and reinstallation of all removed components.

guides.title: Weld-bond replacement body panels
guides.summary: Prepare and bond replacement panels using the specified resistance-spot-welding or MIG plug-welding method, then restore their protective finishes.
guides.introduction: Weld bonding combines metal-bonding adhesive along a panel flange with welded attachments. A successful repair depends on the vehicle's shape, the fit of the replacement panel and the quality of both the adhesive contact and the welds. Resistance spot welding and MIG plug welding share this purpose but require different surface preparation and adhesive placement.
guides.why: Adhesive cannot correct distorted body dimensions or poor panel fit. Welding settings and preparation determine whether the joint forms correctly, while excessive grinding weakens the flange and removes protective coatings. Finishing the visible seam is only part of the job: corrosion protection must also be restored.

when.summary: When a damaged body panel requires replacement using the specified weld-bonding method.
notes: Use the joining method required for the actual panel repair and new genuine Ford replacement components.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange frame-machine measurement, panel cutting and flange-repair equipment. Squeeze-type resistance spot welding (STRW) requires suitable welding equipment and destructive sample testing. The alternative method requires metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) equipment and an 8 mm drill bit for plug-weld holes.

prepare.title: Prepare materials and protection
prepare.detail: Use the specified adhesive, surface-preparation wipes, seam sealer and corrosion-protection materials. Follow product labels and Material Safety Data Sheets. Provide side-shield eye protection and a dust mask for grinding, chemical protection as directed, and appropriate welding eye and skin protection for workers in the weld area.

prepare.title: Address collision safety
prepare.detail: Follow [body-repair precautions](#/document/G1693182), including safety-belt inspection and examination of restraint-module and impact-sensor mounting areas and related components for damage, cracks or loose fasteners.

steps.title: Establish geometry and remove the damaged panel
steps.body: Measure the vehicle on a frame machine and straighten it if necessary. Cut away large damaged sections without entering adjacent parts or mating flanges. Drill out the remaining spot welds, remove panel remnants and repair damaged flanges with a hammer and dolly.

steps.title: Prepare the mating metal for the selected method
steps.body: For STRW, limit grinding of the original adhesive flange to 25 mm and remove galvanizing to expose bright metal. For MIG, remove paint, E-coat and galvanizing from the receiving and replacement mating surfaces. Preserve flange thickness and corners. Remove opposite-side E-coat only at the specified weld sites and clean the prepared surfaces.

steps.title: Prepare plug-weld holes and verify fit
steps.body: For MIG, make 8 mm holes matching the original spot-weld count, close to the original positions but not directly over them. Grind only the immediate hole perimeter. After drilling and grinding, clean all mating surfaces on both the vehicle and replacement panel with Motorcraft Metal Surface Prep Wipes ZC-31-B. For either method, complete the specified surface preparation before dry-fitting and clamping the replacement panel. Verify alignment, then remove the panel for adhesive preparation.

steps.title: Prepare adhesive and qualify STRW settings
steps.body: Dispense enough adhesive to confirm even flow from both cartridge components, attach the mixing tip and purge a tip-length. For STRW, prepare a representative sample with a 6–9 mm adhesive bead and weld it. Clamp the sample in a vice, peel it apart with locking pliers and measure the nugget against the [weld specifications](#/document/G1687502). Adjust settings and repeat until acceptable.

steps.title: Apply adhesive and clamp the panel
steps.body: For MIG, protect the vehicle's plug-weld locations with 25 mm tape before applying adhesive, then remove the tape so these areas remain adhesive-free. Apply a 6–9 mm bead to the prepared vehicle flange. Position the panel and slide it if adjustment is needed; do not pull it away. Clamp evenly and tightly, allowing the adhesive's glass beads to control spacing, and remove excess adhesive before it cures.

steps.title: Complete the correct welding process
steps.body: Follow the [joining procedure](#/document/G1687509) and weld specifications. STRW requires insulated clamp tips and settings appropriate to wet or fully cured adhesive; a shunt weld in an adhesive-free area is recommended, especially with cured adhesive. MIG requires plug welding at the prepared, adhesive-free sites. Either method permits welding during or after adhesive cure. Clamps may be removed after welding; follow product handling instructions.

steps.title: Finish cosmetic seams
steps.body: Apply fiber-filled filler to cosmetic section seams and rough-sand it. After adhesive cure, apply conventional filler and block-sand. Apply primer surfacer, required seam sealer and a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Restore corrosion protection
steps.body: Complete the [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508), using the specified undercoating and rust-inhibiting or cavity-wax materials. Protect repaired areas beyond the visible painted surface.

watchFor.title: Adhesive at MIG weld sites
watchFor.body: Keep the plug-weld areas clear; the STRW permission to weld through adhesive does not apply to this branch.

watchFor.title: Restricted sectioning locations
watchFor.body: Do not section body sides at door-hinge or striker anchorages. Welding within 50 mm of these locations can compromise collision protection.

notes: If a Restraints Control Module (RCM) or impact-sensor mounting area is damaged, restore its original production configuration and replace the component mounted there, regardless of airbag deployment.
Adhesive cure times and handling requirements come from the selected product label.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle is dimensionally incorrect.
diagnostics.meaning: Panel fit cannot yet establish a correct repair.
diagnostics.next: Straighten the vehicle before fitting and joining the replacement panel.

diagnostics.finding: The STRW sample nugget fails the specified size requirement.
diagnostics.meaning: The current welding setup has not demonstrated an acceptable weld.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the welder and repeat destructive sample testing.

verification.title: Record geometry and weld qualification
verification.body: Record dimensional and dry-fit results. For STRW, record the sample nugget measurement and acceptance against the specified requirement.

verification.title: Check completion beyond appearance
verification.body: Confirm the required weld pattern, adhesive handling, seam finishing and corrosion protection are complete.

guides.title: Exchange 6R80 automatic transmission fluid with a fluid exchanger
guides.summary: Use a fluid exchanger at the cooler return tube, restore the cooler connections and complete the separate transmission fluid level check.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 automatic transmission uses electronically controlled fluid flow to apply internal clutches and select gears. Its fluid therefore participates directly in engagement and shift operation. This exchange method connects a service machine to the return tube after the transmission fluid cooler, allowing the exchange to help remove foreign material trapped in the cooler circuit.
guides.why: Connection location and fluid selection are both essential. The specified return-side connection includes the cooler in the exchange path. Fluid intended for this transmission must be used without supplemental additives or cleaning agents, because those products can cause internal component failure. A completed machine cycle still requires a separate fluid level check.

when.summary: When fluid exchange is required and the cooler connections are compatible with this machine-based procedure.
notes: This method excludes vehicles with solid steel cooler lines or plug-in-design fluid coolers.

prepare.title: Confirm transmission and cooler configuration
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted transmission and inspect its cooler connections before preparing the machine. The case identification tag provides the transmission part number, build date and serial number.

prepare.title: Arrange the machine, fluid and lifting capability
prepare.detail: Have a fluid exchanger, its manufacturer's operating instructions, the specified transmission fluid and a hoist. Obtain the applicable fluid specification through the exchange procedure and have the separate level-check instructions available.

steps.title: Establish that this method applies
steps.body: Confirm the vehicle has the relevant 6R80 installation and does not have either excluded cooler arrangement. Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the applicable jacking and lifting instructions.

steps.title: Connect on the cooler return side
steps.body: Following the [fluid exchange procedure](#/document/G1692051), connect the exchanger to the transmission fluid cooler return tube after the cooler. Identify that location before opening a connection; it is selected to help carry foreign material out of the cooler circuit.

steps.title: Perform the machine-controlled exchange
steps.body: Operate the fluid exchanger according to its manufacturer's instructions and the transmission specifications referenced by the procedure. Use only fluid specified for this transmission. Do not add a cleaning agent or supplemental transmission additive to the exchange.

steps.title: Disconnect the machine and restore the tubes
steps.body: Once the exchange is complete, disconnect the exchanger and reconnect every transmission fluid cooler tube disconnected for the operation. Complete this restoration before moving to the final fluid level check.

steps.title: Settle the final level through the specified check
steps.body: Carry out the [Transmission Fluid Level Check](#/document/G1692053). Follow that procedure's required conditions and decisions rather than treating the exchanger's completion indication as confirmation of the final transmission fluid level.

watchFor.title: Incompatible cooler connections
watchFor.body: Solid steel cooler lines and plug-in-design fluid coolers are explicit exclusions. Do not adapt this method to those arrangements by assumption.

watchFor.title: Additives or flushing chemicals
watchFor.body: Supplemental transmission fluid additives and cleaning agents are prohibited because they can damage internal transmission components.

notes: The transmission's electronic controls and hydraulic components both influence shift behavior. A shifting complaint alone does not establish that a fluid exchange is the necessary repair.
Use the applicable specifications and level-check procedure for fluid selection and final level decisions.

diagnostics.finding: The cooler has solid steel lines or a plug-in design.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified exchanger connection method does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Stop this procedure and establish an applicable service method before opening the cooler circuit.

verification.title: Confirm cooler-circuit restoration
verification.body: Confirm the exchanger is disconnected and all cooler tubes disturbed during the exchange are reconnected.

verification.title: Record the final fluid level result
verification.body: Record completion and the result of the separate fluid level check, including any correction it required.

guides.title: Replace the convertible luggage compartment lid latch
guides.summary: Remove and refit the convertible’s luggage lid latch while restoring its electrical connection, release cable, emergency handle and trim.
guides.introduction: The luggage compartment lid latch holds the lid closed and releases it when operated. Its installation includes an electrical connector and a release cable routed through trim and clipped alongside the wiring harness. Replacement requires access to that whole route, as well as removal of the lock cylinder and emergency release handle.
guides.why: The latch cannot be removed cleanly while its cable remains trapped by the trim and routing clips. Releasing those attachments in order avoids pulling on the cable or harness. The cover also has a retaining tab, so controlled, gentle prying is part of the procedure.
searchTerms: luggage compartment lid will not release

when.summary: When the convertible luggage lid latch requires replacement after the release or latching concern has been assessed.
notes: A release complaint alone does not identify which part of the latch, cable or electrical connection requires repair.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and latch access
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver for the latch cover and suitable fastener and torque tools. Access is needed to both the lid trim and the load compartment trim around the cable route.

prepare.title: Include the lock cylinder procedure
prepare.detail: Use the convertible-specific lock cylinder removal and installation procedure as part of the job.

steps.title: Remove the lock cylinder and emergency handle
steps.body: Remove the luggage lid lock cylinder using its linked procedure. Press down the emergency release handle’s retaining tab, then remove the handle. This frees the components that must come off before the latch cover and trim.

steps.title: Release the cover and lid trim
steps.body: Insert the flat-bladed screwdriver between the latch cover and latch. Gently pry the cover away until it disengages from the latch tab. Remove the retainers and luggage lid trim panel.

steps.title: Free the cable through the load compartment trim
steps.body: Remove the retainer and move the load compartment trim panel aside. Remove the cable retainers, then route the latch cable through the panel as shown in the complete procedure. The cable must be free before the latch is withdrawn.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the latch
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and move the wiring harness aside. Release the latch cable from the harness routing clips. Remove the mounting nuts and lift out the latch assembly.

steps.title: Install the latch and restore its connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the latch mounting nuts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), restore the cable to its routing clips and reconnect the electrical connector. Return the cable through the trim and reinstall its retainers.

steps.title: Restore the trim, handle and cylinder
steps.body: Refit the trim panels and latch cover, engaging their retainers. Reinstall the emergency release handle and complete lock cylinder installation using the linked convertible procedure.

watchFor.title: Cover resisting removal
watchFor.body: Release its retaining tab with gentle prying; the cover is not simply a friction fit.

watchFor.title: Cable still attached to the harness
watchFor.body: Free the routing clips before removing the latch, and restore that routing during installation.

notes: The installation torque is given with the removal instructions and applies when the latch nuts are refitted.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm the latch nuts are tightened, the electrical connector is connected, the cable is retained along its route and the emergency handle, cylinder, cover and trim have been restored.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top switch and overhead console
guides.summary: Replace the convertible top switch as part of the overhead console and perform initialization if the new assembly includes an intrusion sensor.
guides.introduction: The convertible top switch is a momentary rocker with UP, DOWN and neutral positions. Holding it sends a request to the roof’s control modules, which coordinate the windows and roof motors. The switch is serviced as part of the overhead console assembly, so replacement involves releasing the console and disconnecting its electrical connectors.
guides.why: The roof operates only when its enabling conditions are satisfied, and it waits for confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully down. A roof that does not move therefore does not, by itself, establish a switch fault. A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor also needs electronic initialization.

when.summary: When assessment identifies a top-switch fault requiring replacement of the overhead console assembly.
notes: Use the convertible branch of the console procedure; headliner lowering belongs to the coupe branch.

prepare.title: Prepare the console tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover to release the overhead console clips and provide access to its electrical connectors.

prepare.title: Check the replacement equipment
prepare.detail: If the new console has an intrusion sensor, arrange a diagnostic scan tool capable of Local Interconnect Network (LIN) New Module Initialization and Body Control Module (BCM) self-testing.

steps.title: Check the roof operating conditions
steps.body: Confirm the accessory delay relay is active and vehicle speed is below 5 km/h (3 mph). Opening requires the top latch to be released; closing requires any tonneau covers to be removed. These conditions help distinguish an inhibited request from a switch concern.

steps.title: Remove the overhead console
steps.body: Follow the convertible console procedure. Release its clips with the interior trim remover, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the assembly. The top-switch replacement procedure specifies assembly replacement rather than separate switch removal.

steps.title: Install the replacement assembly
steps.body: Reverse the convertible console removal sequence, reconnecting the electrical connectors and engaging the clips. Identify whether the new assembly includes an intrusion sensor before considering installation complete.

steps.title: Initialize the intrusion sensor when fitted
steps.body: For a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor, run Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization. Then perform the BCM self-test, clear its diagnostic trouble codes and retrieve them again to confirm they have cleared.

watchFor.title: Windows lower but the roof remains still
watchFor.body: The roof requires full-down confirmation from both rear quarter windows. Lack of that confirmation prevents roof movement.

watchFor.title: An equipment-dependent final step
watchFor.body: Initialization and the BCM code check apply when installing a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor.

notes: Hold the switch in the requested direction while the roof raises or lowers.

diagnostics.finding: The message center requests removal of covers or reduced speed.
diagnostics.meaning: A stated roof operating condition is preventing movement.
diagnostics.next: Correct that condition before judging switch operation.

diagnostics.finding: The roof remains inoperative with the enabling conditions satisfied.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint can involve window confirmation or roof-control faults as well as the switch.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before replacing the console.

verification.title: Verify the operating sequence
verification.body: Under the required operating conditions, confirm the held switch request lowers the windows and permits the requested roof movement.

verification.title: Record the conditional electronic checks
verification.body: For an intrusion-sensor-equipped replacement, record completion of initialization and the final BCM code retrieval result.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible rear seat backrest
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion, release the backrest mountings and locking clips, then reinstall with secure attachments and accessible safety belts.
guides.introduction: The convertible rear backrest supports the occupants and attaches to the vehicle through floor fasteners and locking clips. Removing it begins with the rear seat cushion, which exposes the lower attachments. This job changes or temporarily removes the backrest assembly; correct attachment and belt routing are essential parts of finishing it.
guides.why: The backrest must sit against its intended mounting surfaces. Objects trapped between the seat and body, or inside a seat joint, can prevent correct installation and increase the risk of serious injury. Tightened floor fasteners alone do not complete the job: the locking clips must also engage, and occupants must be able to reach their belts and buckles.

when.summary: When the convertible rear backrest needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: The rear seat cushion must be removed before releasing the backrest.

prepare.title: Arrange cushion access and tightening tools
prepare.detail: Read the linked rear cushion procedure and have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench available for the backrest floor attachments.

prepare.title: Keep the mounting area clear
prepare.detail: Remove loose objects from the working area. Keep the backrest-to-body interfaces and internal seat joints free of anything that could become trapped during installation.

steps.title: Remove the rear seat cushion
steps.body: Follow the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168). This exposes the backrest's lower attachment area and provides access to its floor fasteners.

steps.title: Release the floor attachments
steps.body: Release the fasteners securing the backrest to the floor. The illustration identifies the lower outer mounting positions. Their installation torque is 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm).

steps.title: Release the locking clips and remove the backrest
steps.body: Release the backrest locking clips, then remove the assembly using the [backrest procedure](#/document/G1709034). The clips are a separate retaining feature, so freeing the floor attachments does not by itself release the backrest.

steps.title: Refit the backrest and cushion
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: engage the backrest locking clips, install and tighten the floor attachments, and refit the cushion. Throughout reassembly, keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to the occupants.

watchFor.title: Trapped objects at a seat joint
watchFor.body: An object between the seat and body or within the seat structure can prevent correct installation. Clear the obstruction before securing the assembly.

watchFor.title: Hidden buckles or twisted webbing
watchFor.body: Correct the belt routing before completing cushion installation; a neatly fitted seat can still leave a buckle inaccessible.

notes: Use the locking-clip release instructions in the linked procedure; the floor-fastener illustration does not establish a clip-release direction.

verification.title: Confirm retention
verification.body: Check that the locking clips are engaged and the floor fasteners are tightened to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Record completion of the tightening check.

verification.title: Confirm occupant access
verification.body: With the cushion installed, verify that the belt webbing is untwisted and every belt and buckle remains accessible.

guides.title: Replace a convertible-top tension cable
guides.summary: Replace the tension cable through the roof material while preserving its routing, weatherstrip alignment and fabric attachments.
guides.introduction: The convertible-top tension cable helps maintain tension in the roof material through its front attachment and spring connection to the frame. Replacement involves carefully releasing the fabric and surrounding trim so the cable can be drawn through its existing route. Although one cable may need service, several front-panel attachments must be released on both sides.
guides.why: A partly open roof provides the slack needed to release the material. Marking weatherstrip brackets and preserving shim positions helps restore their fit. A draw cord preserves the cable route, while removing every rivet shaving prevents debris from remaining in the roof assembly.

when.summary: When a convertible-top tension cable has been identified as needing service.
notes: A roof that will not operate does not by itself establish a cable fault.

prepare.title: Prepare for fabric and rivet work
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, rivet gun and draw cord, along with equipment for the trim retainers and specified tightening torques. This job requires careful handling of roof material, clips and weatherstrip brackets.

prepare.title: Set the service position
prepare.detail: Position the top approximately 25–50 percent open. The procedure illustrations show it closed for clarity, but service requires slack in the material.

steps.title: Open access on the affected side
steps.body: Remove the [rear-panel lower weatherstrip](#/document/G1708676) on the side requiring cable service. Keep the roof in the partly open service position throughout the material-release work.

steps.title: Release the front trim and headliner
steps.body: Remove the latch handle, then the front-panel trim retainers. Release the clips beneath the trim's rear edge and remove it. Remove the headliner push pins along the back of the front panel, then remove the headliner tension brackets and retainers on both sides.

steps.title: Preserve weatherstrip positioning
steps.body: Mark both front-panel side-weatherstrip brackets at their retainers and note any shim positions. Remove both weatherstrip/bracket assemblies, then remove the roof-material push pins at the back of the front panel.

steps.title: Fold back the front material
steps.body: On both sides, pull the material backward and down to release the front-panel clips, then separate it from the double-sided tape. Roll it forward and up over the panel, then fold it back to the first crossbow to expose the cable end and stay-pad rivets.

steps.title: Expose the cable attachments
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the front panel. Beneath the removed rear weatherstrip, release the material edge trim at all five locations and pull the material outward from the frame. Lift the material in the area shown in [the cable procedure](#/document/G1708678) for access.

steps.title: Release the frame end
steps.body: Drill out the tension-cable rivet and disconnect the spring end from the frame. Remove all rivet shavings from the vehicle and convertible-top assembly.

steps.title: Preserve the route with a draw cord
steps.body: Attach the draw cord to the tension cable before withdrawing it. Pull out the cable while leaving the cord accessible at both ends of the material, ready to guide the replacement through the same route.

steps.title: Install and restore the roof attachments
steps.body: Reverse [the removal sequence](#/document/G1708678), using the cord to route the cable and restoring its spring, riveted and front attachments. Refit the material, brackets, weatherstrips, headliner, trim and handle. Restore recorded shim positions and bracket marks, using the specified fastener torques.

watchFor.title: Fabric under tension
watchFor.body: Do not use the closed-roof illustration as the service position; tension makes the attachments harder to release.

watchFor.title: Cord pulled completely through
watchFor.body: Keep both cord ends exposed so the installation route remains available.

notes: Left- and right-side operations are similar; follow instructions calling for work on both sides even when replacing one cable.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move when requested.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on control-system conditions, including rear-window full-down confirmation and removal of optional tonneau covers before raising.
diagnostics.next: Check operating conditions before attributing the complaint to the tension cable.

verification.title: Confirm routing and refitting
verification.body: Confirm the cable attachments and material retainers are restored, bracket marks and shim positions are preserved, and all rivet shavings are removed.

procedures.purpose: Convertible tension-cable removal and installation, including front-panel access, fabric release, rivet work and draw-cord routing.
Affected-side rear-panel lower-weatherstrip removal and installation for cable access.
Convertible operating conditions and window interlocks relevant to distinguishing an operating complaint from cable service.
