guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible loadspace trim panels
guides.summary: Remove the upper, middle and lower loadspace trim in sequence, then refit it without trapping the roof flap or seatbelts.
guides.introduction: The convertible's loadspace trim covers the side area around the rear seating and roof opening. The upper panel meets a seatbelt guide and convertible flap, while the middle panel must clear the front and rear safety belts. Removal provides access behind the panels or allows trim replacement; correct refitting preserves belt access and the flap's position.
guides.why: These panels use clips, and the middle panel also has a rear locating tab. Their release sequence matters because simply pulling every panel outward does not follow all its attachments. During installation, trapped roof material or twisted belts can remain hidden behind trim that appears fitted.

when.summary: When convertible loadspace trim needs replacement or removal for access behind the panels.
notes: The illustrated right side is representative of the left; left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive operations are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange roof and seat access
prepare.detail: Fully open the convertible top and have the equipment required for rear seat backrest removal. Allow room to move the panels while keeping the safety belts clear.

prepare.title: Understand the attachments
prepare.detail: Review the upper-panel clip illustration and the middle-panel rear-tab release direction before pulling on the trim.

steps.title: Remove the rear backrest
steps.body: With the roof fully open, follow [Rear Seat Backrest — Convertible](#/document/G1709034) to remove the backrest and gain access to the loadspace trim.

steps.title: Release the upper and middle panels
steps.body: Following [Loadspace Trim Panel — Convertible](#/document/G1692610), move the seatbelt guide aside, release the clips and remove the upper panel. Release the middle-panel clips, then pull forward and outward to free its rear tab. Move the front and rear safety belts aside and remove the middle panel.

steps.title: Remove the remaining trim
steps.body: Release the scuff plate clips and remove that panel. Then release the clips holding the lower loadspace panel and remove it, completing the prescribed removal sequence.

steps.title: Refit with the flap and belts clear
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Before installing the upper panel, inspect the convertible flap and move it aside if necessary so it cannot become trapped underneath. Install the upper panel and restore the seatbelt guide. Refit the backrest through its linked procedure, ensuring belt webbing is untwisted and belts and buckles remain accessible.

watchFor.title: Middle-panel rear tab
watchFor.body: Release it with the specified forward-and-outward movement after releasing the clips.

watchFor.title: Concealed belts
watchFor.body: Keep both front and rear belts clear while positioning the middle panel.

notes: Upper-panel installation includes a specific flap inspection; reversing removal alone does not replace that check.

diagnostics.finding: The convertible flap lies beneath the upper panel.
diagnostics.meaning: The flap is caught in the trim installation.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the flap clear before completing upper-panel installation.

verification.title: Inspect flap and guide
verification.body: Confirm the convertible flap is not trapped and the seatbelt guide is back in position.

verification.title: Check occupant belt access
verification.body: Visually confirm untwisted webbing and accessible belts and buckles after all trim and the backrest are installed.

procedures.purpose: Convertible upper, middle, scuff plate and lower loadspace-trim removal and installation, including flap and belt positioning.
Convertible rear seat backrest removal for trim access and subsequent installation.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace a convertible top motor and initialize the roof
guides.summary: Access the roof motor through the rear speaker area, replace it, and complete the required closing and opening initialization.
guides.introduction: The convertible roof uses two electric motors with integrated control electronics. They share movement and position information so both sides work together. Replacing a motor therefore involves both mechanical access and a final initialization cycle. The rear quarter speakers, their brackets and the motor guards must be moved before the motors can be reached.
guides.why: A roof that will not move does not automatically have a failed motor. Roof movement depends on operating conditions and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered. Establishing the reason for the fault first avoids replacing a motor when an interlock is correctly preventing operation.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a convertible top motor that requires replacement.
notes: Confirm the roof operating conditions and window status before treating non-operation as a motor fault.

prepare.title: Plan access for the fitted audio system
prepare.detail: Use the rear quarter speaker procedure for SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3, as fitted. Speakers and speaker brackets are removed on both sides.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled reassembly
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools and a torque wrench covering the small bracket fasteners and motor attachments. Keep the different fasteners identified.

steps.title: Remove the rear quarter speakers
steps.body: Remove both speakers using the appropriate audio-system procedure. Begin the remaining access work with the [motor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1708675), which distinguishes the shared operations from the extra work on the right.

steps.title: Move the right-side module assembly aside
steps.body: On the right side only, release the module wiring-harness clips from the speaker bracket. Remove the module bracket nut and bolt, then position the module and bracket assembly aside.

steps.title: Clear the speaker brackets and wiring
steps.body: On both sides, remove the speaker bracket stud, bracket nuts and bracket. Disconnect the indicated harness connectors and move the harness aside to expose the motor area.

steps.title: Remove the motor
steps.body: Remove the motor guard bracket retainers and position the guard aside. Remove the convertible top motor, following the appropriate side illustration. The motor mounting torque for installation is 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Reverse removal, restoring the motor guard, harness connections, speaker brackets, right-side module assembly and speakers. Use the individual fastener specifications in the procedure; these attachments have different tightening requirements.

steps.title: Initialize the motors
steps.body: Fully close and latch the convertible top, then release the latch and reopen it fully. Hold the roof switch throughout each movement. Remove any fitted tonneau covers before raising the roof and perform the cycle with the vehicle stationary and accessory operation available.

watchFor.title: Missing rear-window confirmation
watchFor.body: The roof remains inhibited if either rear quarter window fails to report its fully lowered position.

watchFor.title: An incomplete initialization cycle
watchFor.body: Partial roof movement does not complete the specified fully closed, latched and fully reopened sequence.

notes: Brief audio muting when the roof is latched or unlatched is normal.

diagnostics.finding: The display requests cover removal or reduced speed.
diagnostics.meaning: An operating condition is preventing roof movement; the message does not establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: Correct the indicated condition before reassessing operation.

diagnostics.finding: The roof still does not operate with the required conditions satisfied.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof or body control modules can store diagnostic trouble codes even without a dedicated warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the stored faults and window-status inputs before authorizing motor replacement.

verification.title: Record the initialization result
verification.body: Confirm and record that the roof reached fully closed and latched, then fully open after reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm access work is complete
verification.body: Check that disconnected harness connectors and clips, guards, brackets and both speakers have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Convertible top motor removal, installation and motor initialization.
Rear quarter speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Rear quarter speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Explain roof synchronization, window interlocks and roof-status messages.

guides.title: Replace the convertible B-pillar and inner reinforcement
guides.summary: Replace the convertible B-pillar structure at its factory joints, then restore its welded connections, foam, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar assembly and its inner reinforcement form part of the convertible's body structure and connect to the rear floor crossmember. Replacement is a structural body repair involving welded panels, not simply a trim or bolt-on panel change. The reinforcement is boron steel, and the repair must retain the factory-joint replacement approach.
guides.why: Correct body dimensions provide the reference for installing the replacement structure. Welding new parts into a distorted opening would preserve that distortion. The completed repair also needs its noise-control foam, seam sealing and corrosion protection restored; sound welds alone do not finish the job.

when.summary: When structural damage requires replacement of the convertible B-pillar assembly and reinforcement.
notes: Boron-steel reinforcement components cannot be sectioned; replacement must use factory joints.

prepare.title: Use a structural body-repair facility
prepare.detail: The work requires body measurement and restoration capability, resistance spotwelding, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare removal and panel-fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Have an air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit and locking pliers, together with the specified seam sealer and flexible foam repair material.

prepare.title: Plan the surrounding repairs
prepare.detail: Rear seat cushion and convertible quarter-panel removal are prerequisites. Include their reinstatement and the corrosion-prevention procedure in the repair plan.

steps.title: Establish the body dimensions
steps.body: Assess the structure against [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions before removing the pillar. Use the applicable convertible measurements where body-style-specific information is provided.

steps.title: Expose the repair area
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and convertible quarter panel using their procedures. Position the carpeting and wiring harness away from the repair area so they are clear of the removal and joining work.

steps.title: Release the crossmember and remove the foam
steps.body: Remove the rear floor crossmember-to-B-pillar bolts. Remove the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam at the pillar base using the specified air body saw operation. This does not authorize cutting a section from the boron reinforcement.

steps.title: Separate the factory-welded assemblies
steps.body: Drill out the spot welds and remove the B-pillar assembly. Then drill out the inner reinforcement's spot welds and remove the reinforcement. Preserve this sequence and the factory-joint boundaries in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1687553).

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement structure
steps.body: Drill the specified 8 mm plug-welding holes in the replacement panel. Clamp and resistance-spot-weld the inner reinforcement first, followed by the B-pillar assembly. Complete the specified MIG welding of the B-pillar panel.

steps.title: Restore the foam and crossmember attachment
steps.body: Apply the specified expanding NVH foam. Reinstall the rear floor crossmember bolts and tighten them to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), restoring the bolted connection after the welded structure is installed.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area. Seal all affected areas to production level with the specified seam sealer, then restore corrosion protection using [Corrosion Prevention](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reposition the carpeting and wiring harness. Reinstall the rear seat cushion and convertible quarter panel using their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: A proposed partial reinforcement repair
watchFor.body: Do not substitute a cut-and-splice section for factory-joint replacement of the boron reinforcement.

watchFor.title: Unfinished seams or exposed repaired metal
watchFor.body: Sealing and corrosion protection remain required after the metal finishing is complete.

notes: The illustrated left-side sequence applies similarly to the right side.

diagnostics.finding: The body is dimensionally displaced from its pre-accident condition.
diagnostics.meaning: The existing structure is not yet a suitable positioning reference for replacement parts.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required dimensional restoration before pillar replacement.

verification.title: Record dimensional restoration
verification.body: Document the applicable body measurements and any restoration performed against the Body and Frame references.

verification.title: Confirm every repair layer is restored
verification.body: Check completion of the specified welded joints, crossmember bolts, expanding foam, production-level seam sealing and corrosion protection before closing out the repair.

procedures.purpose: Convertible B-pillar and inner reinforcement removal and installation at factory joints.
Body construction information and applicable dimensional references for structural restoration.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation for access.
Convertible quarter-panel removal and installation surrounding the B-pillar repair.
Restore corrosion protection after welding and finishing.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top front panel
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the roof's front panel while preserving shims, fabric attachments and weatherstrip positions, then set alignment with the top latched.
guides.introduction: The convertible top front panel carries the front attachments for the roof material, headliner and side weatherstrips and forms the roof's front latching area. Replacing it requires carefully releasing these layers, the tension cables and the riveted stay pads. Reassembly preserves their original positions and establishes panel-to-frame alignment before final tightening.
guides.why: Partially opening the roof gives the fabric and connected parts enough slack for service. Marks and retained shims preserve the original installation references. The panel-to-frame fasteners remain loose until the roof is closed and latched, allowing alignment to be established in that position.

when.summary: When the convertible top front panel needs replacement or removal for an identified repair.
notes: Service views show a closed roof, but the working position is approximately 25–50 percent open to provide slack.

prepare.title: Tools, materials and assistance
prepare.detail: Arrange an assistant, an electric drill, a rivet gun, stay-pad rivets, double-sided tape and tools capable of the specified fastener torques. Preserve shims and mark bracket positions during removal.

prepare.title: Roof operation
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary and ensure accessory delay is active for roof movement. Release the latch before opening and remove fitted tonneau covers before raising. Roof movement also depends on confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.

steps.title: Release the roof and remove the front trim
steps.body: Begin the [front-panel removal procedure](#/document/G1708671). Lower the latch handle and turn it clockwise to release the roof. Open the top approximately 25 percent and remove the handle. Remove the front trim retainers, release the clips beneath its rear edge and remove the trim.

steps.title: Free the headliner and side weatherstrips
steps.body: Remove the headliner push pins along the panel's rear edge. On both sides, detach the headliner tension brackets from the panel; they may remain attached to the headliner. Mark the side weatherstrip brackets at their retainers, note any shim positions, and remove both weatherstrip-and-bracket assemblies.

steps.title: Release and fold back the roof material
steps.body: Remove the material's rear push pins. Across the front, pull the material backward and downward off the panel clips, then release it from the double-sided tape on both sides. Roll it forward and upward over the panel, then fold it back to the first crossbow to expose the tension-cable ends and stay-pad rivets.

steps.title: Disconnect the remaining attachments and remove the panel
steps.body: Disconnect both tension cables. Drill out the stay-pad rivets and remove every rivet shaving from the vehicle and roof assembly. Slide each stay pad toward the panel's center to disengage it. With an assistant, remove the panel-to-frame retainers and the panel, keeping any shims in their original side positions.

steps.title: Install the panel loosely and restore the stay pads
steps.body: Follow the [installation phase](#/document/G1708671). With an assistant, position the panel and restore the frame shims as removed. Loosely install the frame retainers for later alignment. Slide each stay pad outward into position, install its rivets with the rivet gun, and reconnect both tension cables.

steps.title: Reattach the roof material
steps.body: Fold the material over the panel's front. Apply double-sided tape on both sides in the original positions. Roll the material downward and rearward while engaging it over the front clips, then install the push pins along the panel's rear edge.

steps.title: Restore weatherstrips and headliner
steps.body: Refit the side weatherstrip assemblies using the marks and recorded shim positions, and tighten their retainers to specification. Install the headliner tension brackets, aligning them with the headliner's rear push-pin positions before tightening. Reposition the headliner and install its push pins.

steps.title: Set alignment with the roof latched
steps.body: Close the roof and temporarily install the latch handle and retainer; the handle retainer need not yet be tightened. Pull the roof downward to position the latch, then turn the handle counterclockwise to secure it fully. With the roof latched, tighten the panel-to-frame bracket nuts on both sides to the specified torque.

steps.title: Finish the trim installation
steps.body: Turn the handle clockwise to release the roof and open it approximately 25 percent. Remove the handle, engage the front trim's rear clips, and install and tighten its front retainers. Reinstall the latch handle and tighten its retainer. Use the separate trim and handle torque specifications in the installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Lost installation references
watchFor.body: Weatherstrip bracket marks and shims preserve distinct mounting positions. Keep those references with their original sides.

watchFor.title: Roof refuses to move
watchFor.body: Latch, tonneau-cover and rear-window conditions can inhibit operation. Failure to move does not by itself identify a defective front panel.

notes: Perform the paired cable, stay-pad, weatherstrip and bracket operations on both sides, even where a procedure view shows only one side.

verification.title: Alignment sequence completed
verification.body: Confirm that the panel-to-frame nuts were tightened only after the roof was closed and fully latched.

verification.title: Attachments and cleanliness
verification.body: Confirm that shims, rivets, cables, fabric clips, push pins, weatherstrip brackets and trim have been restored, all specified fasteners tightened, and all rivet shavings removed.

procedures.purpose: Complete front-panel removal and installation, including fabric handling, riveting, shims, closed-roof alignment and individual fastener torques.
Roof operating conditions and window, latch and tonneau-cover interlocks relevant to positioning the top.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Remove and Refit the Convertible Top Headliner
guides.summary: Release the convertible headliner from its bows, straps and rear-window trim ring, then refit it with correct routing and complete rivet cleanup.
guides.introduction: The headliner forms the interior fabric surface of the convertible roof. It attaches to the moving roof structure through bows, straps, rivets and the rear-window trim ring. Servicing it requires the complete top to be removed and both top motors detached. The work is as much about preserving attachment geometry and routing as replacing fabric.
guides.why: Drilling through a linkage instead of removing only a rivet head enlarges the attachment hole and can prevent proper riveting. Loose rivet ends inside the hollow cross bows can cause rattles. Correct strap routing and trim-ring alignment are also essential when rebuilding an assembly that folds through changing positions.

when.summary: When the convertible headliner needs replacement or removal for roof work.
notes: The top assembly must be removed for this procedure.
Adjusting the assembly’s open position may be necessary as the work progresses.

prepare.title: Roof removal and workspace
prepare.detail: Arrange the capability and space to remove the top and both motors under their complete procedures. Position the top on the ground, upside down and fully open.

prepare.title: Drilling, riveting and cleanup
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, 4.2 mm drill bit, pneumatic rivet gun, interior trim remover, vacuum cleaner, compressed air and an air nozzle.

prepare.title: Correct replacement rivets
prepare.detail: Use the specified black multigrip blind rivets: 4 mm diameter, 15 mm length and 11 mm head diameter. Preserve the original nylon-strap routing during removal.

steps.title: Remove and position the top
steps.body: Follow [Convertible Top Assembly](#/document/G1708670), position the removed assembly as specified, then remove both motors using [Convertible Top Motor](#/document/G1708675).

steps.title: Release the front attachments
steps.body: Remove the latch handle. Remove the front-panel trim’s front retainers, release its rear clips with the trim remover and lift away the trim. Remove the headliner push-pin retainers along the back of the front panel.

steps.title: Release the tension bracket and floating-bow strap
steps.body: Drill only the tension-bracket rivet head and remove the resulting shavings. Remove the nylon-strap retainers from the floating bow and route the strap through the frame to release it, preserving how it passes through the structure.

steps.title: Work through the first cross bows
steps.body: Follow [Convertible Top Headliner](#/document/G1708674) to remove the retaining rivets from cross bows 1, 2 and 3 in order. Fold the released headliner down between bows to expose the next attachment. Drill only rivet heads and remove shavings throughout.

steps.title: Release the fourth cross bow
steps.body: Remove the rivets at cross bow 4. Pull the nylon-strap end from the cross bar and push it through the headliner. The strap can remain routed over this bow; its double-sided tape assists positioning during installation.

steps.title: Account for all rivet pieces
steps.body: Remove pieces from inside every cross bow. Blow compressed air through the rivet holes to move debris toward the outer ends, using multiple holes if necessary. Check both ends of each bow, collect the pieces and verify that every rivet end is accounted for.

steps.title: Release the rear-window ring and headliner
steps.body: Carefully pry the headliner trim ring from the rear-window glass frame. Move any clips left on the frame back to their original positions on the ring. Pull the headliner straight out of the floating bow.

steps.title: Refit the headliner attachments
steps.body: Reverse removal, routing the nylon strap through the frame exactly as before. Begin attaching the rear-window trim ring at its top two corners to establish alignment, then work around the frame. Rebuild the riveted attachments with the specified rivets.

steps.title: Complete roof reassembly
steps.body: Refit the push pins, front trim and latch handle, using the individual torque callouts for the strap retainers, trim retainers and handle. Reinstall both motors and the top assembly through their linked procedures.

watchFor.title: Damage to permanent attachments
watchFor.body: The trim ring is permanently attached to the headliner, and the glass frame is permanently attached to the top material. Separate the clipped ring-to-frame connection carefully.

watchFor.title: Rivet debris hidden inside a bow
watchFor.body: Vacuuming visible shavings does not account for rivet ends inside the bows. Complete the compressed-air and collection stage before reassembly conceals them.

notes: The illustrated left-side attachment operations also apply similarly on the right.

diagnostics.finding: A rattle develops after rivet removal.
diagnostics.meaning: Rivet ends left inside a cross bow can create a rattle.
diagnostics.next: Recheck both ends of every bow and account for the removed rivet pieces.

verification.title: Record debris recovery
verification.body: Confirm and record that all rivet ends have been accounted for and all bows are clear of pieces and shavings.

verification.title: Check attachment geometry
verification.body: Confirm original strap routing, correctly positioned trim-ring clips and alignment established from the upper corners.

verification.title: Check the reassembled roof
verification.body: After completing top and motor installation, check operation with accessory delay active and the vehicle stationary. Release the latch for opening, remove fitted tonneau covers for closing and hold the roof switch during travel. The system requires rear-window full-down confirmation before moving the roof.

Complete convertible top assembly removal and installation.
Removal and installation of both convertible top motors.
Roof operating conditions and window interlocks used during the final function check.

guides.title: Replace the convertible top rear-panel lower weatherstrip
guides.summary: Release the riveted weatherstrip with the roof partly open, remove all drilling debris and secure the replacement with the specified rivets.
guides.introduction: This weatherstrip forms a sealing edge at the convertible top's rear panel and is secured with blind rivets. Replacement requires controlled removal of the rivet heads. The surrounding roof material must have enough slack for access, while the linkage holes must retain their original size for the replacement fasteners.
guides.why: Drilling through the linkage instead of stopping at the rivet head enlarges the mounting hole and can compromise rivet installation. Metal shavings must also be removed from the convertible-top assembly. Roof position matters because a fully closed top holds its material under tension.

when.summary: When the convertible top rear-panel lower weatherstrip requires removal or replacement.
notes: The right side is illustrated; the left side is similar.

prepare.title: Prepare drilling, riveting and cleanup equipment
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, 4.2 mm drill bit, pneumatic rivet gun and vacuum cleaner.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified fasteners
prepare.detail: Use silver multigrip blind rivets with a 4 mm diameter, 12 mm length and 8 mm head diameter.

steps.title: Position the roof for slack
steps.body: Follow the [weatherstrip procedure](#/document/G1708676). Open the top approximately 50 percent. Although the illustrations show it fully closed, the service position should be approximately 25–50 percent open to relax the material and adjacent components.

steps.title: Remove only the rivet heads
steps.body: Locate the illustrated weatherstrip rivets and drill their heads with the 4.2 mm bit. Control the cut so the drill does not pass through the linkage assembly. The linkage holes are to be preserved, not redrilled.

steps.title: Remove the strip and all shavings
steps.body: Remove the released weatherstrip and vacuum the drilling debris from the convertible-top assembly. All rivet shavings must be removed before installation.

steps.title: Install the weatherstrip
steps.body: Reverse removal, positioning the weatherstrip at its mountings and using the pneumatic rivet gun to install the specified multigrip blind rivets. Keep the roof in the slack service position during attachment.

watchFor.title: Roof movement unavailable
watchFor.body: Opening requires the accessory-delay relay to be active and the roof latch released. Both rear quarter windows must report fully lowered before the roof can move. Resolve access conditions before drilling.

watchFor.title: Tonneau covers during closing
watchFor.body: Remove fitted tonneau covers before commanding the roof closed.

diagnostics.finding: A drill has enlarged a linkage mounting hole.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct installation of the specified rivet may be hindered.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the mounting damage before continuing weatherstrip installation.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and cleanliness
verification.body: Check that the specified rivets secure the weatherstrip, the linkage holes have not been enlarged and no rivet shavings remain in the top assembly.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear-panel lower-weatherstrip removal and installation, including service position and rivet specification.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Adjust convertible-top tension belt buckles
guides.summary: Adjust both roof tension buckles equally, checking top operation and latching effort after each secured adjustment.
guides.introduction: The convertible top's tension belt buckles provide a mechanical adjustment to roof tension. Tightening their screws adds tension; loosening them reduces it. Because this also changes latching effort, the job is a controlled adjustment-and-test process. The roof's electric motors move the top, but buckle adjustment addresses mechanical tension rather than electronic operating faults.
guides.why: Partially opening the roof unloads the buckles before they are released. Matching the screw positions from side to side preserves equal adjustment, while recording the starting positions provides a way back if the change is unsuitable. Both buckles must be secured to the body before each operational test so the result reflects their installed condition.

when.summary: When convertible-top tension or latching effort needs correction through the tension belt buckles.
notes: Adjustments made on one side must also be made on the other.
A top that will not move requires its operating conditions to be checked before tension is altered.

prepare.title: Provide access and measurement
prepare.detail: Arrange access from both sides of the luggage compartment, a suitable means of measuring the screw positions and tools for the adjusters. Remove the subwoofer speaker if fitted, following its removal procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare to operate the top
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary with accessory delay active. Opening requires the top latch to be released; closing requires any tonneau covers to be removed. The roof switch must be held during movement.

steps.title: Relieve belt tension
steps.body: After any required subwoofer removal, partially open the top as shown in the [buckle adjustment procedure](#/document/G2401442). This removes tension from the buckles before their brackets are disconnected.

steps.title: Release both adjuster brackets
steps.body: Work from the luggage compartment on both sides. Push inward on the rear of each tension belt adjuster to release its locking tabs, then pull its rear downward to disconnect the bracket from the body.

steps.title: Record the starting screw positions
steps.body: Measure and note each screw's initial position before turning it. Check the relationship between the two sides: their positions should match. These measurements allow the adjustment to be returned to its starting setting if needed.

steps.title: Make equal changes and test
steps.body: Turn both buckle screws equally in the direction required: tighten to increase tension or loosen to reduce it. Resecure both buckles to the vehicle after every adjustment, then retest roof operation and latching effort before deciding on another change.

steps.title: Finish at the intended tension
steps.body: Continue the equal-adjustment and secured-test sequence until the intended roof tension is achieved. The fully tightened and maximum-travel loosened illustrations explain the adjustment's endpoints; neither is a prescribed target. Reinstall everything removed for access.

watchFor.title: Unequal screw positions
watchFor.body: Do not make a one-sided correction and leave the opposite buckle unchanged; the procedure requires identical positions and equal adjustments.

watchFor.title: Testing with a buckle released
watchFor.body: Reconnect both buckles to the body before operating the top after an adjustment.

notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side follows the same process.

diagnostics.finding: The top will not raise or lower.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof movement depends on operating permissions and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully down; refusal to move does not establish incorrect belt tension.
diagnostics.next: Check the opening or closing prerequisites and window-down operation before continuing buckle adjustment.

diagnostics.finding: An adjustment changes latching effort.
diagnostics.meaning: Buckle screw position directly changes roof tension and therefore affects the effort needed to latch it.
diagnostics.next: Assess the result with both buckles secured, then make another equal adjustment or return to the recorded starting positions.

verification.title: Confirm the installed result
verification.body: Verify equal screw positions, secure engagement of both brackets and satisfactory top operation after the final adjustment.

verification.title: Record the adjustment
verification.body: Keep the initial and final screw-position measurements with the observed change in roof tension and latching effort.

procedures.purpose: Convertible-top buckle access, release, equal adjustment, repeated operational testing and reassembly.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace convertible rear quarter window glass
guides.summary: Remove the rear quarter glass with its regulator, separate the glass when replacing it, then reinstall and adjust the assembly.
guides.introduction: The convertible’s rear quarter windows close the openings behind the door glass and lower for roof operation. Each glass panel is carried by a powered regulator, and both rear quarter windows respond together to the master window switch. Replacement requires removing the glass and regulator as an assembly before separating the glass when necessary.
guides.why: The glass must be fully raised before it can be separated from its regulator. Access also involves wiring, a speaker bracket and the watershield. Restoring those items and completing glass adjustment are essential parts of reassembly, rather than treating the mounting bolts as the finish point.
searchTerms: convertible rear quarter window glass replacement

when.summary: When rear quarter glass requires replacement or its glass-and-regulator assembly must be removed.
notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand operation is similar, with the stated access difference.

prepare.title: Arrange access and adjustment
prepare.detail: Plan to lower the roof, remove the rear quarter speaker and complete the linked glass adjustment afterward. Have suitable torque equipment for the bracket, assembly and glass fasteners.

prepare.title: Check whether the glass moves
prepare.detail: If the glass is inoperative, plan for regulator-motor removal so the glass can be moved to expose its attachment bolts. Do not assume glass separation is possible in its current position.

steps.title: Lower the roof and open the access area
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. On the right-hand side, remove the radio transceiver module (RTM) using its procedure. On either side, remove the rear quarter panel speaker through the linked speaker procedure.

steps.title: Move the belt mouldings
steps.body: Remove the interior belt moulding’s nut and bolt, then remove the moulding. Position the exterior moulding aside to clear the glass removal path.

steps.title: Place the glass fully up
steps.body: Raise the rear quarter glass to its full-up position. If it will not operate, the regulator motor must be removed to allow glass movement and access to the bolts. Glass and regulator cannot be separated below full up.

steps.title: Remove the speaker bracket
steps.body: Remove the bracket nuts and stud bolt. Detach the wiring retainer, move the harness aside and remove the bracket. Keep the nut and stud-bolt installation specifications distinct.

steps.title: Free the wiring and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the regulator motor connector and position the harness aside. Release the watershield and wiring retainers as directed. Remove the assembly retaining nuts and take out the glass and regulator together.

steps.title: Separate the glass only when replacing it
steps.body: If installing new glass, remove its attachment bolts and separate it from the regulator. This separation step is unnecessary when the existing glass will remain attached to the regulator.

steps.title: Reassemble and adjust
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, applying the listed fastening specifications. Restore the watershield, wiring, speaker bracket, mouldings and speaker, plus the RTM on the right-hand side. Finish with the required rear quarter window glass adjustment.

watchFor.title: Misreading the roof illustration
watchFor.body: The top assembly is absent from some views for visibility. The access instruction is to lower the top.

watchFor.title: Incomplete watershield restoration
watchFor.body: Refit the watershield and its retainers along with the displaced harness; these are part of the reverse installation sequence.

notes: Convertible rear quarter-window motors have no one-touch functions and do not require initialization.

diagnostics.finding: Rear quarter-window controls do not respond while the roof is between its fully raised and fully lowered positions.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof-control system inhibits rear quarter-window switch operation in this condition.
diagnostics.next: Account for roof position before interpreting the lack of movement as a regulator or glass fault.

verification.title: Complete the glass adjustment
verification.body: Carry out the linked convertible rear quarter glass adjustment after installation; use its criteria to establish the final glass position.

verification.title: Confirm restored operation
verification.body: With the roof at a permitted endpoint, check rear quarter-window movement from the master switch. Both rear quarter windows normally operate together.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear quarter glass-and-regulator removal, conditional glass separation and reverse installation.
Radio transceiver module removal and installation for right-hand access.
Rear quarter panel speaker removal and installation for access.
Required convertible rear quarter glass adjustment after installation.

applicability.equipment: Convertible rear quarter window; right-hand side includes radio transceiver module removal.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace the convertible top front-panel side weatherstrip
guides.summary: Remove the front-panel weatherstrip bracket, renew its riveted seal and reinstall the assembly at its marked original position.
guides.introduction: The front-panel side weatherstrip forms part of the convertible roof's sealing edge. It is attached to a bracket, which must be removed from the roof before the retaining rivets are drilled out on the bench. This job combines interior trim access, careful position marking and controlled riveting.
guides.why: The bracket has no weatherstrip adjustment, so its original mounting position must be marked before removal and reproduced during installation. Partly opening the roof relaxes the top material for access. Keeping the bracket straight and removing every rivet shaving protects both the fit of the seal and the surrounding roof assembly.
searchTerms: convertible front panel side weatherstrip replacement

when.summary: When the convertible front-panel side weatherstrip requires replacement.
notes: The left- and right-hand sides follow similar operations.
Retain reliable mounting reference marks because this weatherstrip has no adjustment.

prepare.title: Bench tools and marking
prepare.detail: Have a rivet gun, electric drill, vise, marking tool and tightening equipment suitable for the small trim and bracket fasteners. The work requires drilling rivets without bending the bracket.

prepare.title: Roof positioning
prepare.detail: Perform the work with the roof approximately 25–50 percent open to provide slack. Use the roof controls with the vehicle stationary, the accessory delay relay active and the latch released. Remove any tonneau covers before commanding the roof closed.

steps.title: Release and partly open the roof
steps.body: Begin the [front-panel side weatherstrip procedure](#/document/G1708672) by lowering the convertible top latch handle and twisting it clockwise to release the top. Open the roof approximately 25 percent, then remove the latch handle.

steps.title: Remove the front-panel trim
steps.body: Remove the retainers along the front of the trim. Release the clips beneath its back edge and remove the trim. Separating these two attachment areas in sequence exposes the headliner attachments without treating the trim as a single pull-off piece.

steps.title: Release the local headliner attachments
steps.body: Remove the headliner push-pin retainers along the back of the front panel. Remove the headliner tension bracket retainers and the bracket from the front panel. Follow the corresponding side views; some illustrations omit the headliner only for clarity.

steps.title: Mark and remove the weatherstrip bracket
steps.body: Mark the weatherstrip bracket assembly at its retainers before loosening them. These marks establish its installation position. Remove the retainers and lift out the weatherstrip and bracket assembly.

steps.title: Separate the weatherstrip on the bench
steps.body: Secure the assembly in a vise without bending the bracket, then drill out the retaining rivets. Keep the bracket straight during drilling as well as clamping. Remove all rivet shavings from the vehicle and convertible top assembly.

steps.title: Rivet and reinstall the assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the rivet gun to attach the replacement weatherstrip to its bracket. Refit the bracket at the reference marks and tighten its retainers to 7 Nm. Restore the headliner attachments, front-panel trim and latch handle using their individual tightening values in the linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Lost mounting references
watchFor.body: Do not rely on later adjustment to recover the position. The reference marks are required for installation.

watchFor.title: Bracket distortion
watchFor.body: A vise or drilling load can bend the bracket. Preserve its shape throughout the bench work.

watchFor.title: Rivet debris
watchFor.body: Remove every shaving from the roof assembly and vehicle before completing reassembly.

notes: The illustrations show a fully closed roof for clarity; the actual service position is partly open.
The latch handle, trim attachments and weatherstrip bracket have different tightening requirements.

verification.title: Original position restored
verification.body: Confirm that the weatherstrip bracket matches its mounting reference marks and that its retainers are tightened.

verification.title: Clean and complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that all rivet shavings have been removed and that the headliner tension bracket, headliner retainers, front-panel trim and latch handle are restored.

procedures.purpose: Convertible front-panel side weatherstrip removal, bench rivet removal and replacement, and installation using mandatory bracket reference marks.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace and align a convertible top center-panel side weatherstrip
guides.summary: Replace a center-panel side weatherstrip, preserve any shims, seat it with the roof closed and water-test the completed repair.
guides.introduction: The center-panel side weatherstrips form sections of the convertible roof's side sealing edge. This procedure applies to any of the four center-panel side strips. The replacement is initially fitted loosely so its position can be checked with the roof closed before the mounting nuts are tightened.
guides.why: The partly open service position reduces tension in the roof material, making the strip accessible. Final alignment is checked in the closed position because that is where the seal must fit correctly. Any original shims belong back in their recorded locations, and a water test establishes whether the completed repair is leak-free.

when.summary: When a center-panel side weatherstrip requires replacement or refitting for a confirmed sealing problem.
notes: Identify the affected strip before dismantling; a roof water leak alone does not identify which seal needs work.
The same procedure applies to the left- and right-hand positions.

prepare.title: Fasteners, shims and testing
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the weatherstrip nuts, controlled tightening equipment and a way to record any shim locations. Arrange a water test after reassembly.

prepare.title: Make the roof ready to move
prepare.detail: Position the roof with the vehicle stationary and the accessory delay relay active. Release the latch before opening, and remove any tonneau covers before closing. Normal roof operation lowers the windows before moving the top.

steps.title: Open the roof to the service position
steps.body: Follow the [center-panel side weatherstrip procedure](#/document/G1723914) and open the roof approximately 25 percent. The general working position is approximately 25–50 percent open, allowing slack even though the illustrations show the roof closed.

steps.title: Expose and remove the weatherstrip
steps.body: Pull the center-panel side weatherstrip trim downward to remove it. Before removing the mounting nuts, note the location of any shims. Remove the nuts and weatherstrip, keeping the shims associated with their original positions.

steps.title: Fit the replacement loosely
steps.body: Install the weatherstrip with any shims removed from that location. Leave the mounting nuts loose at this stage so the strip can settle into its correct position during the closed-roof alignment check.

steps.title: Close the roof and seat the strip
steps.body: Close the convertible top, then check the weatherstrip alignment. Gently wiggle the strip to seat it properly if necessary. Once correctly positioned, tighten the mounting nuts to 7 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the trim and test the seal
steps.body: Install the weatherstrip trim. Water-test the convertible top after the repair to verify that no water leak remains. This is the required final sealing check, so include it in the job rather than judging completion from appearance alone.

watchFor.title: Missing or misplaced shims
watchFor.body: Reinstall shims if they were present, using the locations noted before removal.

watchFor.title: Premature tightening
watchFor.body: Leave the strip loose until the roof is closed and its seating has been checked.

watchFor.title: Roof movement inhibited
watchFor.body: The roof depends on rear-window fully lowered signals. Failure to move is not evidence that the new weatherstrip is faulty; do not force the mechanism.

notes: The headliner is omitted from some illustrations for clarity; headliner removal is not a listed operation in this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The loosely installed strip is not seated correctly with the roof closed.
diagnostics.meaning: Its final mounting position has not yet been established.
diagnostics.next: Gently reposition it as directed before tightening the nuts.

diagnostics.finding: Water enters during the post-repair water test.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair has not met the required leak-free completion check.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the serviced strip's seating and shim placement and resolve the leak before accepting the repair.

verification.title: Installed alignment
verification.body: Confirm that the strip was aligned with the roof closed, its shims were restored, the nuts were tightened and the trim was installed.

verification.title: Record the water-test result
verification.body: Record which weatherstrip was serviced and whether the completed water test showed any leakage. Completion requires a leak-free result.

procedures.purpose: Removal and installation of any convertible center-panel side weatherstrip, including shim retention, closed-roof alignment and the required water test.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Adjust convertible rear quarter window glass
guides.summary: Set the rear quarter glass height, spacing and inward or outward pitch so it meets the door glass and convertible-top seals correctly.
guides.introduction: The convertible rear quarter glass must meet both the front door glass and the roof seals. Its mounting bolts control height and fore/aft position, while the regulator assembly's jack screws control inward or outward pitch. Adjustment corrects this geometry without replacing the glass or regulator.
guides.why: A gap can look acceptable at one end while the glass is tilted at the other. Recorded measurements establish alignment; a separate roof-seal check establishes engagement. Both must remain correct after the fasteners are tightened.
searchTerms: uneven gap between door and quarter glass
rear quarter window clips door glass

when.summary: When measured glass spacing or height is outside specification, or the division-bar seal fails to engage correctly.
notes: The right-hand procedure is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Measurement and fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable millimetre measuring equipment, a way to record readings and torque tools for the glass, regulator and speaker-bracket fasteners.

prepare.title: Access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove the rear quarter speaker, its bracket and, if equipped, the radio transceiver module (RTM), following their linked procedures.

steps.title: Expose the adjustment area
steps.body: Open the door, lower the roof and raise all windows fully. Remove the RTM if equipped, then the speaker and access plug. Remove the bracket nuts and stud bolt, release the wiring retainers and move the harness aside before removing the bracket. Close the door for the dimensional checks.

steps.title: Record the starting geometry
steps.body: Measure the inter-glass gap at the rear edge of the door glass, 7.5 mm from the base of the outer belt moulding and 7.5 mm from the top of the door glass. Each gap must be 9.8 mm ± 1.5 mm, with a top-to-bottom difference within ± 1.0 mm. The quarter glass must be level with, or up to 1 mm higher than, the door glass.

steps.title: Correct height and fore/aft position
steps.body: Loosen the glass bolts only enough to permit movement. Adjust the glass and repeat the height and gap measurements. Once correct, tighten the glass bolts to 11 Nm without shifting the glass.

steps.title: Check engagement with the roof
steps.body: Close the roof, raise all windows fully and open the door. Check that the division-bar seal enters the roof seals completely and engages the door glass without clipping. This checks a different aspect of alignment from the measured gap.

steps.title: Adjust inward or outward pitch
steps.body: Lower the roof, close the door and raise all windows fully. Loosen the appropriate regulator assembly nuts and adjust the jack screws: two control pitch near the quarter panel, and one controls pitch at the roof. Repeat the roof-closed engagement check, then tighten the assembly nuts to 20 Nm without moving the glass.

steps.title: Repeat both checks and restore access components
steps.body: With the roof lowered, door closed and windows fully raised, repeat and record all height and gap measurements. Then close the roof, raise the windows and open the door to recheck seal engagement. Repeat the relevant adjustment until both checks pass. Refit removed components; speaker-bracket nuts tighten to 8 Nm and the stud bolt to 11 Nm.

watchFor.title: Movement during tightening
watchFor.body: Holding the correct position matters: tightening can disturb an otherwise satisfactory adjustment.

watchFor.title: Clipping at the division bar
watchFor.body: Correct measured spacing does not excuse incomplete roof-seal entry or contact that clips the door glass.

notes: Rear quarter window motors do not require initialization; they have no one-touch up or down function.

diagnostics.finding: Gap, height or top-to-bottom difference is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The quarter glass requires positional adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Use the glass-bolt adjustment and repeat the recorded measurements.

diagnostics.finding: The division-bar seal does not engage completely or clips the door glass.
diagnostics.meaning: Inward or outward pitch needs correction.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the regulator jack screws and repeat both alignment checks.

verification.title: Record the final result
verification.body: Retain the final upper gap, lower gap, their difference and relative glass height after tightening.

verification.title: Confirm seal engagement
verification.body: With the roof closed and windows fully raised, confirm complete division-bar seal entry and engagement without clipping.

procedures.purpose: Complete convertible rear quarter glass adjustment, including access, dimensional checks, pitch adjustment and final verification.
Remove and reinstall the radio transceiver module when equipped.
Remove and reinstall the rear quarter panel speaker for adjustment access.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible parcel shelf
guides.summary: Release the convertible's parcel shelf by disconnecting both sensor connectors and moving the top tension-belt adjuster brackets into the interior.
guides.introduction: The convertible parcel shelf forms the trim surface behind the rear seating area. Its removal involves more than releasing the visible shelf retainers: surrounding trim, tonneau cover sensor wiring and convertible-top tension-belt adjuster brackets must also be released. The work moves between the luggage compartment and interior, with matching operations on both sides.
guides.why: The adjuster brackets remain locked to the body until their tabs are released. Trying to lift the shelf before completing these surrounding operations can load connected wiring or retained components. Working through each attachment in sequence makes it clear what still holds the assembly and preserves the parts needed for refitting.

when.summary: When the convertible parcel shelf needs replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Complete the paired operations on both sides, even where an illustration shows only one side.

prepare.title: Provide access from both areas
prepare.detail: Arrange working access to the luggage compartment and the interior behind the rear seats. The tension-belt adjusters are released from the luggage compartment and then passed inward.

prepare.title: Identify the attachments
prepare.detail: Review the loadspace-trim and parcel-shelf procedures so the pin-type retainers, cover clips, electrical connectors and bracket locking tabs can be released individually.

steps.title: Remove the loadspace trim
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim panels on both sides using the [convertible loadspace-trim procedure](#/document/G1692610). This exposes the surrounding connections needed for shelf removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensors
steps.body: Disconnect the tonneau cover sensor electrical connectors on both sides. Complete this before moving the trim assembly so connected wiring does not restrict removal.

steps.title: Remove both D-tower covers
steps.body: Remove each cover's pin-type retainers, release its clip and remove the cover. The left and right sides follow the same operation.

steps.title: Release the tension-belt adjusters
steps.body: From the luggage compartment, push inward on the rear of each convertible-top tension-belt adjuster to release its locking tabs. Pull the rear of the adjuster downward to disconnect its bracket from the body.

steps.title: Pass the brackets inward and remove the shelf
steps.body: On both sides, push the released adjuster bracket through the body opening into the interior. Then remove the shelf's pin-type retainers and lift out the parcel shelf, following the [parcel-shelf procedure](#/document/G1692611).

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reinstall the shelf and its retainers, return the adjuster brackets through the body and restore their locked attachments. Refit the D-tower covers, reconnect both sensor connectors and reinstall the loadspace trim panels.

watchFor.title: An adjuster that remains locked
watchFor.body: Release the rear locking tabs before pulling the adjuster downward; shelf movement is not the release action.

watchFor.title: An unfinished opposite side
watchFor.body: Check both sides before lifting the shelf, especially the electrical connectors and adjuster brackets.

notes: This procedure releases the tension-belt adjuster brackets from the body; it does not call for changing their adjustment.

verification.title: Check paired attachments
verification.body: Confirm both adjuster brackets are restored to their locked body attachments and both tonneau cover sensor connectors are reconnected.

verification.title: Check trim retention
verification.body: Confirm the parcel-shelf retainers, D-tower cover clips and retainers, and both loadspace trim panels are restored.

procedures.purpose: Convertible parcel-shelf removal and installation, including sensor connections and tension-belt adjuster bracket release.
Convertible loadspace trim removal and installation for access on both sides.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace a convertible rear quarter window regulator
guides.summary: Remove the quarter glass and regulator assembly, replace the required component and finish with the mandatory glass adjustment.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter window regulator carries and moves the convertible's small rear side glass. Its motor responds to the master window switch and roof-related window commands. Regulator replacement involves removing the glass and mechanism together, separating components only as needed, then restoring the glass alignment against the door and roof.
guides.why: The glass must be fully raised before it can be separated from the regulator because that position provides access to the bolts. Installation also changes the assembly's position, so glass adjustment is a required finishing operation.
searchTerms: convertible rear quarter window regulator replacement
rear quarter window will not move
rear quarter window will not close

when.summary: When regulator replacement is justified, or the glass/regulator assembly must be removed for component service.
notes: An inoperative window does not by itself establish a failed regulator.
The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Access and handling
prepare.detail: Prepare for speaker, moulding and watershield removal, careful handling of the glass/regulator assembly, and right-side radio transceiver module (RTM) removal.

prepare.title: Fastening and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, plus the measuring capability required by the linked glass-adjustment procedure.

steps.title: Lower the roof and open the access area
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. On the right-hand side, remove the [RTM](#/document/G1694188). Remove the rear quarter panel speaker as directed by the regulator procedure. The roof assembly is omitted from some illustrations for clarity; that does not add a roof-removal operation.

steps.title: Release the belt mouldings
steps.body: Remove the interior belt moulding's nut and bolt, then remove the moulding. Move the exterior moulding aside to clear the glass/regulator assembly's removal path.

steps.title: Establish the glass position
steps.body: Raise the quarter glass fully. If the glass is inoperative, the regulator motor must be removed to permit movement of the glass and access to the separation bolts. Do not attempt to separate the glass and regulator while the glass remains below its full-up position.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and watershield
steps.body: Remove the speaker-bracket nuts and stud bolt, release the wiring retainer and move the harness aside. Remove the bracket. Disconnect the regulator-motor electrical connector, move its harness aside, and release the watershield and associated wiring retainers.

steps.title: Withdraw the combined assembly
steps.body: Remove the assembly mounting nuts and take out the rear quarter glass/regulator assembly. Keeping the components together at this stage follows the prescribed removal route.

steps.title: Separate only the components required
steps.body: Remove the glass-to-regulator bolts and separate the regulator when installing a new regulator. Remove the motor bolts and motor only when installing a new component, except where motor removal was already required to reposition inoperative glass.

steps.title: Reinstall and adjust the glass
steps.body: Reverse removal, restoring the wiring, watershield, mouldings and access components. Tighten glass-to-regulator bolts to 11 Nm and assembly mounting nuts to 20 Nm. Speaker-bracket nuts tighten to 8 Nm and its stud bolt to 11 Nm. Complete the [rear quarter glass adjustment](#/document/G1697267) before considering the repair finished.

watchFor.title: Roof interlocks can resemble a window fault
watchFor.body: Rear quarter window operation is inhibited while the roof is between its fully raised and fully lowered positions.

watchFor.title: Glass position controls separation access
watchFor.body: The inoperative-window motor-removal branch exists to permit glass movement; it is not evidence that the motor itself needs replacement.

notes: Rear quarter window motors require no initialization because they have no one-touch up or down function.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not operate when commanded.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof operation requires full-down signals from both rear quarter window motors.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether both windows reach full down before attributing the complaint to the regulator.

diagnostics.finding: The glass cannot reach full up for separation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required bolt access has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified motor-removal branch to permit glass movement.

verification.title: Complete and record alignment
verification.body: Carry out the linked adjustment procedure and record its final measurements and seal-engagement result.

verification.title: Confirm coordinated operation
verification.body: With the roof at an end position, confirm rear quarter window operation from the master switch. Check that a roof command lowers the windows and that roof movement follows both quarter windows reaching full down.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear quarter glass/regulator assembly removal and installation, including conditional regulator and motor separation.
Right-hand-side radio transceiver module removal and installation for access.
Mandatory rear quarter glass adjustment after regulator installation.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace the convertible top tension belt
guides.summary: Remove the convertible top assembly, release the material at the floating bow, and replace the tension belt with the roof partly open.
guides.introduction: The tension belt is a mechanical part of the convertible roof’s material-support arrangement, attached at the floating bow by a sliding connection and retaining screw. Replacing it involves the surrounding roof material and its retaining clips as well as the belt itself. The complete convertible top assembly must be removed before the belt work.
guides.why: The roof must be partly open to provide slack in the top material and associated components. Working with the material under closed-roof tension makes the attachments harder to service. The material-retaining clips must also return to their proper locations so that releasing the floating bow does not leave the roof material incorrectly attached.

when.summary: When a confirmed roof repair requires removal or replacement of the convertible top tension belt.
notes: A roof that will not operate needs its operating conditions checked before the tension belt is treated as the cause.

prepare.title: Plan for complete top removal
prepare.detail: Have the full Convertible Top Assembly removal and installation procedure available, together with the handling capability and workspace it requires. Assembly removal is a prerequisite to belt access.

prepare.title: Prepare for clips and screw tightening
prepare.detail: Be ready to preserve the material-retaining clip locations. Have an appropriate screw driver and torque equipment for the tension-belt retaining screw.

prepare.title: Use the service position
prepare.detail: The procedure illustrations show the roof fully closed, but the actual service position is approximately 25–50 percent open to provide slack.

steps.title: Position and remove the top assembly
steps.body: Use the partly open service position and follow the complete Convertible Top Assembly procedure to remove the assembly. Follow that procedure’s handling and removal requirements before proceeding to the belt.

steps.title: Release material from the floating bow
steps.body: Remove the convertible top material retaining clips from the floating bow and partially disconnect the material. Preserve the proper clip locations for installation. The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side is similar.

steps.title: Remove the tension belt
steps.body: Remove the belt retaining screw, then slide the belt out of the floating bow. The illustration identifies the screw attachment and sliding engagement; maintain slack while working at these connections.

steps.title: Install the belt and restore the material
steps.body: Reverse removal to slide the belt into the floating bow and install its retaining screw. Tighten the screw to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Reattach the roof material, placing its retaining clips on the material in their proper locations.

steps.title: Reinstall the top assembly
steps.body: Complete refitting through the Convertible Top Assembly procedure. Restore the assembly before checking powered roof operation and follow any completion requirements in that procedure.

watchFor.title: Taut material during service
watchFor.body: Do not copy the fully closed position shown in the illustrations. Establish the specified partly open position so the material and related components have service slack.

watchFor.title: Lost clip locations
watchFor.body: Removing the material from the floating bow includes removing its retaining clips. Their correct placement on the material must be restored during installation.

notes: The roof uses coordinated electric motors and waits for both rear quarter windows to report fully lowered before moving. An operating inhibition does not by itself identify a belt problem.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move and both rear quarter windows have not reported fully down.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof control system inhibits movement until it receives both window-down signals.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the window position or related operating fault before attributing the stopped roof to the tension belt.

diagnostics.finding: TOP DISABLED — REMOVE COVERS appears when raising the roof.
diagnostics.meaning: Installed tonneau covers prevent the roof from being raised.
diagnostics.next: Remove the covers before checking closing operation.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check the belt’s sliding engagement, retaining-screw tightening and restoration of the roof-material clips to their proper locations.

verification.title: Check operation under valid conditions
verification.body: With the vehicle stationary and accessory delay active, hold the roof switch in the requested direction. Release the latch for opening and remove any tonneau covers for closing. Confirm that the windows lower before roof movement and that the roof reaches the requested position.

Required complete convertible top assembly removal and subsequent installation.

guides.title: Remove and rebond convertible-top rear window glass
guides.summary: Remove the convertible-top rear glass and restore its urethane bond using the fixed-glass preparation and curing procedure.
guides.introduction: The convertible-top rear glass closes the rear window opening and provides rearward visibility. Its adhesive bond must retain the glass and seal against air and water. This job follows the fixed-glass removal and installation method, whether fitting replacement glass or reinstalling reusable glass. It concerns the bonded pane, separate from the movable rear quarter windows.
guides.why: Bond strength depends on clean surfaces, compatible materials and strict timing. Cut urethane becomes unsuitable for rebonding after its working window expires. Damaged mounting surfaces, gaps in the bead or disturbed adhesive can compromise sealing and glass retention.

when.summary: When the convertible-top rear glass requires removal, replacement or reinstallation.
notes: Establish that a leak originates at the glass bond before choosing this repair.

prepare.title: Arrange glass-removal capability
prepare.detail: Plan access and any necessary trim removal. Available methods use a cold knife, powered fixed-glass removal tool or glass cut-out wire; the wire method requires an assistant. Methods may be combined.

prepare.title: Prepare the bonding materials
prepare.detail: Have a power caulk gun, knife, soft brush or vacuum, specified glass cleaner, and an approved urethane adhesive with same-brand primer. Review the products' preparation and curing instructions before cutting.

prepare.title: Plan the working time
prepare.detail: New or reused glass must be installed within 2 hours of cutting the existing urethane. Have the required materials and access ready before starting.

steps.title: Choose and protect the cutting route
steps.body: A cold knife cuts from outside where its blade can reach the bead; powered cutting works from inside. Wire cutting uses access from both sides. For cold-knife work, protect the opening perimeter with tape, adding layers as needed.

steps.title: Cut out the glass
steps.body: Follow the Fixed Glass removal procedure, protecting surrounding components, paint, primer and the mounting flange. Locating pins may need cutting if present. Avoid scratching or deforming the bonding surface.

steps.title: Prepare the mounting surface
steps.body: Repair corrosion before bonding. Trim the old urethane to a 1 mm to 2 mm base when installation will remain within the 2-hour limit. Remove debris with a soft brush or vacuum and avoid touching the adhesive surface. Prime damaged paint or clearcoat and previously primed areas as directed, minimizing primer over retained urethane. Observe at least 10 minutes of flash time.

steps.title: Prepare new or reusable glass
steps.body: For new glass, clean the inside with the specified cleaner, then apply primer according to its instructions and allow at least 10 minutes to dry. For reused glass, retain a thin urethane layer and prime areas where the old adhesive was completely removed, again allowing at least 10 minutes.

steps.title: Apply a continuous bead
steps.body: Cut the applicator tip to the illustrated specification. Use the power caulk gun to apply a uniform bead 14 mm high and 8 mm wide over the trimmed urethane. Start and finish at the original overlap points and leave no gaps. Control squeeze-out where peripheral mouldings are absent.

steps.title: Seat and secure the glass
steps.body: Open the door windows before installation to prevent closing-door pressure from disturbing the bond. Install the glass within 10 minutes of applying urethane. Press firmly by hand and hold it in the correct position with tape until cured.

steps.title: Finish and allow full curing
steps.body: Remove excess uncured adhesive with the specified cleaner as necessary and reinstall removed components. Leave the door windows open throughout curing. Follow the adhesive manufacturer's curing instructions and do not drive until the seal has cured.

watchFor.title: Expired bonding time
watchFor.body: Do not continue as though freshly cut urethane remains active after the 2-hour installation window.

watchFor.title: Corrosion or premature vehicle release
watchFor.body: Corrosion at a structural pinch weld requires repair. Inadequately cured adhesive can compromise glass retention during a crash.

notes: The shared fixed-glass procedure also includes windshield-only requirements for camera brackets, adhesive mouldings, alignment pins and spacers, A-pillar strips and camera alignment. Those branches do not apply to this rear-glass job.

diagnostics.finding: A gap or discontinuity is present in the fresh bead.
diagnostics.meaning: The bond may allow air or water leakage.
diagnostics.next: Correct the bead before installing the glass, while preserving the required working times.

verification.title: Confirm retention conditions
verification.body: Confirm correct glass positioning, continuous bonding preparation and completion of the manufacturer's cure before vehicle release.

verification.title: Record the bonding timeline
verification.body: Record cutting, primer drying, bead application, glass installation and cure completion to confirm the required timing was met.

procedures.purpose: Convertible-top rear glass removal and installation, directing both phases to Fixed Glass.
Detailed cutting methods, surface preparation, new/reused glass branches, urethane application and curing.
