guides.title: Replace the convertible rear seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Remove the convertible rear backrest, release its cover attachments carefully and refit the upholstery without damaging the foam-mounted fastening strips.
guides.introduction: The rear backrest cover is the upholstery fitted over the foam pad and secured around the backrest frame. J-clips and pin-type retainers secure its edges and carpet section, while hook-and-loop strips hold portions of the cover against the foam. Replacing the cover requires removing the backrest from the convertible first, then releasing these different attachment types in sequence.
guides.why: The foam-mounted hook-and-loop strips are the vulnerable part of this operation. Pulling the cover away carelessly can tear those strips out of the foam, creating an attachment problem during a trim repair. Releasing the frame fixings first leaves the final separation focused on the hook-and-loop connection.
searchTerms: convertible rear seat backrest cover replacement

when.summary: When the convertible rear backrest upholstery needs replacement or removal for access beneath the cover.
notes: Plan for complete backrest removal before releasing the cover.

prepare.title: Prepare for backrest removal
prepare.detail: Be able to complete the linked convertible backrest removal and installation procedure. The cover work begins with the backrest removed from the vehicle.

prepare.title: Identify the attachment types
prepare.detail: Locate the frame J-clips, carpet pin-type retainers, upper frame retainers and foam-mounted hook-and-loop strips. Distinguishing them helps avoid pulling against a fixing that is still engaged.

steps.title: Remove the backrest assembly
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Backrest — Convertible](#/document/G1709034). With the backrest removed, proceed to the cover attachments described in [Rear Seat Backrest Cover — Convertible](#/document/G1709035).

steps.title: Release the frame attachments
steps.body: Release the cover J-clips from the frame. Release the carpet pin-type retainers and fold the carpet forward, then release the cover pin-type retainers from the top of the frame. This clears the mechanical fixings before separating the upholstery from the foam.

steps.title: Separate the cover from the foam
steps.body: Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips between the cover and foam, then remove the cover. Watch the foam-side strips during separation: they must remain attached to the foam rather than being pulled out with the cover.

steps.title: Refit the cover and backrest
steps.body: Reverse removal. Restore the hook-and-loop attachment, upper frame retainers, carpet position and retainers, and frame J-clips. Complete backrest installation using the linked convertible backrest procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam-side strips lifting
watchFor.body: If a strip begins pulling away from the foam, stop pulling the cover in that manner. The specified precaution is to preserve those strips during separation.

notes: The carpet is folded forward after its retainers are released; include its return and fastening in reassembly.

verification.title: Check the foam attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the hook-and-loop strips remain attached to the foam and have been re-engaged with the cover.

verification.title: Confirm every retention stage
verification.body: Check the upper retainers, carpet retainers and J-clips, then confirm completion of the convertible backrest installation procedure.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear backrest cover removal and installation, including the attachment sequence and foam-strip damage precaution.
Convertible rear backrest removal before upholstery work and installation after the cover is restored.

guides.title: Replace a convertible top front striker
guides.summary: Remove and refit the front roof striker using its alignment marks, while preserving the left-side latch-switch connection.
guides.introduction: The front striker provides the engagement point for the convertible roof latch at the windshield header. Its installed position matters to how the roof latches. A magnet-operated latch switch also tells the roof controller when the top is secured. This repair opens the header trim, removes the striker and returns it to the recorded position during installation.
guides.why: The striker and its upper retainers need separate reference marks before removal. Those marks preserve the required alignment. On the left side, the latch-switch harness must also be disconnected and restored; mechanical attachment and electrical confirmation of latching are related parts of the completed job.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of a convertible top front striker.
notes: A roof-status message or failure to move does not, by itself, identify a faulty striker.

prepare.title: Prepare for header trim access
prepare.detail: The work requires careful release of trim clips, handling of any visor wiring, a means of making alignment marks and torque-controlled fastening.

prepare.title: Use the normal roof operating conditions
prepare.detail: Opening requires active accessory-delay power, a released latch and vehicle speed below 5 km/h (3 mph). Carry out the repair with the vehicle stationary.

steps.title: Position the roof and remove the side trim
steps.body: Open the convertible top approximately halfway. Remove both [convertible A-pillar trim panels](#/document/G1692609), providing access to the ends of the windshield header trim.

steps.title: Remove the visors and upper header trim
steps.body: On both sides, remove the sun visor cap, release the clip and remove the visor, disconnecting its electrical connector if fitted. Remove the visor latch clips. Release the upper header panel clips from the lower panel first, then from the windshield header, and remove the upper panel.

steps.title: Lower the lower header trim for access
steps.body: Release the lower panel's clips from the header, followed by the clips at the sun visor locations, and lower the panel. Disconnect wiring as necessary for clearance. The illustrations omit some components for clarity; follow the [striker procedure](#/document/G1708673) for the actual access sequence.

steps.title: Mark and release the lower attachment
steps.body: On the left side, disconnect the convertible top latch-switch harness connector. Mark the striker's position against the header before removing its lower bolt. Preserve this reference for installation rather than relying on memory of the striker position.

steps.title: Mark the upper retainers and remove the striker
steps.body: Mark the header around the upper retainers before removing them. Remove the retainers and striker, keeping both sets of alignment references visible. The left and right striker removal methods are similar, with the electrical disconnection applying to the left side.

steps.title: Install to the recorded position
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using the striker and retainer reference marks. Tighten the upper retainers to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm) and the lower bolt to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Reconnect the left-side latch-switch harness, restore any other disconnected wiring and reinstall the header trim, visors and A-pillar panels.

watchFor.title: Missing alignment marks
watchFor.body: Both the striker-to-header and upper-retainer marks are required installation references.

watchFor.title: Forgotten left-side connector
watchFor.body: A disconnected latch switch interrupts the controller's information about whether the roof is secured.

notes: Brief audio muting when the roof is latched or unlatched is normal system behavior.

diagnostics.finding: TOP NOT SECURE is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: With the top raised and speed above 5 km/h (3 mph), this message indicates that the latch is not fully engaged.
diagnostics.next: Check the actual latching condition and the disturbed alignment and switch connection; do not replace a striker solely because of the message.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on latch status, operating prerequisites and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Check those conditions before attributing the complaint to the striker or roof motors.

verification.title: Confirm alignment and reassembly
verification.body: Verify that the striker and retainers match their saved references, their tightening is complete and all disturbed wiring and trim are restored.

verification.title: Record the completed work
verification.body: Record the side serviced, restoration to the alignment marks and reconnection of the latch switch when working on the left side.

procedures.purpose: Convertible top front striker removal and installation, alignment references and fastener torques.
Convertible A-pillar trim removal and installation for header access.
Explain latch-switch feedback, roof operating prerequisites and roof-status messages.

guides.title: Replace the convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the convertible rear backrest, disconnect the latch cable and replace the retained lock cylinder before restoring the seat.
guides.introduction: The convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder provides a mechanical input to the lid latch through a cable. This repair separates that cable connection and removes the cylinder from its mounting. Access comes through the rear seating area, making correct seat reinstallation an essential part of the job.
guides.why: The cable connection uses retaining tabs, while a separate retaining clip secures the cylinder. Releasing those attachments in sequence avoids pulling against a part that is still retained. The rear backrest also has critical mounting requirements: nothing may be trapped between seat components and the body or within a seat-structure joint.

when.summary: When the convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder requires removal or replacement.
notes: A luggage-lid release complaint can involve the cylinder, cable or latch; this procedure covers cylinder replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare seat access
prepare.detail: Follow the convertible backrest procedure, including its preliminary rear cushion removal. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for restoring the backrest attachments.

prepare.title: Plan the attachment sequence
prepare.detail: Identify the cable retaining tabs and the separate cylinder retaining clip before removal. Keep the seat mounting joints clear throughout the work.

steps.title: Remove the rear backrest
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Backrest – Convertible](#/document/G1709034): remove the rear cushion, release the backrest-to-floor fasteners, then release the backrest locking clips and remove the backrest. The attached illustration shows the seat-access fasteners, not the lock cylinder.

steps.title: Detach the latch cable
steps.body: Release the lock-cylinder retaining tabs and detach the luggage-compartment lid latch cable. Complete this connection release before attempting to withdraw the cylinder.

steps.title: Exchange the cylinder
steps.body: Remove the separate cylinder retaining clip, then remove the lock cylinder. Reverse these operations to install the replacement: secure the cylinder with its clip and restore the cable connection and retaining tabs.

steps.title: Restore the rear seating
steps.body: Reverse the backrest removal sequence and tighten its floor attachments to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Restore the cushion as directed. Keep objects out of all seat mounting joints, and leave the belt webbing untwisted with belts and buckles accessible.

watchFor.title: Cable or cylinder still retained
watchFor.body: The cable tabs and cylinder clip are separate attachments. Confirm the appropriate attachment is released before moving either component.

watchFor.title: Obstructed seat joints
watchFor.body: Objects between the seat structure and body can prevent correct installation and operation. Clear the joints before securing the backrest.

notes: Mechanical cylinder and cable attachment should be checked separately from any passive-entry release complaint.

verification.title: Confirm cylinder and cable attachment
verification.body: Before closing access, confirm the cylinder retaining clip is installed and the cable connection and tabs are restored.

verification.title: Confirm seating restoration
verification.body: Check the backrest locking clips, specified floor-fastener torque and clear seat joints. Confirm that belts and buckles remain accessible without twisted webbing.

procedures.purpose: Convertible luggage-compartment lock cylinder and latch-cable removal and installation.
Convertible rear backrest removal and installation for cylinder access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible A-pillar trim panel
guides.summary: Remove the sun visor, release the pillar trim in stages, and reconnect any fitted visor and speaker wiring during refitting.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar borders the windshield, and its interior trim covers the body member beside the front occupants. On this convertible arrangement, removing the sun visor is the first access step. The panel then releases from retainers and clips. A fitted pillar speaker and an electrically connected sun visor introduce separate connectors that must be dealt with during removal and installation.
guides.why: The removal sequence creates access while allowing any attached wiring to be disconnected before the component is carried away. The panel’s retainers are released before the optional speaker connector, followed by the remaining clips. Recognizing these stages helps prevent pulling on a panel that is still mechanically attached or tethered by wiring.
searchTerms: sun visor removal for pillar trim

when.summary: When the convertible A-pillar trim needs replacement or removal for access behind it.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive with the right-side panel shown; right-hand drive and the opposite side are similar.
Visor and speaker electrical disconnections apply only where those connections are fitted.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted connections
prepare.detail: Check whether the sun visor has an electrical connection and whether the pillar panel carries a speaker. Plan to support each component while disconnecting its wiring.

prepare.title: Understand the attachment sequence
prepare.detail: Use the procedure and illustration to identify the visor cap and clip, followed by the pillar retainers and remaining clips. The speaker connection is released between the panel’s two mechanical release stages.

steps.title: Remove the sun visor
steps.body: Remove the sun visor cap, release its clip, and remove the visor. If equipped, disconnect its electrical connector while keeping the visor supported.

steps.title: Release the pillar retainers
steps.body: Release the A-pillar panel retainers as shown. This is the initial panel-release stage; the remaining clips still need to be released before removal is complete.

steps.title: Disconnect the speaker and remove the panel
steps.body: If a speaker is fitted, disconnect its electrical connector. Then release the remaining clips and remove the A-pillar trim panel.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the panel clips, any speaker connection, and the retainers. Reconnect the visor wiring if fitted, reinstall the visor, and restore its clip and cap.

watchFor.title: A component still attached by wiring
watchFor.body: A released visor or panel may remain connected electrically. Disconnect the applicable connector before moving it away.

verification.title: Confirm attachments and connections
verification.body: Confirm the pillar panel’s retainers and clips are engaged, any speaker and visor connectors are reconnected, and the sun visor clip and cap are restored.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the convertible A-pillar trim, including sun visor access and equipment-dependent electrical connections.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Adjust Convertible Door Glass for Correct Seal Fit
guides.summary: Set door-glass height, fore/aft position and inward/outward alignment against the convertible roof seals and rear quarter glass.
guides.introduction: The door glass must meet both the convertible-top weatherstrips and the rear quarter glass. Its clamps establish height and fore/aft position, while the regulator rails control inward/outward alignment. This adjustment restores those relationships through measured changes.
guides.why: A misaligned door or rear quarter window can make correctly positioned front glass appear wrong. Establishing those references first avoids compensating at the wrong component, while equal rail movement prevents binding.

when.summary: When measurements show incorrect door-glass engagement or spacing, including during wind-noise or water-leak investigation.
notes: Check door alignment first if the door has been removed or replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare for measured adjustment
prepare.detail: Have marking tape, a measuring scale, suitable access tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening values.

prepare.title: Arrange access and initialization
prepare.detail: Use the applicable speaker removal procedure and have the named Power Door Window Initialization procedure available for completion.

steps.title: Establish the surrounding alignment
steps.body: For wind noise or water entry, check and correct rear quarter glass alignment first. If the door was removed or replaced, check front-door alignment before adjusting the glass.

steps.title: Expose the adjustment points
steps.body: Open the door and remove its speaker. Position the passenger front door module aside as directed, then remove the grommets, adhesive tapes and lower watershield. Install the window control switch, raise the door glass fully and close the door.

steps.title: Measure seal engagement
steps.body: Place tape at the A-pillar position 245 mm from the outer belt moulding base and at the roof-line position 230 mm forward from the glass rear edge. With the door open, record tape-to-glass-top distances. Close it and record tape-to-seal-retainer-bottom distances. Subtract the closed-door readings from the open-door readings.

steps.title: Correct height and fore/aft position
steps.body: Open the door, loosen both glass clamps and reposition the glass. Tighten the clamps to 9 Nm, then repeat the measurements. Required engagement is 4 mm ±2 mm at the A-pillar and 8 mm ±2.5 mm at the rear roof-line location.

steps.title: Check the quarter-window gap
steps.body: Measure the gap at positions 75 mm above the outer belt moulding base and 75 mm below the glass top. Each gap should be 9.8 mm ±1.5 mm, with top-to-bottom variation within ±1.0 mm. Record both readings.

steps.title: Set inward/outward engagement
steps.body: Lower the rear quarter glass and cycle the door glass against the top weatherstrips. Open the door, loosen the fore/aft run nuts and lower regulator nuts, and move both rails equally. Close and cycle again; repeat as needed. Open the door and lower its glass before tightening the regulator-rail nuts, lower run bolt/nuts and upper run nuts to 11 Nm without shifting the runs. Raise both windows and close the door.

steps.title: Repeat the checks and restore the door
steps.body: Repeat the taped engagement measurements and the in/out cycling check with the quarter glass lowered. Correct any remaining error, raise the quarter glass and close the door. Remove the tape, reinstall removed components and carry out Power Door Window Initialization.

watchFor.title: Binding during travel
watchFor.body: Unequal front and rear rail adjustments can bind the glass.

watchFor.title: Movement during tightening
watchFor.body: Keep the glass runs stationary while securing their fasteners.

notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand procedure is similar.
Convertibles lack one-touch up and bounce-back features. Rear quarter window motors do not require initialization.

diagnostics.finding: Front engagement is correct, but quarter-window spacing or parallelism is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The remaining correction belongs at the rear quarter glass.
diagnostics.next: Follow Rear Quarter Window Glass Adjustment - Convertible.

verification.title: Record the final geometry
verification.body: Retain final engagement readings, both quarter-window gaps and their difference.

verification.title: Confirm operating engagement
verification.body: Complete the repeated weatherstrip-engagement check and required door-window initialization.

procedures.purpose: Complete convertible door-glass measurement, adjustment, reassembly and initialization reference.
Check or correct convertible rear quarter glass alignment.
Establish front-door alignment after door removal or replacement.
Right-hand speaker removal and installation for the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 access branch.
Left-hand speaker removal and installation for the SYNC access branch.

guides.title: Remove and refit the convertible top trough assembly
guides.summary: Remove the convertible roof drainage trough while preserving its flexible water bags, drain connections and surrounding paintwork.
guides.introduction: The convertible top trough collects water around the roof opening and directs it into the body drains. Its flexible water bags connect to the drain hoses through fittings seated in body-panel grommets. Removing the trough involves removing the convertible top assembly first, releasing these drain connections and carefully maneuvering the trough through the body opening.
guides.why: The flexible bags and their drain fittings must remain joined during removal. Pulling them apart would disturb a connection that this job does not require you to dismantle. Slack in the roof material improves service access, while the specified extraction movement creates clearance around the painted body panels.

when.summary: When the convertible top trough needs replacement or removal for associated roof work.
notes: Plan for the complete convertible top removal and refitting operation before beginning the trough work.

prepare.title: Arrange roof-assembly access
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the linked Convertible Top Assembly procedure. Trough access begins only after that assembly has been removed.

prepare.title: Protect the body
prepare.detail: Fully cover the vehicle body with fender blankets or equivalent protection before moving the trough out of the opening.

prepare.title: Identify the retainers
prepare.detail: Use the illustrated retainer locations to identify the push pins securing the trough to the inner body panel. The illustration also shows a trim-removal tool.

steps.title: Create slack and remove the roof assembly
steps.body: Position the convertible top approximately 25–50 percent open so the material and associated components have slack. Although some procedure views show a closed roof, that is not the intended service position. Remove the top using the [Convertible Top Assembly procedure](#/document/G1708670).

steps.title: Release the body retainers
steps.body: Remove the trough-to-inner-body-panel push-pin retainers shown in the [trough procedure](#/document/G1708679). Release the illustrated attachments before trying to lift or turn the assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect both body drains
steps.body: Work from inside the trough on each side. Carefully pull upward on the flexible water bag and its drain fitting together until the fitting releases from the inner body-panel grommet/drain hose. Leave the fitting attached to the flexible bag.

steps.title: Maneuver the trough out
steps.body: With the body fully protected, coordinate these movements as one action: pull the right-hand side inward, roll it forward and slightly downward, and lift the right-hand rear portion above the body panels. Once clear, remove the assembly toward the right-hand side of the vehicle.

steps.title: Reverse the removal path
steps.body: Refit the trough by reversing the removal procedure. Restore both drain-fitting connections and the body retainers, keeping each fitting attached to its water bag throughout. Complete roof reinstallation through the linked top-assembly procedure.

watchFor.title: A drain fitting separating from its bag
watchFor.body: The intended separation is between the fitting and the body grommet/drain hose. Do not remove the fitting from the flexible water bag.

watchFor.title: Contact with painted panels
watchFor.body: If the trough lacks clearance, reassess the coordinated inward, forward and lifting movement before continuing.

notes: The left-hand drain arrangement is illustrated; the right-hand side is serviced similarly.

verification.title: Confirm drainage connections and retention
verification.body: Check that both drain fittings are back in their body grommet/drain-hose connections and that the trough push-pin retainers have been restored.

verification.title: Complete the roof installation
verification.body: Confirm completion of the separate convertible top installation procedure before returning the vehicle to use.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the convertible top trough, including drain release and the coordinated extraction movement.
Remove the convertible top assembly for trough access and reinstall it afterward.

guides.title: Replace a convertible rear seatbelt retractor
guides.summary: Remove the rear trim and belt attachments, replace the retractor and verify belt routing and both locking functions.
guides.introduction: The rear seatbelt retractor stores the webbing while allowing ordinary movement. Its Emergency Locking Retractor (ELR) function responds to vehicle motion to restrain the occupant during hard braking, cornering or an impact. The passenger belt also has an Automatic Locking Retractor (ALR) mode for securing a child seat. Replacement must preserve the belt’s attachment, routing and operating modes.
guides.why: A securely mounted retractor still needs untwisted webbing and accessible belt hardware to work correctly. Trim removal also has a specific direction of release. On the left side, the luggage-compartment lock-cylinder bracket shares the retractor removal area and must be moved aside.
searchTerms: rear seatbelt locked after full extension

when.summary: When seatbelt diagnosis establishes that a convertible rear retractor requires replacement.
notes: Check whether an apparently locked belt is operating normally in automatic locking mode before condemning the retractor.
The illustrated left-hand procedure also applies to the right side, except for the specified left-side bracket operation.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-service capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable trim and fastener tools and a torque wrench. The technician must be able to complete the Seatbelt Systems functional checks after installation.

prepare.title: Plan rear trim access
prepare.detail: Use the convertible rear seat backrest procedure first. Keep the upper and middle loadspace trim sequence available so the belt guide, clips and rear locating tab can be released correctly.

steps.title: Remove the backrest and upper trim
steps.body: Remove the rear seat backrest. Position the seatbelt guide aside, release the upper loadspace trim panel clips and remove that panel to expose the next layer of access.

steps.title: Release the middle loadspace panel
steps.body: Release its clips, then pull forward and outward to disengage the rear tab. Position the front and rear safety belts aside and remove the panel without trapping either belt.

steps.title: Free the belt attachment
steps.body: Remove the retainer and position the seatbelt aside. Its installation torque is 30 lb.ft (40 Nm); retain that requirement for reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the retractor
steps.body: Remove the D-ring bolt, then the retractor bolt. On the left-hand side only, position the luggage-compartment lid lock-cylinder bracket aside before removing the retractor. Both bolts have an installation torque of 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).

steps.title: Install and route the belt
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the left-side bracket where applicable and tightening the specified attachments correctly. Keep the webbing untwisted and make sure the seatbelts and buckles remain accessible to occupants as the trim and backrest are refitted.

steps.title: Check the complete seatbelt system
steps.body: Carry out the linked Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure. Use its retractor road-test inspection for emergency locking and its automatic-locking functional test to confirm the relevant operating modes.

watchFor.title: A rear tab still engaged
watchFor.body: The middle trim panel must move forward and outward after clip release; pulling elsewhere can leave its rear tab trapped.

watchFor.title: Webbing twisted during trim installation
watchFor.body: Check the belt’s route as the panels return, rather than waiting until the belt or buckle is hidden behind trim.

notes: Automatic locking engages after the passenger belt is fully extracted and then allowed to retract. Clicking during retraction is part of this mode.

diagnostics.finding: The fully extended belt clicks as it retracts and will not pull back out.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the described automatic-locking behavior and does not alone prove a fault.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage the mode, then use the specified functional test.

verification.title: Confirm fit and operation
verification.body: Check untwisted webbing, accessible belts and buckles, correct attachment tightening and successful completion of the prescribed seatbelt operating checks.

verification.title: Record the restraint-service result
verification.body: Record the serviced side, attachment torque completion and functional-test results. Keep any failed operating check unresolved until the seatbelt diagnosis is completed.

Convertible rear seat backrest removal and installation for access.

guides.title: Replace the convertible high-mounted stoplamp
guides.summary: Remove the convertible’s luggage-lid trim, release the stoplamp’s electrical and mechanical attachments, and refit the lamp and access parts.
guides.introduction: The high-mounted stoplamp provides an elevated braking signal alongside the rear stoplamps. Applying the brake pedal supplies voltage to these lamps through the stoplamp system. On the convertible, this lamp is serviced through the luggage compartment lid after removing its inner trim. The work involves the lamp assembly, its connector, mounting nuts and two-sided sealing tape.
guides.why: The trim cannot simply be pulled away: the emergency release handle and latch cover have retaining features that must be released first. The lamp also remains attached by sealing tape after its nuts are removed. Controlled release protects these parts, while the specified light tightening torque secures the lamp without treating its attachments like large body fasteners.
searchTerms: convertible third brake light not working

when.summary: When the convertible high-mounted stoplamp needs removal or diagnosis has established that replacement is required.
notes: An unlit stoplamp is a reason to investigate the stoplamp system, not proof that the lamp assembly is defective.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver, suitable tools for the trim retainers and lamp nuts, and a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening torque.

prepare.title: Identify the attachments
prepare.detail: Locate the emergency release handle tab, latch-cover engagement and lamp connector before beginning. The lamp illustration shows its attachment points behind the lid trim.

steps.title: Release the emergency handle
steps.body: Follow [High Mounted Stoplamp — Convertible](#/document/G1694121). Press down the luggage compartment lid emergency release handle’s retaining tab, then remove the handle to begin clearing the trim.

steps.title: Remove the latch cover
steps.body: Insert the flat-bladed screwdriver between the cover and latch. Gently pry the cover away to disengage it from the latch tab. The aim is to release the engagement, not force the cover past it.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the lamp
steps.body: Remove the retainers and luggage compartment lid trim panel. Disconnect the high-mounted stoplamp’s electrical connector before removing its attachments.

steps.title: Release the lamp
steps.body: Remove the mounting nuts, then release the two-sided seal tape and remove the lamp. The taped joint is a separate attachment and must be released even after the fasteners are off.

steps.title: Refit the lamp and access parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the taped joint and lamp attachment. Tighten the mounting nuts to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector, and reinstall the lid trim, latch cover and emergency release handle.

watchFor.title: Resistance after removing the nuts
watchFor.body: The sealing tape can still hold the lamp. Release that joint rather than assuming another pull will free it.

watchFor.title: Excessive tightening
watchFor.body: The lamp nut specification is in pound-inches. Do not confuse it with pound-feet.

notes: This access and removal sequence applies to the convertible lamp installation.

diagnostics.finding: The high-mounted stoplamp remains unlit when the brake pedal is applied.
diagnostics.meaning: The stoplamp concern remains unresolved; lamp replacement alone has not established its cause.
diagnostics.next: Continue stoplamp-system diagnosis rather than assuming another lamp is required.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm the lamp attachment, connector, trim retainers, latch cover and emergency release handle have all been restored.

verification.title: Check the braking signal
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal and confirm the high-mounted stoplamp illuminates, consistent with the system’s described operation.

procedures.purpose: Convertible high-mounted stoplamp removal and installation, including luggage-lid access, sealing-tape release and lamp fastening.

guides.title: Remove and install the convertible top assembly
guides.summary: Remove the complete convertible roof with controlled frame compression and coordinated lifting, then restore its attachments, initialization and latching adjustment.
guides.introduction: The convertible top combines folding structure, roof material, a water-management trough and synchronized electric motors. Removing the complete assembly is a substantial body repair involving trim, wiring and carefully managed clearance around the rear body opening. It may be needed for assembly replacement or to reach individual roof components on a workbench.
guides.why: The folded roof must pass close to painted panels and exposed sheet-metal edges. Its frame is temporarily drawn inward to obtain clearance, but excessive compression can damage it. Trough alignment, material placement and floating-bow support also matter: a roof that has been bolted back in place still needs these details restored and its latching effort adjusted.

when.summary: When the complete roof needs replacement or removal is required to service its components.
notes: A roof that will not operate needs diagnosis before complete assembly replacement is chosen.
Follow the specified roof positions during the work; many procedure views show a fully closed roof for illustration.

prepare.title: Provide protection and coordinated handling
prepare.detail: Arrange another technician, a suitable workbench, full body coverage with fender blankets or equivalent, and a large tarp or blanket for the seat-belt tower edges.

prepare.title: Prepare for measured frame compression
prepare.detail: Have a measurement tape, ratchet strap and torque tools available. Use the measurement and strap attachment locations in the complete procedure.

prepare.title: Plan access and finishing work
prepare.detail: Allow for subwoofer removal if fitted, parcel-shelf removal, tension-belt adjustment and conditional motor removal for bench component work.

steps.title: Release the tension-belt brackets
steps.body: Protect the body and remove the subwoofer if fitted. From the luggage compartment on both sides, push in the rear of each tension-belt adjuster to release its locking tabs, pull its rear downward, and pass the bracket through the body into the interior.

steps.title: Disconnect the water-management trough
steps.body: Remove the [convertible parcel shelf](#/document/G1692611), then open the roof approximately halfway. Disconnect both trough hanging retainers and slide the water-bag portions from their brackets. Note the alignment notches and original material positions before pulling the trough from the floating-bow track along the back and sides.

steps.title: Clear modules, speakers and wiring
steps.body: Fully open the roof. On the right only, release the radio transceiver module (RTM) harness clips and bracket fasteners, then position the assembly aside. Remove the cellular antenna modules and rear quarter speakers with their brackets as directed. Disconnect the roof harness connectors and routing clips.

steps.title: Release the roof mountings
steps.body: Loosen the forward mounting-bracket bolts approximately 13 mm (1/2 in.) for guide-pin clearance. Follow the [assembly procedure](#/document/G1708670) when removing the remaining mounting bolts, retaining the designated positioning bolt. Remove the floating-bow bolt on each side.

steps.title: Position the assembly for clearance
steps.body: Grasp both sides near the gears and motors and draw them together to release the guide pins from the interior sheet metal. With the second technician, lift and tilt this area upward and rearward until it rests on top of the interior sheet metal.

steps.title: Measure and restrain the frame
steps.body: Measure the frame width at the indicated locations. Attach the ratchet strap to the bottom of both floating-bow brackets and reduce their separation by no more than 140 mm (5.5 in.). Cover exposed sheet-metal edges on the seat-belt towers before lifting farther.

steps.title: Lift the roof clear together
steps.body: Coordinate the movements with the second technician. Raise the right side while pressing the floating-bow area inward until that side clears the body, then move the floating-bow portion outward. Move the assembly toward the right while raising the left side, and remove it at the rear onto the workbench.

steps.title: Prepare only the necessary bench work
steps.body: If component access requires repositioning the roof on the bench, remove both motors using the [motor procedure](#/document/G1708675). Skip that operation when replacing the complete assembly. Reinstall the floating-bow bolts during component disassembly and assembly to protect the rear-window support rods.

steps.title: Transfer parts and reinstall
steps.body: Transfer parts as necessary and reverse removal, using the specified fastener torques. Restore the trough alignment notches and place all flexible trough material and roof material exactly where they were originally positioned. Reconnect the harnesses, brackets, speakers and removed trim.

steps.title: Initialize and adjust
steps.body: After complete assembly replacement, fully close and latch the roof, then reopen it to initialize the motors. Perform the [tension-belt buckle adjustment](#/document/G2401442). With new roof material, leave the roof continuously closed and latched for at least one week to allow it to stretch.

watchFor.title: Excessive frame compression
watchFor.body: The working reduction limit is 140 mm (5.5 in.). Reduction exceeding 165 mm (6.5 in.) can damage the assembly.

watchFor.title: Unprotected contact points
watchFor.body: Maintain body protection throughout handling; cover the seat-belt tower edges before the roof passes over them.

notes: Higher latching effort is expected initially with new material. Opening the roof during its closed break-in period may extend that period.

diagnostics.finding: The roof does not move when commanded.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation depends on accessory-delay availability, latch or tonneau-cover conditions, and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Check these operating conditions before treating non-operation as a reason to replace the assembly.

verification.title: Check restored installation details
verification.body: Confirm trough alignment, original material placement, harness routing and reinstalled attachments before operating the roof.

verification.title: Record initialization and adjustment
verification.body: Record completion of tension-belt adjustment and, after assembly replacement, the close–latch–reopen initialization. Operate the switch while stationary with accessory delay active, releasing the latch to open and removing fitted tonneau covers to close.

guides.title: Replace the convertible rear quarter window regulator motor
guides.summary: Replace the quarter-window drive motor, refit the regulator assembly and adjust the glass against the door window and convertible-top seals.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter window motor drives the regulator that raises and lowers the small glass behind the door. The convertible’s master window switch operates these windows. This repair involves removing the glass/regulator assembly and checking its alignment after installation.
guides.why: Motor replacement restores the drive mechanism, but correct glass positioning remains essential. The quarter glass must meet the door glass and enter the roof seals correctly without catching on either.
searchTerms: convertible rear quarter window will not raise
rear quarter window will not close

when.summary: When motor replacement has been justified, or motor removal is required during quarter-window regulator work.
notes: An inoperative window alone does not establish that its motor has failed.

prepare.title: Prepare for access and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools, a torque wrench and equipment for accurate millimetre measurements. Allow access to the rear speaker area and space to operate the convertible top.

prepare.title: Plan the glass-position branch
prepare.detail: Glass must be fully raised before separating it from the regulator. If it is inoperative, the regulator procedure provides a motor-removal branch to permit glass movement and bolt access.

steps.title: Open the quarter-panel access
steps.body: Lower the convertible top. Follow the [regulator removal procedure](#/document/G1695925), including removal of the radio transceiver module (RTM) on the right side, the rear quarter speaker and the interior belt moulding. Position the exterior moulding aside.

steps.title: Establish the required glass position
steps.body: Raise the glass fully if it operates. Follow the inoperative-glass branch when necessary. The separate glass-to-regulator removal step is required when installing a new regulator; avoid treating it as an automatic part of a motor-only repair.

steps.title: Remove the assembly
steps.body: Remove the speaker bracket, release the wiring retainers and watershields, and disconnect the motor connector in the prescribed sequence. Remove the assembly retaining nuts and take out the glass/regulator assembly.

steps.title: Exchange the motor and refit
steps.body: Remove the motor mounting bolts and separate the motor from the regulator as shown in the [motor procedure](#/document/G1695926). Reverse the removal sequence to install it and restore the assembly, electrical connection, wiring retainers and watershields.

steps.title: Set height and fore/aft alignment
steps.body: Carry out the [glass adjustment procedure](#/document/G1697267), including its access preparations. With the top lowered, door closed and windows fully raised, measure the glass gaps and relative height. Loosen the glass bolts only enough to adjust, then tighten without shifting the glass.

steps.title: Set inward/outward alignment
steps.body: With the top closed, windows raised and door open, inspect the division-bar seal engagement. If adjustment is needed, lower the top and follow the jack-screw sequence for the base and upper glass pitch. Repeat both alignment checks, tighten without moving the assembly and reinstall the access components.

watchFor.title: No automatic reversal
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have bounce-back protection. Keep the glass path clear while operating the windows.

watchFor.title: Alignment changes during tightening
watchFor.body: Holding or pushing the glass while tightening its bolts or assembly nuts can alter the position just measured.

notes: The motor procedure illustrates the right side; the left side uses a similar method.

diagnostics.finding: The quarter glass is inoperative and its attachment bolts cannot be reached.
diagnostics.meaning: The glass position is obstructing access; this does not identify the electrical cause.
diagnostics.next: Use the regulator procedure’s motor-removal branch to permit glass movement where separation is required.

verification.title: Record the glass measurements
verification.body: Record the door-to-quarter glass gap at points 7.5mm from the belt-moulding base and 7.5mm from the top of the door glass. Each gap must be 9.8mm ± 1.5mm, with top-to-bottom variance within ± 1.0mm. Record the quarter glass height: level with, or up to 1mm above, the door glass.

verification.title: Confirm seal engagement
verification.body: With the top closed and windows fully raised, confirm that the division-bar seal fully enters the top seals and engages the door glass without clipping. Repeat adjustment until both dimensional and seal checks pass.

procedures.purpose: Convertible rear quarter window motor removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace the convertible-top stay pad
guides.summary: Release the roof trim, fabric and riveted stay-pad attachments, remove all rivet debris, and restore the original mounting arrangement.
guides.introduction: The stay pad is part of the convertible top's webbing and tension-belt arrangement, attached along the front panel and roof crossbows. Replacing it requires access beneath the fabric and headliner rather than simply removing an exposed strap. The work also involves the wiring routed through the left-hand stay-pad webbing and the material attachments at the floating bow.
guides.why: The roof needs slack during this work, even though the procedure illustrations show it closed. Marked weatherstrip bracket positions and retained shim locations help preserve the original fit. Drilled rivet ends can fall inside the hollow crossbows; leaving them there can introduce a rattle after an otherwise successful repair.

when.summary: When a convertible-top stay pad requires replacement.
notes: A roof that will not operate does not, by itself, identify a stay-pad fault.

prepare.title: Prepare roof-trim and riveting capability
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill, rivet gun, compressed air and an air nozzle, plus tools suitable for the trim and bracket fasteners. Plan how to collect rivet ends and shavings.

prepare.title: Preserve installation references
prepare.detail: Prepare to mark weatherstrip bracket positions and retain any shims in their original locations. Use the convertible-top assembly procedure for associated access requirements.

steps.title: Position the roof for slack
steps.body: Work with the convertible top approximately 25–50 percent open so the fabric and related components are slack. The fully closed position shown in the procedure views is not the service position.

steps.title: Release the front trim and headliner attachments
steps.body: Remove the latch handle. Remove the front panel trim's front retainers, release the clips beneath its rear edge and remove the trim. Remove the headliner push pins along the back of the front panel, then remove both headliner tension brackets and their retainers.

steps.title: Preserve the weatherstrip bracket positions
steps.body: On both sides, note any shim positions and mark the side weatherstrip bracket assemblies at their retainers. Remove the retainers and weatherstrip/bracket assemblies. Remove the roof-material push pins at the back of the front panel.

steps.title: Expose the front stay-pad attachments
steps.body: On both sides, pull the roof material backward and down to release the front underside clips. Separate it from the double-sided tape, then roll it forward and up over the front panel. Fold the front material back to the first crossbow to expose the tension-cable end and stay-pad rivets.

steps.title: Release the riveted attachments
steps.body: Drill out the front-panel stay-pad rivets, then slide the stay pad toward the panel's center to disconnect it. Pull the headliner edge inward to reach the stay-pad-to-crossbow rivets and drill them out. Follow the illustrated side-specific access; the opposite side is similar.

steps.title: Remove every rivet fragment
steps.body: Clear the two center crossbows, then the front and rear crossbows. Blow compressed air through the rivet holes to move pieces toward the outer ends; multiple holes may be needed. Collect debris at both ends of each crossbow and account for all rivet ends. Remove shavings and pieces from the roof assembly and vehicle interior.

steps.title: Free the wiring and floating-bow material
steps.body: Disconnect the rear-window wiring connector and routing connector, if equipped, and route the harness through the left-hand stay-pad webbing to free it. Partially disconnect the roof material from the floating bow. Remove its material-retaining clips from the bow and preserve their correct installation locations on the material.

steps.title: Remove the stay pad
steps.body: Remove the stay-pad retaining screw and slide the tension belt out of the floating bow. Keep the removal path clear so the replacement can follow the same attachment arrangement.

steps.title: Install and restore the roof attachments
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, using the rivet gun to restore the riveted attachments. Restore the tension belt, wiring route and connectors, and place the floating-bow clips correctly on the roof material. Return weatherstrip brackets and shims to their recorded positions, then restore fabric, headliner, trim and latch handle. Follow the individual fastening values in the stay-pad procedure; the retaining screw is tightened to 62 lb.in (7 Nm).

watchFor.title: Debris trapped inside a bow
watchFor.body: Surface cleanup is insufficient if rivet ends remain inside the crossbows. Both ends of every affected bow require checking.

watchFor.title: Floating-bow clips in the wrong place
watchFor.body: The material-retaining clips must be positioned correctly on the roof material during installation, rather than left on the floating bow.

notes: Normal roof movement requires the operating interlocks to be satisfied, including confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully down.

diagnostics.finding: A rattle appears after the rivets have been drilled out.
diagnostics.meaning: A retained rivet end inside a crossbow is a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the affected crossbows and collect remaining fragments before closing the access.

verification.title: Record debris recovery
verification.body: Before covering the bows, confirm and record that all rivet ends are accounted for and both ends of each affected crossbow have been checked.

verification.title: Confirm the restored arrangement
verification.body: Confirm original shim and bracket positions, correct floating-bow clip placement, wiring routing and reconnection, and completion of the reverse installation sequence.

procedures.purpose: Complete stay-pad removal and installation, including roof-material access, rivet removal, crossbow debris recovery and attachment restoration.
Referenced convertible-top assembly removal and installation procedure for associated access requirements.

guides.title: Remove and install the automatic-transmission flexplate on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove the automatic transmission, service the flexplate using the engine-specific fastener requirements, and complete the required misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The flexplate is the engine-mounted drive plate connecting the crankshaft to the automatic transmission's torque converter. Its toothed outer rim provides the starter's engagement surface. Reaching it requires transmission removal, so this is a substantial driveline repair even though the plate itself has relatively few attachments. The three engine variants share the overall access path but use different bolt and tightening instructions.
guides.why: Flexplate fasteners secure a rotating connection that carries engine torque. Their specified tightening method must match the engine. The 2.3L requires new special bolts, and the 5.0L uses non-reusable torque-to-yield bolts. All three branches also require a scan-tool correction after repair, including when the original flexplate is refitted.

when.summary: When flexplate repair or replacement has been established, or it must be removed during related engine work.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before ordering parts or planning transmission removal.

prepare.title: Lifting and transmission-removal capability
prepare.detail: Use suitable hoist facilities and the complete engine-specific transmission procedure. Locate the designated lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this work.

prepare.title: Holding, tightening and scan equipment
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures specify flywheel holding tool 303-103 (T74P-6375-A). Have appropriate torque equipment, angle measurement for the 5.0L branch, and a diagnostic scan tool capable of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

prepare.title: Correct replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Obtain new special flexplate bolts for the 2.3L and new flexplate bolts for the 5.0L. Use engine identification information when selecting parts.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle using its engine branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist as directed. Follow the [lifting guidance](#/document/G1663631), including correct support locations and clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components. For the 5.0L, begin with its transmission-removal procedure.

steps.title: Remove the automatic transmission
steps.body: Use the [2.3L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692044), [3.7L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692046) or [5.0L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692048). This exposes the flexplate; complete the applicable access sequence before working on its fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the flexplate and handle the bolts correctly
steps.body: On the 2.3L and 5.0L, install holding tool 303-103 before removing the bolts and plate, and discard those bolts. On the 3.7L, remove the bolts and flexplate as directed by its procedure.

steps.title: Install with the engine-specific tightening method
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1945806), use new special bolts, never standard bolts, and tighten through 50 Nm, 80 Nm and 112 Nm stages. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1681522), align the offset hole, which permits only one installation position, and tighten to 80 Nm in the illustrated sequence. For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685324), fit new bolts and tighten first to 20 Nm, then a further 60°.

steps.title: Remove the holding tool and reinstall the transmission
steps.body: Remove holding tool 303-103 on the branches where it was fitted. Reinstall the automatic transmission through the same engine-specific procedure used for removal.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction and conditional road test
steps.body: After repairs, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the diagnostic scan tool on every engine branch. If a new flexplate was installed, road test the vehicle afterward.

watchFor.title: Mixing tightening methods
watchFor.body: The 5.0L torque-and-angle method is distinct from the 2.3L staged torque method and the 3.7L torque-and-sequence instruction.

watchFor.title: Ignoring the 3.7L indexing hole
watchFor.body: Align the offset hole to establish the correct position, then use that procedure's illustrated tightening order.

notes: Follow the fastener and tightening instructions for the fitted engine; keep discarded bolts separate from installation hardware.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm the applicable tightening process is complete, any holding tool has been removed, and the transmission installation is finished.

verification.title: Record scan-tool correction
verification.body: Record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction for the repaired vehicle.

verification.title: Record the replacement road test
verification.body: When a new flexplate was fitted, record completion of the required road test.

guides.title: Flywheel replacement for 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and install the manual-transmission flywheel using the correct engine-specific fasteners, tightening stages and final misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The flywheel connects the rear of the crankshaft to the clutch and provides the rotating surface against which the clutch works. Removing it requires clutch access first. Although the four engine versions follow a similar overall path, their bolt requirements and tightening methods differ substantially. This is an advanced repair that also requires a diagnostic scan tool after mechanical assembly.
guides.why: Correct bolt clamping keeps the flywheel secured to the crankshaft. Reusing bolts designated for disposal, substituting ordinary bolts where special ones are required, or borrowing another engine's tightening schedule can compromise that attachment. The final electronic correction is also part of the repair: mechanical reassembly alone does not finish the prescribed work.
searchTerms: misfire monitor correction after flywheel replacement

when.summary: When flywheel removal or replacement is required during clutch or engine repair.
notes: Identify the installed engine before selecting parts and instructions.

prepare.title: Arrange clutch access and safe lifting
prepare.detail: Have the matching clutch procedure and suitable lifting facilities available. Use the identified lifting points, check hoist clearance and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific equipment
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures require flywheel holding tool 303-103. Have suitable torque equipment, angle measurement for the 5.0L final stage, and a scan tool supporting the specified correction routine.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct fasteners
prepare.detail: Plan new special flywheel bolts for the 2.3L and new torque-to-yield bolts for the 5.0L and 5.2L. Follow the separate 3.7L fastener and tightening instructions for that engine.

steps.title: Remove the clutch through the matching engine procedure
steps.body: Follow the linked clutch disc and pressure plate procedure for the installed engine. The 2.3L and 3.7L flywheel instructions begin with the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Complete the specified clutch removal before working on the flywheel.

steps.title: Release the flywheel attachment
steps.body: Install holding tool 303-103 on the 2.3L or 5.0L. Remove the flywheel bolts and flywheel. Discard the bolts on the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L; the two V8 procedures explicitly identify their bolts as non-reusable torque-to-yield fasteners.

steps.title: Position the flywheel and correct bolts
steps.body: Fit the flywheel using the fasteners required by its engine procedure. The 2.3L requires special new bolts, not standard substitutes. On the 3.7L, one of the eight mounting holes is offset, so the flywheel fits in only one position.

steps.title: Apply the exact tightening schedule
steps.body: For the 2.3L, tighten in stages to 50 Nm, 80 Nm and 112 Nm. The 3.7L uses 80 Nm. The 5.0L uses 10 Nm, 20 Nm and then 60°. The 5.2L uses 10 Nm, 20 Nm and then 80 Nm. Complete every stage in order, then remove holding tool 303-103 where fitted.

steps.title: Reinstall the clutch
steps.body: Complete clutch installation through the same engine-specific procedure used for removal. Its assembly requirements remain part of the job; the flywheel instructions do not replace them.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction
steps.body: For the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the scan tool. For the 5.2L, use the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine.

watchFor.title: Similar V8 stages with different endings
watchFor.body: The 5.0L finishes with an angle turn; the 5.2L finishes with a torque setting. Their initial stages do not make the complete schedules interchangeable.

notes: Use the engine identification information when ordering replacement parts; parts can differ within an engine family.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check that the correct fasteners and tightening stages were used, the holding tool has been removed where applicable, and clutch installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the correction result
verification.body: Record the engine variant and successful completion of its specified scan-tool routine.

guides.title: Replace a 6-piston front brake caliper on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the 6-piston front caliper with new mounting bolts and hose washers, then pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the pads against the brake disc. Removing it separates both its mechanical mounting and its brake-hose connection. This procedure covers the 5.0L application equipped with 6-piston front calipers, including the required pad-removal prerequisite, replacement hardware and final bleeding operation.
guides.why: The mounting bolts secure the caliper, while the washers seal the hydraulic hose connection. Both have explicit discard instructions, so they must be replaced during installation. Opening the hose connection also makes brake-system bleeding a required finishing phase. Clean, sealed openings help protect the hydraulic circuit while it is disconnected.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of a 6-piston front brake caliper.
notes: This procedure gives the replacement path; it does not diagnose the cause of a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct hardware and tools
prepare.detail: Have new caliper mounting bolts, new brake-hose sealing washers, suitable tools and torque equipment. The removed mounting bolts and washers must not return to service.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic protection and bleeding
prepare.detail: Provide suitable means to seal every opened connection and the equipment and capability for Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Have the linked 6-piston brake-pad procedure available for removal and installation.

steps.title: Remove the brake pads
steps.body: Follow Brake Pads — Vehicles With: 6-Piston Brake Caliper before removing the caliper. This is the first required phase and provides the equipment-specific pad handling and installation details.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the brake-hose flow bolt, disconnect the hose and discard the sealing washers. Seal all openings. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts, discard them and remove the caliper. If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Refit with replacement hardware
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Install the caliper with new mounting bolts and tighten them to 115 Nm. Reconnect the hose with new sealing washers and tighten the flow bolt to 40 Nm. Reinstall the pads using the dedicated 6-piston procedure.

steps.title: Complete pressure bleeding
steps.body: Perform Brake System Pressure Bleeding after reassembly. Follow that complete procedure for the hydraulic finishing phase; bolting the caliper back into place does not complete a repair that opened the brake circuit.

watchFor.title: Old hardware mixed with new parts
watchFor.body: Keep the discarded caliper mounting bolts and hose sealing washers separate from installation hardware. Follow the flow-bolt and washer instructions for the exact fitted caliper.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint or exposed openings
watchFor.body: Wash paint contamination immediately with cold water and keep disconnected hydraulic openings sealed.

notes: The illustrated pair of mounting bolts is the pair that must be discarded.

verification.title: Confirm the completed assembly
verification.body: Verify installation of new mounting bolts and sealing washers, the specified fastener tightening and completion of the pad installation.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm that the required brake-system pressure-bleeding procedure has been completed before closing the repair.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L 6-piston front caliper removal and installation, including discarded hardware, tightening and the pressure-bleeding requirement.
Equipment-specific brake-pad removal before caliper service and pad installation during reassembly.

authoring.method: Codex source review of fastener language and required HCU commissioning

guides.title: Replace the rear brake pads
guides.summary: Remove and refit the rear brake pads while protecting the brake hose and correctly engaging the caliper’s parking-brake mechanism.
guides.introduction: The rear brake pads press against the brake disc to produce braking force. They sit on either side of the disc inside the caliper assembly, as the illustration shows. Replacing them involves more than exchanging friction material: the caliper piston must accommodate the new pads, and its notch must align with the locating pin on the inboard pad. This procedure covers the rear brakes for the supplied 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
guides.why: The rear caliper incorporates a parking-brake mechanism that affects piston retraction. The retractor needs moderate to heavy force toward the piston so the internal clutch cone engages; without that engagement, the piston will not compress. Supporting the removed caliper also matters because its weight can damage the flexible brake hose.
searchTerms: rear caliper piston will not retract

when.summary: When rear brake pads require replacement or removal during brake service.
notes: Piston retraction is specified when installing new pads.
This procedure does not establish a pad wear limit or diagnose the cause of abnormal wear.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Use the linked Wheel and Tire procedure for removal and refitting, with the capability to support the vehicle safely. Have a way to support the caliper independently of its hose.

prepare.title: Have the correct retraction equipment
prepare.detail: A brake caliper piston retractor is required for new-pad installation. Have suitable fastening tools and the specified brake fluid available for the final level check.

steps.title: Expose and move the caliper
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the [wheel procedure](#/document/G1686507). Following the [rear brake-pad procedure](#/document/G1693756), remove the caliper bolts and position the caliper aside on its support. Keep its weight off the brake hose throughout the work.

steps.title: Remove the pads and clips
steps.body: Remove the pads from their positions around the disc, then remove the clips. Keep track of the clip locations and the inboard pad’s locating pin so those relationships can be restored during assembly.

steps.title: Retract the piston when fitting new pads
steps.body: Use the brake caliper piston retractor to retract the piston into its bore. Apply the specified moderate to heavy force toward the piston; this engages the internal parking-brake clutch cone and allows compression.

steps.title: Restore the pad and piston alignment
steps.body: Reinstall the clips and pads in reverse removal order. Before fitting the caliper over them, make sure the piston notch aligns with the pin on the inboard pad. Refit the caliper bolts and tighten them to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm).

steps.title: Complete reassembly and the hydraulic check
steps.body: Finish reversing the removal procedure, including wheel installation. Depress the brake pedal, then check the reservoir level and top up as necessary using the fluid specified in [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

watchFor.title: A caliper hanging from its hose
watchFor.body: Reposition its support immediately; the hose must not carry the caliper’s weight.

watchFor.title: A locating pin that misses the piston notch
watchFor.body: Correct the alignment before installing the caliper. This is an explicit assembly requirement.

diagnostics.finding: The piston does not compress during retraction.
diagnostics.meaning: Insufficient force toward the piston can prevent the parking-brake clutch cone from engaging; resistance alone does not establish that the caliper has failed.
diagnostics.next: Check that the specified retractor is being used with the required force and follow the complete procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm the clips and pads are installed, the inboard pin matches the piston notch, and the caliper fasteners are tightened.

verification.title: Record the completion checks
verification.body: Record that the brake pedal was depressed and the reservoir level checked, including any top-up with the specified fluid.

procedures.purpose: Rear brake-pad removal and installation, including conditional piston retraction, for the supplied 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Wheel and tire removal and installation needed for brake access.
Brake-fluid specification for the final reservoir check and any necessary top-up.

guides.title: Replace the rear brake disc shield with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the rear brake disc shield by removing the parking brake shoes and rear hub, then rebuilding those assemblies with the required new fasteners.
guides.introduction: The brake disc shield is the stationary plate behind the rear brake disc. On the 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, reaching its mounting bolts requires removal of both the parking brake shoes and the wheel bearing and hub assembly. The shield itself is straightforward to replace; most of the work lies in gaining access and correctly restoring the brake and hub assemblies.
guides.why: The hub connects the wheel to the rear suspension and halfshaft, so its fastening requirements remain critical even when the original repair concerns only the shield. The spindle nut and hub bolts must be renewed, and the hub installation includes both cross-pattern tightening and a staged spindle-nut tightening sequence.
searchTerms: SVT rear brake disc shield replacement
rear hub removal for brake shield

when.summary: When an inspected rear brake disc shield requires replacement on a car with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: This is a removal and installation job; it does not establish whether a brake noise originates at the shield.

prepare.title: Plan the brake and hub access work
prepare.detail: Arrange safe wheel-off access and the capability to remove and reinstall the package-specific parking brake shoes, rear brake disc and hub. Follow the prerequisite procedures reached through the shield instructions.

prepare.title: Have the puller and replacement hardware ready
prepare.detail: The rear hub procedure specifies tool 205-D070 (D93P-1175-B), Remover, Front Wheel Hub. Obtain a new spindle nut and four new hub bolts, plus suitable torque and angle-tightening equipment.

steps.title: Remove the parking brake shoes
steps.body: Begin with the SVT Performance Package parking brake shoe procedure referenced by the [shield procedure](#/document/G1716402). Complete that access phase before removing the hub. Keep track of components already removed so the overlapping brake and hub procedures remain a coherent job.

steps.title: Release the halfshaft and remove the hub
steps.body: Follow the [rear wheel bearing and hub procedure](#/document/G1686657). Remove and discard the spindle nut, then use the specified remover to press the halfshaft from the hub. Complete the required brake-disc access, discard the four hub bolts and remove the bearing and hub assembly.

steps.title: Remove the exposed shield
steps.body: With the parking brake shoes and hub out of the way, remove the shield bolts and lift away the shield. This is the component replacement phase; the preceding removals provide access to its otherwise obstructed mounting area.

steps.title: Install the replacement shield
steps.body: Position the shield and reinstall its bolts, reversing its removal. Tighten the shield bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Keep this specification separate from the much higher hub-fastener tightening requirements.

steps.title: Restore the hub and brake assemblies
steps.body: Reverse the access work through the hub and package-specific parking brake procedures, coordinating their shared disc and wheel access. Install four new hub bolts and tighten them in a cross pattern. Apply the brake to prevent halfshaft rotation while completing the full staged tightening sequence for the new spindle nut.

watchFor.title: Discarded hardware returning to service
watchFor.body: The removed spindle nut and four hub bolts must not return to service. Keep discarded hardware separate and follow the distinct shield-attachment instructions.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable suspension fasteners
watchFor.body: Replacement suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design. Their role in retaining the hub makes substitution with lesser-quality parts unacceptable.

notes: The linked hub procedure applies to several engines; the shield and parking brake access here are specifically for the SVT Performance Package.
The illustration shows the hub-removal access area and the hub bolts designated for disposal.

verification.title: Confirm shield and brake reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the shield bolts are tightened and all parking brake, brake-disc and wheel installation work required by the access procedures is complete.

verification.title: Confirm hub fastening
verification.body: Verify that new hub bolts received cross-pattern tightening and that the new spindle nut received every stage of its specified tightening sequence.

procedures.purpose: SVT Performance Package rear brake disc shield removal and installation, including parking brake shoe prerequisites.
Rear wheel bearing and hub removal and installation, including halfshaft release, replacement fasteners and staged tightening.
