guides.title: Remove and replace the rear subframe
guides.summary: Lower the supported rear subframe, transfer components when replacing it, and reinstall it with new required fasteners and final fluid and camber checks.
guides.introduction: The rear subframe bolts to the body, contributes structural support and provides mounting points for the rear suspension arms. It also carries the differential involved in this removal. Changing it disturbs suspension, driveline and potentially cooling-system connections, so the job combines several component procedures with controlled lowering and accurate repositioning.
guides.why: Subframe position affects suspension alignment and drivetrain operation. Index marks preserve installation references, while final camber checking verifies the resulting geometry. Several fasteners must be discarded during removal. Their replacements and specified tightening are essential because these joints secure suspension and driveline components.

when.summary: When the rear subframe requires removal or has been identified for replacement.
notes: Differential and upper-arm transfer are required when installing a new subframe.
Confirm optional suspension sensors and differential cooling connections before lowering.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and suspension capability
prepare.detail: Use the specified 300-OTC1585AE Powertrain Lift beneath the subframe. The workshop must also support the vehicle safely and carry out the linked halfshaft, toe-link, spring and stabilizer-bar procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Provide new driveshaft-to-pinion bolts and forward and rearward subframe bolts. Component transfer also requires replacement differential mounting bolts and the discarded upper-arm flag-bolt and nut. Use the same or equivalent quality and design.

prepare.title: Plan the completion work
prepare.detail: Have means to support the disconnected driveshaft, make installation reference marks, tighten fasteners correctly, check differential fluid level and check or adjust rear camber.

steps.title: Remove the suspension and axle prerequisites
steps.body: Follow [Rear Subframe](#/document/G1686636), using the linked component procedures. Remove both rear halfshafts, both toe links, both rear springs and the rear stabilizer bar, in that order. If dynamic suspension is fitted, remove both rear ride-height sensors.

steps.title: Separate the driveshaft correctly
steps.body: Index-mark the driveshaft and pinion flange, then remove and discard their connecting bolts. Support the driveshaft. Insert a screwdriver into the pinion-flange slot and pry the joint free. Do not pull on the driveshaft tube: that can damage the constant-velocity (CV) joint.

steps.title: Release the differential connections
steps.body: Disconnect the differential fluid-temperature sensor if fitted. On cooler-equipped vehicles, remove the return-line retaining clip and line, then the supply-line clip and line, positioning both lines aside. Disconnect the differential vent tube.

steps.title: Support and lower the subframe
steps.body: Index-mark the subframe on both sides and position the powertrain lift beneath it. Remove and discard the forward subframe bolts. Remove the bracket bolts and brackets, then remove and discard the rearward subframe bolts. Lower the assembly with the lift.

steps.title: Transfer components when fitting a new subframe
steps.body: Remove and discard the differential mounting bolts and transfer the differential. Remove and discard the upper-arm-to-frame flag-bolt and nut and transfer the arm. Install the transferred components with new fasteners and tighten as specified in the procedure.

steps.title: Raise, locate and secure the subframe
steps.body: Raise the subframe with the powertrain lift. Install new rearward bolts finger-tight, then fit the brackets and their bolts finger-tight. Install new forward bolts. Align the reference marks on both sides before tightening the bracket bolts, forward bolts and rearward bolts in the specified order.

steps.title: Restore differential and driveline connections
steps.body: Reconnect the vent and any fitted temperature sensor. Install the cooling supply line and retaining clip, then the return line and clip, where fitted. Align the driveshaft and pinion-flange index marks and install new connecting bolts to the specified torque.

steps.title: Reinstall the suspension components
steps.body: Install both ride-height sensors if fitted, followed by the stabilizer bar, rear springs, toe links and rear halfshafts. Use each component's installation procedure for its particular assembly and fastening requirements.

steps.title: Complete fluid and alignment checks
steps.body: Check differential fluid level using Differential Fluid Level Check. Check rear camber and adjust it if necessary using Rear Camber Adjustment. These checks remain required even when the removal index marks line up.

watchFor.title: A connection still attached during lowering
watchFor.body: Account for the vent, optional sensor, cooling lines and supported driveshaft before lowering the subframe.

watchFor.title: Discarded fasteners returning to service
watchFor.body: Keep discarded bolts separate from the bracket hardware and replacement fasteners so they cannot be installed accidentally.

watchFor.title: Position fixed before reference alignment
watchFor.body: Keep the rearward and bracket bolts finger-tight at the specified stage; align the marks before final tightening.

notes: Suspension fasteners must not be replaced with parts of lesser quality or a substitute design.
Index marks provide installation references; final rear camber still requires checking.

verification.title: Confirm installation and connections
verification.body: Verify reference-mark alignment, required new fasteners, specified tightening, restored vent and optional cooling connections, and completion of the component installation procedures.

verification.title: Record fluid and camber results
verification.body: Record the differential fluid-level check and rear camber result, including whether adjustment was necessary.

procedures.purpose: Rear subframe removal and installation, optional differential connections, replacement-only component transfer, fastening sequence and final checks.
Removal and installation of both rear halfshafts before and after subframe work.
Removal and installation of both rear toe links.
Required rear spring removal and installation.
Rear stabilizer-bar removal and installation.
Rear ride-height sensor removal and installation on vehicles equipped with dynamic suspension.

applicability.equipment: Dynamic suspension, differential temperature sensor and differential cooling system, if fitted

guides.title: Replace the brake hydraulic control unit
guides.summary: Remove and refit the hydraulic control unit, pressure-bleed the brakes, and initialize and calibrate a newly installed unit.
guides.introduction: The hydraulic control unit (HCU) controls brake-fluid delivery during anti-lock braking and stability-control intervention. These systems help prevent wheel lock and unwanted skidding by adjusting braking at the wheels. The HCU is a separately serviced component from the anti-lock brake system (ABS) electronic module.
guides.why: Disconnecting the brake tubes opens the hydraulic circuit, making pressure bleeding a required installation stage. A new HCU also needs scan-tool initialization and valve calibration. Secure mounting and reconnected pipes alone do not complete the repair.
searchTerms: longer pedal travel after ABS activation

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the HCU requires replacement, or the unit must be removed for related work.
notes: Normal ABS intervention noise and pedal feedback do not establish HCU failure.

prepare.title: Provide brake hydraulic service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange suitable means of sealing every opened connection, torque-controlled reassembly and the equipment and procedure for Brake System Pressure Bleeding.

prepare.title: Arrange scan-tool completion
prepare.detail: For a new HCU, have a scan tool capable of ABS service bleeding as well as the named IVD Initialization Sequence and Valve Calibration routines.

prepare.title: Confirm the replacement component
prepare.detail: The ABS module and HCU are supplied individually. A new ABS module does not include an HCU.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connection
steps.body: Begin the HCU removal procedure by disconnecting the ABS module electrical connector. This releases the electrical connection before the hydraulic unit is separated from its mounting.

steps.title: Disconnect and seal the brake tubes
steps.body: Disconnect the six brake-tube fittings and seal all openings. Protect the exposed hydraulic connections from contamination throughout the work. If brake fluid reaches painted surfaces, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Separate the HCU from its bracket
steps.body: Remove the retaining bolt and separate the HCU from the bracket using the illustrated mounting arrangement. The illustration identifies the unit and its bracket attachment points.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the unit
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to mount the HCU and reconnect the brake tubes and electrical connector. Follow the fitting-specific torque assignments in the complete procedure: the brake-tube connections have different specified tightening values.

steps.title: Bleed and complete the new-unit routines
steps.body: Carry out [Brake System Pressure Bleeding](#/document/G2361881) after installation. A new HCU requires a complete pressure bleed, the scan-tool ABS service bleed, and a second complete pressure bleed. After that hydraulic sequence, perform the IVD Initialization Sequence and Valve Calibration, following the scan-tool instructions through completion.

watchFor.title: Unsealed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Every opened connection must remain sealed during the work. Contamination introduced here enters the brake hydraulic system.

watchFor.title: Paint exposure
watchFor.body: Wash spilled brake fluid from paint immediately with cold water.

notes: Keep the hydraulic-unit replacement decision separate from the electronic-module replacement decision; the components are serviced individually.

diagnostics.finding: Noise or brake-pedal pulsation occurs during ABS or stability-control intervention.
diagnostics.meaning: These can be normal effects of system operation.
diagnostics.next: Do not use this observation alone to justify HCU replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Pedal travel increases immediately after ABS or stability-control activation.
diagnostics.meaning: This can occur following an intervention and does not by itself establish a defective HCU.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the actual complaint before selecting a replacement repair.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record hydraulic completion after reconnection. For a new HCU, confirm both complete pressure-bleeding passes and the ABS service-bleed routine between them.

verification.title: Record initialization and calibration
verification.body: For a new HCU, record the completion results of both scan-tool routines. Include pressure-bleeding completion in the repair record.

procedures.purpose: HCU removal and installation, fitting-specific tightening, pressure-bleeding requirement and new-unit initialization and calibration.
Complete hydraulic pressure bleeding, including the additional scan-tool ABS bleed and second pressure bleed required for a new HCU.

authoring.method: Codex source review of fastener language and required HCU commissioning

guides.title: Replace the intake air temperature sensor on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Disconnect the intake air temperature sensor, release its illustrated twist mounting and reinstall it in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor supplies information about the temperature of incoming air to the electronic engine controls. The powertrain control module (PCM) combines sensor inputs with its stored control strategy to operate the engine. This job removes the sensor from the intake duct shown in the illustration and restores its mounting and electrical connection.
guides.why: The sensor has two separate connections: its electrical plug and its physical mounting in the duct. Disconnecting the plug first leaves the wiring free while the sensor is turned for removal. Following the illustrated release movement avoids treating the sensor as a straight pull-out fitting. Replacement should follow diagnosis, because general engine-control concerns can involve several inputs and do not establish an IAT sensor failure.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires IAT sensor replacement or the sensor needs to be removed for access.
notes: Use this procedure for the 2.3L EcoBoost intake sensor arrangement.

prepare.title: Identify the sensor and mounting
prepare.detail: Match the sensor on the intake duct to the removal illustration, including its connector and twist-release mounting.

prepare.title: Plan controlled handling
prepare.detail: Arrange access to disconnect the plug and turn the sensor without twisting the attached wiring. Review the illustrated removal movement before applying force.

steps.title: Confirm the component
steps.body: Locate the IAT sensor using the [2.3L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692145). Match the component and surrounding duct before disturbing the connection.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical plug
steps.body: Disconnect the IAT sensor electrical connector before moving the sensor. Handle the connector body so the wiring does not carry the removal load.

steps.title: Release and remove the sensor
steps.body: Follow the illustrated 45° counterclockwise release movement and remove the sensor from the duct. Use the mounting illustration to guide the movement rather than pulling against the engaged retention.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the sensor by reversing the removal movement, then reconnect its electrical connector. Complete the physical mounting before restoring the wiring connection.

watchFor.title: Unexpected resistance
watchFor.body: If the sensor does not release with the illustrated movement, recheck the mounting and direction before increasing force.

notes: This is a component replacement procedure, not an electrical test for the cause of a driveability concern.

diagnostics.finding: A general engine-control concern exists without an established IAT fault.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM uses multiple sensor inputs; the complaint alone does not isolate this sensor.
diagnostics.next: Complete the relevant engine-control diagnosis before choosing replacement.

verification.title: Confirm mounting and connection
verification.body: Check that the sensor has returned to its retained installation position and the electrical connector is fully attached.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost IAT sensor connector disconnection, illustrated sensor removal and reverse-sequence installation.

authoring.method: Codex original-image and engine-specific completion review

guides.title: Remove and refit the fuel tank
guides.summary: Remove the drained fuel tank by clearing the exhaust and driveshaft, then restore its mountings, connections and service-opening seals.
guides.introduction: The fuel tank stores fuel and accommodates the pump/sender and fuel-level sensor openings. Its position around the rear driveline makes removal a substantial access job. The work includes moving the exhaust and driveshaft, disconnecting filler and vapor connections, and restoring both sealed openings during installation. Separate procedures apply to the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines.
guides.why: Draining, supporting the driveline and renewing seals address different risks. Excessive driveshaft articulation can damage the shaft, while dirt or damaged sealing faces can compromise an O-ring joint. Index marks preserve the driveshaft's installed relationship to the pinion flange.

when.summary: When tank replacement or a repair requiring tank removal has been established as necessary.
notes: Use the complete draining and coupling procedures for the fitted engine before opening or lowering the tank.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and handling capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated triangle-marked lifting points and check clearance. Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack. Arrange an assistant and a jackstand or mechanics wire for driveshaft support.

prepare.title: Gather the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Have a flat-headed screwdriver, an appropriate impact tool with a TP50 Torx Plus socket, a wire brush and torque tools. Lock-ring tool 310-123 is specified for 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L; the 3.7L procedure calls for a lock-ring wrench.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have new driveshaft-to-pinion bolts, both required O-ring seals and Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B. The 2.3L procedure also requires discarding the driveshaft center-support bolts.

steps.title: Select the engine route and drain
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L](#/document/G1671580), [3.7L](#/document/G1671602), [5.0L](#/document/G1671614) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794942) procedure. Position the vehicle on the hoist in NEUTRAL. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L sequences explicitly disconnect battery ground before draining; the 3.7L sequence begins with its separate draining prerequisite. Complete the applicable battery and draining operations.

steps.title: Clear the exhaust and driveshaft
steps.body: Remove the engine-appropriate muffler and tailpipe; the [5.2L exhaust procedure](#/document/G1940316) is the matching route for that engine. Mark the driveshaft and pinion flange, then discard the flange bolts. Support the shaft and separate it using the specified screwdriver slot. Remove the center-support bolts and lower the shaft without over-articulating it; discard these bolts on 2.3L.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the tank
steps.body: Disconnect the filler pipe and vapor quick coupling, then move both emergency-brake cable brackets aside. Support the tank while removing its strap bolts with the specified impact tool and socket. Lower the tank's front and remove it; the 3.7L illustration specifies two-person handling. Once clear, hand-install center-support bolts and support the shaft's rear, using replacements where discard is required.

steps.title: Raise and secure the tank
steps.body: Position the tank above the rear differential and raise it into place. Lightly wire-brush the strap bolts and weld nuts, apply the specified threadlocker, and start the bolts several threads by hand before tightening. This reduces the risk of cross-threading the mountings.

steps.title: Restore brackets and tank connections
steps.body: Reinstall both emergency-brake cable brackets and tighten their nuts. Reconnect the vapor coupling through the correct engine procedure, then reconnect the filler hose and tighten its clamp.

steps.title: Reinstall the driveline and exhaust
steps.body: With an assistant, align the index marks without over-articulating the shaft. Apply threadlocker to new flange bolts and tighten in a star pattern. Clean the center-support bolts being installed, apply threadlocker and tighten as specified, using new bolts on 2.3L. Refit the muffler and tailpipe.

steps.title: Restore the pump/sender opening
steps.body: Inspect the pump/sender and tank O-ring contact surfaces. Install a new seal and carefully use the applicable lock-ring wrench to secure the unit without damaging it. Reconnect the electrical connector and fuel quick coupling, then install the access cover.

steps.title: Restore the level-sensor opening
steps.body: Complete the specified sealing-face inspection and install a new level-sensor O-ring. Fit its lock ring carefully, clean the connections and surrounding flange area, reconnect the electrical connector and install the cover. Refit the rear seat cushion and reconnect battery ground.

steps.title: Complete the fuel-system return-to-service checks
steps.body: Finish the matched fuel-pressure-release procedure after the tank, sender units and fuel connections are restored. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L has two connectors. Restore the rear cushion, cycle the ignition and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start and check for fuel leaks again.

watchFor.title: Unsupported or sharply angled driveshaft
watchFor.body: Maintain support during separation, tank removal and reassembly; the shaft must not be over-articulated.

watchFor.title: Sealing-face damage
watchFor.body: Do not polish or reshape an O-ring contact area to compensate for scratches, corrosion or bending.

notes: Use the selected engine procedure for tightening values and exhaust access; retain the 2.3L-specific center-support bolt replacement requirement.

diagnostics.finding: A pump/sender or tank O-ring contact surface is bent, scratched or corroded.
diagnostics.meaning: A new O-ring alone does not address the specified sealing-surface defect.
diagnostics.next: Replace the affected pump/sender unit or tank as directed instead of modifying the contact surface.

verification.title: Check completed assembly
verification.body: Confirm the tank straps, cable brackets, filler connection, vapor and fuel couplings, electrical connectors, covers, exhaust and rear seat are restored.

verification.title: Record critical installation results
verification.body: Record the engine procedure used, required fastener replacements, alignment of the driveshaft marks, specified tightening completion and renewal of both O-rings.

verification.title: Record the fuel-leak checks
verification.body: Confirm control-module reconnection and both the pre-start and running fuel-leak checks before releasing the vehicle.

guides.title: Diagnose B00B5 driver seat-position sensor faults
guides.summary: Follow the B00B5 fault-specific tests to distinguish driver seat-track sensor, wiring and restraints-control faults before authorizing replacement.
guides.introduction: The driver seat-track position sensor supplies seat-position information to the Restraints Control Module (RCM). The RCM monitors its circuits and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. This diagnosis uses controlled changes in circuit condition, electrical measurements and restored-connection self-tests to identify the cause.
guides.why: Most faults in this test arise from wiring or connectors. A B00B5 code describes an electrical condition, not a confirmed failed sensor. Some steps deliberately create a different fault to check the RCM’s response. Their connection, depowering and repowering sequence is essential because the work involves the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS).

when.summary: When RCM testing retrieves B00B5:11, B00B5:12, B00B5:13 or B00B5:1D.
notes: On-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 takes priority, even when B00B5 is present only in memory.

prepare.title: Use qualified SRS personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions. Use the complete depowering and repowering procedures whenever directed; ignition switching and SRS depowering are separate actions. Disconnect or reconnect components only as instructed.

prepare.title: Provide the correct diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, appropriate electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper for the sensor-circuit test. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 and the Cell 5 repair information available.

steps.title: A1: Establish whether the fault is active
steps.body: Inspect the sensor, harness and connectors, then perform the ignition-ON RCM self-test. Address U3003:16 or U3003:17 through [Test AJ](#/document/G1696405) first. Otherwise, active :11 or :1D goes to A2, :12 to A4 and :13 to A5. A continuous-memory diagnostic trouble code (CMDTC) without an on-demand B00B5 fault goes to A10.

steps.title: A2: Check the response to sensor disconnection
steps.body: For :11 or :1D, switch the ignition off, disconnect the driver seat-position sensor, switch on and repeat the RCM self-test. A change to the open-circuit code :13 leads to A8. If unchanged, :11 goes to A3 and :1D goes to A9. Follow the exact connector instructions in the [pinpoint test](#/document/G1696369).

steps.title: A3 and A4: Separate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: A3 requires ignition OFF, SRS depowering and RCM disconnection before the specified sensor-circuit resistance-to-ground measurement. Greater than 10,000 ohms leads to A9; otherwise repair the circuit and go to A11. A4 also requires driver-side-airbag inline and sensor disconnection before repowering without prove-out for the ignition-ON voltage test. Any voltage requires circuit repair and A11; no voltage leads to A9.

steps.title: A5: Check the response to an induced sensor-circuit short
steps.body: For :13, switch off and depower, disconnect the driver-side-airbag inline connector and seat-position sensor, then fit the specified fused jumper across the sensor circuits. Repower without prove-out and perform the ignition-ON self-test. A change to :11 leads to A8; no change leads to A6. Remove the jumper in either case. This connection is confined to the specified sensor circuit.

steps.title: A6 and A7: Check both circuit paths
steps.body: Switch off, depower and disconnect the RCM as directed. A6 checks the sensor signal path: resistance below 0.5 ohm leads to A7. A7 checks the ground path: resistance below 3 ohms leads to A9. Failure of either check requires circuit repair followed by A11. Use the specified connector pins in the complete test.

steps.title: A8: Confirm the sensor before replacement
steps.body: Switch off and depower. Inspect terminals, wire connections, damaged or pinched wiring, and RCM Connector Position Assurance (CPA) locks; correct concerns. Restore all required connections, repower without prove-out and repeat the ignition-ON self-test. If the original code returns, install the correct new seat-position sensor and proceed to A11. If it does not, replace nothing and continue to A10.

steps.title: A9: Confirm an RCM fault
steps.body: Repeat the depowered connector, harness and CPA-lock inspection and restore every required connection before repowering without prove-out and self-testing. If the original code returns, check Ford’s OASIS service information for an applicable Technical Service Bulletin (TSB). Follow any applicable bulletin; only if none addresses the concern does this branch direct a new RCM, followed by A11. A disappearing fault goes to A10.

steps.title: A10: Investigate an intermittent fault
steps.body: Switch off, depower and disconnect the sensor. Inspect for corrosion, loose or spread terminals, frayed connections, harness damage and faulty CPA locks. Correct concerns, reconnect everything, repower without prove-out and self-test. A returning code resumes its A2, A4 or A5 branch. If the fault cannot be recreated, install no new SRS components and proceed to A11.

steps.title: A11: Restore and test the complete restraints system
steps.body: Switch off, depower and reconnect any disconnected SRS components. Repower without prove-out, switch on and run the Restraints self-test. Check the RCM, occupant classification system module and any additional modules returned for fitted equipment. Diagnose all on-demand codes before clearing any; no on-demand codes completes this test.

watchFor.title: Deployable-device connectors are not test points
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors. Incorrect repair actions can cause accidental deployment.

watchFor.title: Connector repairs and replacement parts
watchFor.body: Use service pigtails when restraint connector terminals require repair. Confirm replacement component part numbers; similar-looking parts can be incompatible.

notes: Disconnected components can create additional codes. Restore all required connections before confirmation self-tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00B5:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground lasting more than 6 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Begin the active-fault path at A2.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00B5:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to voltage lasting more than 6 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Begin at A4 after resolving priority supply-voltage codes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00B5:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Either sensor circuit is detected open for more than 6 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Begin the controlled fault-change test at A5.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00B5:1D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Sensor-circuit current remains outside the acceptable range for more than 6 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Begin at A2; the code alone does not identify the failed part.

verification.title: Meet the release condition
verification.body: The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release. Resolve every on-demand fault found by the final Restraints self-test.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record original on-demand and memory codes, induced fault changes, circuit results, repairs and the final self-test outcome.

guides.title: Diagnose driver front impact sensor codes B1413:11 and B1413:93
guides.summary: Trace driver front impact sensor faults through connector, wiring and controlled fault-response checks before replacing restraint components.
guides.introduction: The driver front impact severity sensor supplies information used by the restraints control module (RCM) to assess a collision. The RCM monitors its electrical circuits and illuminates the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. This diagnosis separates sensor failure from wiring problems and, only after confirmation, an RCM fault.
guides.why: A stored code does not identify the failed part. The prescribed fault simulations establish whether the RCM recognizes changing circuit conditions, while connector inspections help avoid unnecessary replacement. Exact electrical isolation matters because incorrect supplemental restraint system (SRS) work can cause accidental deployment.

when.summary: When RCM testing or continuous memory records B1413:11 or B1413:93.

prepare.title: Qualified restraint-system diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use personnel qualified for pyrotechnic service, an RCM-capable scan tool, correct probe adapters, harness-measurement equipment and the prescribed fused jumper. Read the linked safety, depowering and repowering procedures first.

prepare.title: Access and electrical isolation
prepare.detail: Inspect sensor damage, mounting, orientation and harness condition. Left-hand-drive vehicles require air-cleaner removal where directed. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only at the specified steps; follow every depowering transition and omit prove-out during intermediate repowering.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is active
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test in A1 of the [pinpoint procedure](#/document/G1696385). Diagnose U3003:16 or U3003:17 first if present on-demand. Otherwise, an active B1413:11 enters A2, an active B1413:93 enters A5, and a continuous-memory-only fault enters A10.

steps.title: Follow the short-to-ground branch
steps.body: For B1413:11, A2 disconnects the sensor using the prescribed power sequence and repeats self-test. A change to B1413:93 directs sensor replacement. If the code does not change, A3–A4 check the isolated harness for a feed short to ground and a short between sensor circuits. Repair failed circuits before proceeding.

steps.title: Follow the no-operation branch
steps.body: For B1413:93, A5 first checks that the sensor and RCM connectors are seated and locked. Retest after correcting connections. If the code remains, A6–A7 isolate the components and check for unwanted feed voltage, then continuity of both feed and return circuits.

steps.title: Use the prescribed fault simulation
steps.body: If those circuits pass, follow A8 exactly for RCM reconnection and the fused jumper at the disconnected sensor harness connector. A change from B1413:93 to B1413:11 directs sensor replacement; no change leads to A9. Remove the jumper in either case. Never substitute a test directly on the sensor.

steps.title: Confirm before condemning the RCM
steps.body: A9 checks terminals, inline connectors, damaged wiring and connector-position-assurance locks, then retests with all components connected. If the original code remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before the directed RCM replacement. If it disappears, continue as an intermittent concern without replacing components.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A10 repeats the detailed connector and harness inspection under the specified depowered conditions. Repair findings, reconnect and retest. A returning code resumes its active-code branch; a fault that cannot be recreated does not justify new SRS components.

steps.title: Complete the whole-system check
steps.body: After any directed repair or replacement, follow A11 to restore connections and run the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand code before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Unsafe probing or module movement
watchFor.body: Never probe an impact sensor or deployable-device connector. Do not move the RCM while connected with the ignition on.

watchFor.title: Collision and terminal damage
watchFor.body: Crash-damaged mounting areas require restoration and replacement of the original sensor or RCM at that location. Damaged restraint connector terminals require service pigtails.

notes: Check replacement part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physical similarity does not establish compatibility. Follow the replacement procedure’s mounting torque requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1413:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground on the sensor feed.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2–A4; distinguish the sensor from harness faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1413:93 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sensor failure, feed short to voltage, or open feed or return.
diagnostics.next: Follow A5–A8; connection and circuit results determine replacement.

verification.title: Fault-free restraints result
verification.body: The final self-test must find no unresolved on-demand faults in the RCM, occupant classification system module or other fitted modules included in the test.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record initial codes, fault-response changes, repairs and final self-test results. The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before release.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seatbelt tension sensor faults B0061
guides.summary: Check buckle-mounted belt tension sensing, its wiring and occupant classification electronics to identify the correct repair.
guides.introduction: The belt tension sensor (BTS), incorporated in the front passenger buckle, sends a voltage that rises with belt tension. The occupant classification system (OCS) uses this information to recognize the possible presence of a child safety seat. Its module (OCSM) monitors the signal and reports faults to the restraints control module (RCM), which requests the airbag warning light.
guides.why: A low or high signal can result from a missing reference supply or return connection, as well as a short circuit. Testing those paths prevents a misleading code description from prompting replacement of a working buckle.

when.summary: When OCSM testing reports B0061:11, B0061:12, B0061:13, B0061:49 or B0061:64.

prepare.title: Prepare qualified electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Follow the pyrotechnic precautions and complete supplemental restraint system (SRS) power procedures. Use an OCSM-capable scan tool, meter, correct probe adapters and specified fused jumper leads. Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 support identification and repair.

prepare.title: Inspect the passenger seat area
prepare.detail: Check the buckle and sensor, cushion wiring harness, OCSM and their connectors for damage or looseness. Do not back-probe deployable connectors or probe the side airbag assembly.

steps.title: Retrieve the OCSM's own results
steps.body: Run the OCSM self-test at [A1](#/document/G1696406). Route active codes by suffix as below; continuous-memory-only faults go to A12. An accompanying RCM B00A0:09 reports an OCS concern and does not independently identify a failed buckle.

steps.title: Trace a low signal: B0061:11
steps.body: A2 disconnects buckle connector C3238 as directed and repeats self-test. If B0061:11 disappears, the test directs buckle replacement. If it remains, A3 checks for wiring shorts to ground or between circuits; A4 checks voltage-reference continuity. Repair failed checks; passing results lead to A11.

steps.title: Trace a high signal: B0061:12
steps.body: A5 depowers the SRS and isolates the side airbag, buckle and OCSM before repowering for a harness voltage check. Unexpected voltage requires circuit repair. Otherwise, A6 depowers again, disconnects the RCM and tests the ground return. A sound return leads to the sensor-output test at A10.

steps.title: Test the open-circuit response: B0061:13
steps.body: A7 uses its prescribed depowered setup, side-airbag isolation and harness-side fused jumper to induce a ground-short condition. A change from B0061:13 to B0061:11 directs buckle replacement. Without that change, A8 checks signal-wire continuity; repair an open or continue to A10.

steps.title: Separate internal and plausibility faults
steps.body: On-demand B0061:49 directs replacement of the OCS sensor assembly. B0061:64 instead follows A9: switch the ignition off and wait one minute for backup power to deplete before the specified disconnections. Check for a short between signal and voltage reference; repair it or proceed to A10.

steps.title: Measure the sensor's response to tension
steps.body: A10 depowers the SRS, reconnects the OCSM, isolates the side airbag and uses specified fused leads to supply the sensor while measuring its output. After prescribed repowering, output should vary from approximately 0.95 volt without tension to approximately 3.8 volts at full tension. Remove the leads in either case: correct response leads to A11; incorrect response directs buckle replacement.

steps.title: Confirm the classification-system decision
steps.body: A11 inspects and repairs connections before restoring the system and repeating OCSM self-test. Depower before reconnecting the side airbag if it was disconnected. If the original code persists, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins; follow any bulletin, otherwise install the specified OCS sensor. A vanished code goes to A12.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent behavior
steps.body: A12 inspects the buckle connection and harness, repairs defects and repeats self-test. A returning code follows its active branch. Otherwise, flex the harness, cycle the ignition and operate other systems sharing that harness to recreate the concern. Repair identified problems without speculative SRS replacement, then proceed to A13.

watchFor.title: Expected buckle-switch faults
watchFor.body: The tension sensor shares C3238 with the buckle switch. Disconnecting it can also produce a buckle-switch code in the RCM.

watchFor.title: Preserve calibrated assemblies
watchFor.body: Keep OCS components and connectors free of contamination. Replace OCS parts only in their supplied calibrated configuration; do not separate the assembly.

notes: Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails, and verify replacement part numbers in the Ford catalog.
Follow the exact power state for each branch. Intermediate SRS repowering excludes prove-out.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0061:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The signal is below its threshold; an open voltage-reference supply can also cause this code.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2–A4 before considering the OCSM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0061:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The signal is above its threshold; an open return circuit can also cause this code.
diagnostics.next: Check unwanted voltage and return continuity through A5–A6.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0061:64 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: With the belt unbuckled, the signal exceeds the normal maximum.
diagnostics.next: Check signal-to-reference isolation before evaluating sensor output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0061:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM detects an internal electronic fault associated with the sensor signal.
diagnostics.next: Follow the explicit OCS sensor replacement route, not an assumed buckle replacement.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Retain the active or intermittent code status, relevant circuit results and tension-response readings if A10 was performed. These establish why the selected repair follows the test.

verification.title: Restore and test all restraints
verification.body: At A13, depower before reconnecting a previously isolated side airbag, restore all SRS connections and repower as directed. Run the complete Restraints self-test. Resolve all returned on-demand faults before clearing codes; release only with the SRS operational and fault-free.

guides.title: Diagnose fog lamps that will not light or stay on continuously
guides.summary: Use the lamp's location, observed behavior and body-control fault codes to distinguish switch, wiring, lamp and output-driver concerns.
guides.introduction: The headlamp switch requests fog lighting, while the body control module (BCM) controls the lamp outputs. Front fog lamps require ignition in RUN, parking lamps on and high beams off. China-market vehicles also have a rear fog-lamp circuit, with separate diagnostic branches.
guides.why: A dark lamp may have lost its supply or ground, or the BCM may have disabled its output to protect against excessive current. Replacing a lamp or module before finding that cause can leave the concern unresolved.
searchTerms: both front fog lamps not working

when.summary: When front fog lamps, or a China-market rear fog lamp, remain off when requested or stay on continuously.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following component-replacement decisions.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, digital multimeter and required Rotunda Flex Probes. Complete Diagnostic Methods preliminary checks, including battery and charging-system checks and battery state of charge greater than 70%.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted lamps
prepare.detail: Inspect applicable bulbs and the headlamp switch. Use Wiring Diagrams Cell 86 for lamp circuits and Cell 149 for switch testing. Follow each step's ignition and connector-isolation instructions.

steps.title: Choose the branch from the actual complaint
steps.body: Retrieve BCM diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then use the symptom chart in [Fog Lamps](#/document/G1694227). If a module does not communicate, follow [Communications Network](#/document/G1813071). Route other BCM codes through [BCM diagnosis](#/document/G1692965), rather than assuming every code belongs to the fog lamps.

steps.title: Test A: both front fog lamps are inoperative
steps.body: Check low-beam operation first; incorrect operation leads to [Headlamps diagnosis](#/document/G1694228). Otherwise test the disconnected headlamp switch, then check continuity of the front fog-switch input to the BCM. Replace a failed switch or repair an open input circuit before evaluating the module.

steps.title: Test B: China rear fog lamp is inoperative
steps.body: Check the switch and rear enable-circuit continuity first. Follow B3's parking-lamp and rear-switch test setup to measure lamp supply. Missing voltage leads through the prescribed self-test/reset check, then supply-short and continuity tests. Available supply leads to the ground check; the specified successful voltage results authorize a new rear bulb.

steps.title: Test C: an individual front fog lamp is inoperative
steps.body: Test the affected side's supply, using the prescribed self-test/reset branch if absent. Check the ground when supply is available, or supply wiring for a ground short and open when it remains absent. Successful lamp-circuit results authorize a halogen bulb replacement or, for light-emitting diode (LED) equipment, replacement of the complete front lamp.

steps.title: Test D: front fog lamps stay on
steps.body: Test the headlamp switch first. With the specified BCM output connector disconnected, continued illumination identifies a supply-circuit short to voltage. If the lamps go out, check the switch-input circuit for a ground short before proceeding to BCM confirmation.

steps.title: Test E: China rear fog lamp stays on
steps.body: Test the switch, then its rear fog-input circuit for a ground short. Next isolate the rear output at the specified BCM connector. A lamp that remains illuminated requires supply-circuit repair; one that goes out leads to BCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm the BCM only after circuit checks
steps.body: At the branch's final module check, inspect all BCM connectors for corrosion, damaged or pushed-out pins, and secure latching. Repair the cause and retest. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins; otherwise continue through the vehicle identification number (VIN)-dependent BCM guided routine.

watchFor.title: A misleading unloaded reading
watchFor.body: Voltage with a lamp disconnected does not exclude excessive circuit resistance. Follow Diagnostic Methods when voltage readings and operation disagree.

watchFor.title: Another lighting function
watchFor.body: Where fitted, daytime running lamps use the fog-lamp assemblies; identify the active function when confirming continuous illumination.

diagnostics.finding: Switch codes B1046:11 or B1047:11
diagnostics.meaning: The front or rear switch-input circuit is reported shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use Test D or China-only Test E, respectively.

diagnostics.finding: Lamp-output codes B1147, B1148 or B1A79
diagnostics.meaning: These identify left front, right front or rear output concerns. The :11 suffix indicates a ground short; :15 descriptions include open or battery-short faults.
diagnostics.next: Use C or B for inoperative lamps; route :15 codes with continuous illumination to D or E.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Correct the cause, clear codes and repeat the self-test to enable the driver.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has permanently disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Address other faults and correct the overload before any BCM replacement; use the VIN-dependent routine.

verification.title: Confirm operation and record the result
verification.body: Operate the affected lamps after repair and confirm the original complaint is gone. Record final BCM self-test results and, where U1000:00 applied, successful output restoration after clearing and retesting.

guides.title: Diagnose passive-key detection and ignition-on failures
guides.summary: Separate key recognition, programming, antenna-circuit and ignition-control faults before replacing PATS components.
guides.introduction: The Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS) permits starting when it recognizes a programmed key inside the vehicle. Antennas activate the key, the radio transceiver module (RTM) receives its identity, and the body control module (BCM) exchanges authorization information with the powertrain control module (PCM). Diagnosis follows this chain to establish where recognition or authorization stops.
guides.why: A key-location problem, electrical interference and an antenna-circuit fault can produce similar complaints. Backup starting, identity comparison and circuit testing distinguish these causes before expensive components are condemned.
searchTerms: Mustang starts only with key in backup location
START STOP will not turn ignition on

when.summary: Use when key detection, key programming or switching the ignition on fails.
notes: The complaint must be present when following a replacement decision.

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, correct terminal probe adapters and wiring diagrams for the antenna circuits. Follow Diagnostic Methods for isolation and measurement practices; do not measure resistance on powered circuits.

prepare.title: Establish a sound starting point
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs and obvious wiring damage. Have the suspect key and the correct backup-key orientation available.

steps.title: Choose the entry point
steps.body: If ignition cannot be switched on, begin with Test B below. Otherwise run the BCM self-test with ignition on, record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then switch ignition off. Antenna codes lead directly to A8. If available, check that passive entry/passive start is enabled; disabling it makes backup placement necessary.

steps.title: Try the backup starting location
steps.body: With no antenna code directing the test elsewhere, place the suspect key correctly in the floor-console rear cup holder backup location and attempt starting. Follow the orientation information in the system-operation article. Successful starting leads to remote-button, location and interference checks; failure leads to identity comparison.

steps.title: Compare key identities when backup starting fails
steps.body: Record the BCM programmed transmitter identifiers, TIC_01_BCM through TIC_06_BCM. Compare them with RTM Lst_Xm_ID_Cd while pressing the suspect key's lock and unlock buttons. No match ends this branch as a key-identity mismatch without establishing a vehicle fault. If an identifier matches, recheck operation: persistent failure requires replacement and programming of that key. Restored operation follows A4's incomplete-programming conclusion.

steps.title: Check normal detection conditions
steps.body: After successful backup starting, test remote locking and unlocking. Failed buttons lead to Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis. Otherwise move the key away from interior corners, then remove possible interference from other keys, chargers, USB connections or nearby electronics. Retry after each change to identify the cause.

steps.title: Test the antenna and its wiring
steps.body: Follow A8–A11 using the exact connector tables. With no DTC, or when new keys cannot be programmed, use the center-antenna branch. Check the disconnected antenna for 1–3 ohms. If it passes, disconnect BCM C2280D and check for unwanted voltage, resistance to ground greater than 10,000 ohms, then circuit continuity below 3 ohms. Repair failed circuits. A failed antenna measurement, or passing circuit checks, directs antenna replacement.

steps.title: Resolve a persistent antenna concern
steps.body: Test operation after antenna replacement. If the concern remains, inspect every BCM connector for corrosion, damaged or displaced terminals, and proper seating and latching. Repair the underlying connection problem. Continued failure requires checking applicable Ford service bulletins, then the guided BCM routine using the vehicle identification number if no bulletin applies.

steps.title: Follow Test B for ignition-on failure
steps.body: Start with the Battery Condition Test; correct a failed battery condition and verify charging. Press START/STOP: No Key Detected sends you to Test A. Without that message, a continuously flashing ignition-mode indicator directs diagnosis of no power in ON outside PATS. Otherwise establish a scan session and self-test both BCM and PCM. Follow their DTC charts if codes exist; with none, pursue no-power-in-ON diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Detection messages while running
watchFor.body: PATS does not stop an already running vehicle. A message after the key leaves the cabin is different from failure to authorize starting.

watchFor.title: Probe damage
watchFor.body: Incorrect adapters can damage terminals and create an additional intermittent fault.

notes: BCM replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI), at least 2 programmed keys and a parameter reset. PCM replacement requires PMI and a parameter reset, but does not require reprogramming the keys.

diagnostics.meaning: These identify rear, center, passenger-door or driver-door antenna circuits respectively, not necessarily failed antennas.
diagnostics.next: Enter Test A at A8 for the indicated circuit.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10D7:05 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Key programming failed.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose other DTCs first; then retry programming. Replace and program the suspect key only if programming fails again.

diagnostics.meaning: The first identifies incomplete Configurable Engine Immobilizer setup during PMI; the second means fewer than 2 keys are programmed.
diagnostics.next: Complete the immobilizer setup or program the customer's second key, as applicable.

diagnostics.finding: B10DA:51 or P161A
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM lacks a stored PCM identity, or the PCM receives an unexpected BCM identity, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Perform the parameter reset; for B10DA:51, diagnose all other DTCs first.

diagnostics.finding: Other BCM or PCM codes
diagnostics.meaning: They require their respective module or engine diagnostic paths.
diagnostics.next: Use BCM diagnosis or the appropriate engine-control diagnosis rather than assuming a PATS component failure.

verification.title: Confirm operation at the decision point
verification.body: Repeat the affected operation after the identified correction. Confirm connector repairs remain secure and explain any demonstrated location or interference limitation.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Retain DTCs, compared key identifiers, circuit measurements and the operation result supporting the final branch decision.

guides.title: Diagnose occupant classification faults behind an airbag warning
guides.summary: Trace B00A0 occupant-classification codes through module fault messages, part identification and restraints-module configuration.
guides.introduction: The occupant classification system module (OCSM) sends information to the restraints control module (RCM) over the high-speed controller area network, HS-CAN2. The RCM checks both the messages and the module's identity. If classification information is faulty or incompatible, it stores a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and requests the airbag warning indicator. This job separates reported classification faults from incorrect components or configuration.
guides.why: An airbag warning does not identify a failed airbag. These codes concern information exchanged between modules, and some require diagnosis inside the occupant classification system first. Checking actual part numbers and configuration prevents replacing a working module simply because its messages are unacceptable to another module.

when.summary: When RCM self-test or stored fault information identifies one of the listed B00A0 occupant-classification codes.
notes: A current self-test fault and a stored intermittent fault follow different branches.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic and programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM and OCSM self-tests, Log Viewer and programmable module installation. Have access to the Ford parts catalog, vehicle As-Built configuration data, Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 and applicable service bulletins.

prepare.title: Prepare for restraint-system work
prepare.detail: Read Health and Safety Precautions before service. Disable remote start if fitted and wear the specified protection. Inspect wiring and connectors thoroughly, but disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when a procedure instructs it.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is current
steps.body: With ignition ON, run the RCM self-test. A listed B00A0 code retrieved on demand represents a fault that cannot be cleared successfully until corrected. Record the code and its suffix; that suffix determines whether to investigate classification-system faults or module identity.

steps.title: Follow reported classification faults
steps.body: For current B00A0:09, :63 or :68, retrieve OCSM codes and follow the OCSM DTC chart in the SRS diagnostic procedure. The RCM is reporting information received from the OCSM, so replacing the RCM at this stage would bypass the required diagnosis.

steps.title: Verify the classification module for identity-related codes
steps.body: For B00A0:4A or :64, use Log Viewer to retrieve and record the OCSM part number. Compare it with the parts catalog for this vehicle. If incorrect, install the correct component using the OCS sensor procedure, then proceed to the final restraints self-test.

steps.title: Verify the restraints module
steps.body: If the OCSM is correct, retrieve and record the RCM part number in the same way. An incorrect RCM requires the correct replacement and final testing. If both module identities match the catalog, proceed to configuration.

steps.title: Check RCM configuration
steps.body: Carry out programmable module installation (PMI) for the RCM, manually entering As-Built data as directed by the scan tool. Repeat the RCM self-test. If B00A0:4A remains, check Ford OASIS for an applicable technical service bulletin and follow it; without an applicable bulletin, the test directs RCM replacement.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults without speculative replacement
steps.body: If none of the listed codes returns on demand at entry, attempt to reproduce the fault by flexing the harness and cycling ignition as directed. Do not install new SRS components merely because a stored code exists. Continue to the final restraints self-test after this investigation.

watchFor.title: Similar-looking modules
watchFor.body: Physical similarity does not establish compatibility. Verify the catalog part number before installation.

watchFor.title: Premature clearing
watchFor.body: Do not clear codes while unresolved SRS faults remain; a warning disappearing temporarily is not completion.

notes: The configuration branch specifically rechecks B00A0:4A. Final testing must still address every other on-demand restraint code.

diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM reports an occupant classification fault; :68 identifies fault-event information.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve OCSM codes for the next diagnostic direction.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00A0:63 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM has received at least 8 invalid states from the OCSM.
diagnostics.next: Follow the OCSM DTC chart.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00A0:4A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM is detected but is not configured.
diagnostics.next: Verify both module identities before carrying out RCM PMI.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00A0:64 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Received upper or lower data limits differ from those stored by the RCM.
diagnostics.next: Follow the part-number and configuration branch.

verification.title: Run the complete restraints self-test
verification.body: Cycle ignition OFF, then ON, and select Restraints self-test. Resolve all on-demand codes from the RCM, OCSM and any other fitted module included in that test before clearing codes. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and fault-free.

verification.title: Retain the identification results
verification.body: Record the retrieved OCSM and RCM part numbers when checked, their catalog comparison, and the final self-test result.

guides.title: Diagnose a horn that will not sound or stays on
guides.summary: Separate horn power, relay control and steering-wheel switch faults using the correct symptom-based electrical tests.
guides.introduction: Pressing the driver airbag closes spring-separated horn-switch contacts. That sends a ground signal through the clockspring to the body control module (BCM). The BCM grounds the horn relay coil, and the relay supplies voltage to the horn. Diagnosis follows this chain to distinguish a silent horn from a circuit that remains switched on.
guides.why: The horn, its power circuit and its switch input can fail independently. Scan-tool commands separate the output side from the driver's switch, while a specified test lamp checks circuits under load. A trouble code identifies a circuit condition; it does not prove that the named component needs replacement.

when.summary: When the horn will not sound, sounds continuously, or has a related BCM code requiring diagnosis.
notes: Confirm the complaint is currently present before following component-replacement branches.

prepare.title: Electrical testing equipment
prepare.detail: Use Wiring Diagrams Cell 44, a diagnostic scan tool with BCM active commands and parameter identification (PID) data, a digital multimeter, a known-good relay and fused jumpers. Use the Rotunda SGT27000 test lamp or a 250–300mA incandescent test lamp with Rotunda Flex Probes; never insert the lamp probe directly into a connector.

prepare.title: Power and restraint-system prerequisites
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Steering-wheel isolation requires driver-airbag removal: follow the complete linked airbag procedure and its supplemental restraint system precautions. Test only the specified horn circuits, never airbag igniter terminals.

steps.title: Select the symptom branch
steps.body: Retrieve BCM codes and use [Pinpoint Test A for an inoperative horn or Test B for a horn that stays on](#/document/G1688198). For an inoperative horn, first verify battery junction box fuse 21 (20A). A failed fuse requires investigation of the short, not repeated replacement.

steps.title: For a silent horn, command the output
steps.body: With ignition on, command BCM HORN_RELAY on and off. If the horn sounds, move to switch-input testing at A9. If not, switch ignition off and substitute a known-good relay. Normal operation identifies the relay for replacement; otherwise A3 checks both relay supply sockets for greater than 11 volts.

steps.title: Separate horn, power and relay-control faults
steps.body: A4 substitutes the specified lamp at the disconnected horn and uses a momentary fused relay-socket jumper. If it lights, A5 reinstalls the relay and repeats the scan-tool command: illumination now directs horn replacement. No illumination directs relay-control short-to-voltage and continuity checks at A6–A7. If A4 never lights, A8 repeats the load test using chassis ground: illumination identifies the horn ground circuit; darkness identifies the power-supply circuit.

steps.title: Check the switch input when commanded operation works
steps.body: At A9, switch ignition off and disconnect the specified BCM connector. Resistance below 3 ohms while pressing the horn sends diagnosis to the BCM connector check. Otherwise follow driver-airbag removal, then A10's specified horn-switch jumper test. If the horn sounds, replace the driver airbag assembly containing the horn switch. Remove the jumper after testing.

steps.title: Trace an open steering-wheel path
steps.body: If A10 fails, A11–A13 separate switch-ground wiring, clockspring and steering-wheel harness faults. A14 checks the signal path toward the BCM; A15 isolates the wheel harness. Follow the exact connector and jumper sequence before choosing wiring repair, steering-wheel replacement or clockspring replacement. If A15 directs a new clockspring and the horn remains inoperative after retesting, the next instruction is steering column control module (SCCM) replacement.

steps.title: For a continuously sounding horn, isolate relay power
steps.body: B1 replaces the horn with the specified lamp and removes the relay. A lamp that stays lit identifies a short to voltage in the horn supply circuit. Otherwise try a known-good relay at B2. Replace the relay if operation returns to normal; if not, reinstall the original relay before continuing.

steps.title: Separate an unwanted command from a grounded control circuit
steps.body: Monitor HORN_SW at B3. If it reads OFF, B4 disconnects the BCM relay-control connector: a lit lamp identifies a control-circuit short to ground; darkness leads to the BCM check. If HORN_SW does not read OFF, B5 isolates the switch input. Continued illumination leads to the BCM check; otherwise B6 isolates the input wiring at the SCCM and identifies a short to ground if illumination returns.

steps.title: Isolate a stuck switch or steering-wheel circuit
steps.body: B7 requires driver-airbag removal and clockspring-connector isolation. Illumination directs clockspring replacement, followed by retesting and SCCM replacement only if the lamp remains lit. If B7's lamp is off, B8 reconnects the wheel wiring: illumination directs steering-wheel replacement; no illumination directs replacement of the driver airbag containing the horn switch.

steps.title: Complete the BCM branch only when directed
steps.body: At A16 or B9, inspect BCM connectors. Renew corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins. Restore the relay where removed, reconnect the horn and latch the connectors securely. Retest. If the concern persists, check applicable Ford service articles and follow any matching instructions before the branch directs BCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Incorrect test loading
watchFor.body: Use the specified lamp and adapters. An unsuitable probe can damage terminals and create another fault.

watchFor.title: A successful connector repair
watchFor.body: If reconnecting restores operation, find and correct the underlying pin or connector problem.

notes: BCM repair validation code generation requires the vehicle identification number and single-step test view.
Use the complete component procedure for any replacement reached by diagnosis, including airbag, clockspring and steering-wheel work.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C55:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects voltage on the relay-control circuit and disables the horn.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A; do not assume the horn itself has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C55:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The relay-control circuit is open or shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A if the horn is silent and Test B if it stays on.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1323:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects a horn-signal circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B to isolate wiring, switch and steering-wheel paths.

verification.title: Restore and operate
verification.body: Remove diagnostic jumpers, restore the relay and connections, and confirm normal horn operation. Perform the explicit retest before any conditional SCCM replacement.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Record the original symptom, BCM codes, commanded-output or switch-input result, decisive lamp test and final operating result.

guides.title: Diagnose interior lamps that stay on, fail to light or lose ambient colors
guides.summary: Separate door-input, lamp-circuit, battery-saver and ambient-lighting faults before deciding which component needs repair.
guides.introduction: Courtesy lamps illuminate entry and exit, while demand lamps light specific areas such as the vanity mirrors and luggage compartment. The body control module (BCM) controls their supplies and battery-saving functions. Optional ambient lighting uses light-emitting diodes (LEDs), settings from the instrument panel cluster (IPC), and Body Control Module B (BCMB).
guides.why: A dark lamp can result from a missing input, damaged wiring or protective output shutdown. A lamp that stays on can likewise have several causes. Establishing the circuit behavior prevents unnecessary lamp, latch or module replacement.
searchTerms: interior lights do not come on when door opens

when.summary: When interior or pony projection lamps malfunction, ambient colors fail, or the battery saver does not switch lamps off.
notes: Ambient-lighting tests apply only when fitted. Memory-seat vehicles have an additional door-module branch.
The complaint must be present during testing before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Inspect previous repairs, fuses, harness damage, bulbs and lamp damage.

prepare.title: Provide electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting module data, active commands and network tests, a digital multimeter, specified flex probes and fused jumper wires. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 89 and 117 available.

prepare.title: Protect circuits and terminals
prepare.detail: Follow each test's ignition and connector-disconnection sequence. Isolate resistance tests from voltage; disconnect the battery for ground-circuit resistance measurements. Use jumpers only where directed and remove them afterward.

steps.title: 1. Match the complaint and collect fault information
steps.body: Use the symptom chart in [Interior Lighting diagnosis](#/document/G1694266) to select the relevant branch. Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) across the network and address circuit faults first. A module that does not communicate needs communications diagnosis, including its fuse, wiring and connections, before lighting diagnosis can continue.

steps.title: 2. Tests A and D: establish what the doors are reporting
steps.body: For lamps that stay dark with a door open, Test A disconnects the suspect latch: illumination points to the latch; otherwise check the input for a short to ground. For all courtesy lamps staying on, Test D compares door positions with scan-tool parameter identifications (PIDs). Directed fused-jumper checks separate latch, ground and input-wire faults. Memory-seat vehicles additionally use the driver or passenger door module for the latch return. Correct door data redirects diagnosis to Test B or C.

steps.title: 3. Test B: isolate overhead courtesy-lamp faults
steps.body: Close the doors and press LOCK on the remote keyless entry transmitter. If the lamps switch off normally, a single failed overhead lamp takes the bulb-first branch; continued failure calls for the overhead console. Both lamps failing requires supply and ground checks. Lamps remaining on require the short-to-voltage branch before BCM assessment.

steps.title: 4. Test C: isolate pony projection-lamp faults
steps.body: Inspect the exterior mirrors for damage and perform the closed-door lock check. A single failed lamp requires the scan-tool Courtesy Puddle Step Lamps command and supply/ground tests. Both lamps failing requires open-circuit and short-to-ground checks. Lamps still illuminated with the BCM output disconnected indicate a short to voltage. Replace a lamp only when its branch supports that decision.

steps.title: 5. Tests E and F: separate local demand-lamp and luggage-lamp faults
steps.body: Test E compares vanity, map, console-bin and glove-compartment lamps. All failing points toward the shared supply; an individual failure requires its supply and ground checks before replacing the lamp, visor or overhead console. Test F checks luggage-lamp operation and the demand supply. For a continuously lit luggage lamp, disconnecting its latch separates a grounded circuit from a latch fault. For a dark lamp, voltage, socket and fused-jumper checks separate supply, socket, latch and ground faults.

steps.title: 6. Test G: investigate battery-saver failure
steps.body: Normal shutoff occurs after 10 minutes for courtesy lamps and 30 minutes for demand lamps; factory and transport modes differ. Door, ignition and remote activity can restart the timer. With ignition off and BCM C2280C disconnected, a demand lamp that still switches on indicates a short to voltage. Otherwise proceed to BCM connection checks.

steps.title: 7. Test H: investigate complete ambient-lighting loss
steps.body: Under nighttime ambient-light conditions, check whether other IPC message-center settings can be changed and saved. Failure redirects diagnosis to instrumentation. If those settings work, follow the specified ambient return-circuit voltage and continuity checks, then the BCMB connection and operation checks.

steps.title: 8. Test I: investigate missing ambient color combinations
steps.body: With ignition and parking lamps on under nighttime conditions, compare all lighting locations while changing colors. If all are affected, test IPC/BCMB network communication and check BCMB memory for U0155:87, which redirects to BCMB diagnosis. An IPC-only fault takes the IPC branch; other affected LEDs require zone color-output circuit checks before BCMB assessment.

steps.title: 9. Test J: investigate one ambient-lighting location
steps.body: Select the scuff plate, interior door handle, footwell or cup-holder branch. With the specified connectors disconnected, test its color feeds and common return. Passing continuity checks directs replacement of that LED; failing checks requires wiring repair. An IPC lighting fault follows IPC connector inspection and its guided diagnostic route.

steps.title: 10. Resolve connections before module decisions
steps.body: At a module-check endpoint, inspect for corrosion, bent or pushed-out pins and poor terminal fit. Replace damaged connectors or terminals, clean module pins and latch connectors securely. Retest, then check applicable Ford service information if the fault remains. BCM and IPC endpoints require the vehicle identification number for their guided routines; BCMB and door-module replacement follows only the applicable test outcome.

watchFor.title: Normal delays mistaken for faults
watchFor.body: Illuminated-entry delays and timer restarts can keep lamps on legitimately. Confirm the relevant operating conditions before diagnosing continuous illumination.

watchFor.title: Misleading voltage readings
watchFor.body: Voltage measured with a lamp disconnected does not establish that its wiring can carry the operating load. Follow the diagnostic methods for suspected resistance.

notes: Ambient zone 1 serves footwells, door handles and cup holders; zone 3 serves scuff plates. Both share the BCMB-controlled return.
Use the body-style-specific procedure if luggage-compartment latch replacement is indicated.

diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a driver or passenger door-ajar circuit fault; this does not establish latch failure.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for failure to illuminate or Test D for continuous illumination.

diagnostics.finding: B1313 or B12C2 output faults
diagnostics.meaning: These concern interior or pony projection outputs respectively. Suffix :11 indicates short to ground; :15 indicates short to battery or open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B or C and establish the wiring condition.

diagnostics.finding: BCMB ambient red, green or blue output DTCs
diagnostics.meaning: The code identifies an affected color and zone, with separate short-to-ground and short-to-battery/open distinctions.
diagnostics.next: Use Test I and its exact code and circuit tables. Route other module DTCs to that module's diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Repair the underlying fault first, clear DTCs and repeat the self-test. BCM recovery also requires the prescribed ignition cycle.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive-current events have permanently disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Correct the load fault before the BCM guided routine or directed BCMB replacement; clearing codes cannot restore that output.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating condition
verification.body: Confirm the affected lamps now respond correctly to door position, demand switches, locking or ambient-color selection. Check battery-saver behavior without restarting its timer.

verification.title: Record the electrical result
verification.body: Record the original codes, decisive PID or circuit findings, repair and final self-test result. Clear codes after correcting their causes and confirm the complaint does not recur.
