guides.title: Diagnose autolamps that do not switch on or stay on continuously
guides.summary: Separate headlamp faults, light-sensor circuit faults and body control module problems using the appropriate autolamp pinpoint test.
guides.introduction: Autolamps use a light sensor, headlamp switch and body control module (BCM) to control exterior lighting automatically. They also retain lighting for a selected delay after ignition shutdown. Diagnosis checks whether the BCM receives a usable light signal and whether circuit protection has disabled an output.
guides.why: A sensor code does not prove the sensor has failed. Wiring faults and poor terminals can produce the same complaint, while excessive current can temporarily or permanently disable a BCM output. Correcting the underlying circuit fault protects any replacement module.
searchTerms: automatic headlights will not turn on

when.summary: Test when automatic lighting fails to operate or remains on beyond its configured shutdown delay.
notes: The complaint must be present during testing before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish reliable electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Review repairs and related codes; inspect fuses, wiring, the headlamp switch and light sensor.

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, required Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 85. Follow each ignition and connector-disconnection state; resistance measurements require an isolated, unpowered circuit.

prepare.title: Identify the sensor variant
prepare.detail: Electronic manual temperature control (EMTC) uses autolamp and rain sensor connector C287. Dual automatic temperature control (DATC) uses sunload sensor connector C286. Select that branch throughout.

steps.title: Choose the complaint path
steps.body: For inoperative autolamps, Pinpoint Test A starts by switching the headlamps manually on and off. If this fails, follow headlamp diagnosis first. For continuously illuminated autolamps, Pinpoint Test B begins with the BCM self-test: B1A85:11 routes to B3, B1A85:13 to B6, and no codes to B2.

steps.title: Check the sensor input for Test A or the no-code branch
steps.body: At A2 or B2, switch ignition off and disconnect the appropriate sensor. Switch ignition on, select AUTOLAMPS and measure sensor connector pin 2 to ground. Approximately 5 volts directs replacement of the matching sensor through the Light Sensor procedure. Otherwise, continue to A3 or B11 for BCM connector checks.

steps.title: Trace B1A85:11 through B3–B5
steps.body: This code indicates a light-input short to ground. With the sensor disconnected, approximately 5 volts at pin 2 directs sensor replacement. If absent, perform the self-test, clear codes, repeat the self-test and remeasure as B4 directs. If voltage remains incorrect, switch ignition off and disconnect BCM C2280B. Resistance from sensor pin 2 to ground greater than 10,000 ohms leads to B11; otherwise repair the circuit.

steps.title: Trace B1A85:13 through B6–B10
steps.body: This code covers an open input or short to voltage. If pin 2 to ground measures approximately 5 volts, measure between sensor pins 2 and 4: approximately 5 volts directs sensor replacement. Otherwise, B8 checks pin 4 to BCM C2280B pin 22 with ignition off and the BCM disconnected. If the initial voltage was incorrect, B9 checks for unwanted voltage with the BCM disconnected; any voltage requires circuit repair. With none present, B10 checks sensor pin 2 to BCM pin 24. Each continuity check must be less than 3 ohms; failure requires wiring repair, while a pass leads to B11.

steps.title: Inspect the BCM connections before condemning it
steps.body: At A3 or B11, inspect all BCM connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; renew damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect and latch everything, then operate the system. If the concern persists, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin. With none applicable, the test directs BCM replacement.

steps.title: Complete the fault-specific recovery
steps.body: After circuit repair, apply the protection-code decisions below. If no codes are present, test normal operation. If reconnection resolved the complaint, address the underlying terminal or connector defect rather than stopping at temporary recovery.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during measurement
watchFor.body: Do not force probes into connectors or apply substitute power or ground to module-controlled circuits without a directed test.

watchFor.title: Normal delayed lighting
watchFor.body: Allow the configured autolamp shutdown delay before identifying a continuous-on fault.

notes: B1A85:11 can occur in continuous memory and on-demand testing; B1A85:13 is an on-demand code.
Use the complete pinpoint procedure for connector states and measurements; sensor connector identities depend on climate-control equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Address other codes and correct the cause, then clear codes and obtain a successful self-test to re-enable the driver.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has permanently disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Correct the overload and address other codes before following the bulletin check and BCM replacement branch.

diagnostics.finding: A module does not communicate
diagnostics.meaning: Fuse, wiring, connector or module faults can prevent scan-tool access.
diagnostics.next: Follow Communications Network diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Other BCM codes are present
diagnostics.meaning: They require their own diagnostic path.
diagnostics.next: Use the BCM diagnostic chart rather than assuming a light-sensor failure.

verification.title: Confirm lighting operation
verification.body: Reconnect the system and verify normal operation, including the original complaint and configured shutdown delay.

verification.title: Record the electrical outcome
verification.body: Retain initial codes, circuit readings, repairs and final self-test results. Where U1000:00 occurred, confirm the successful self-test restored output operation.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger airbag OFF indicator faults: B00D5:11, B00D5:12 and B00D5:13
guides.summary: Separate passenger-airbag indicator wiring, power-supply and indicator faults from a confirmed restraints-control-module fault.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) briefly lights the passenger airbag deactivation (PAD) indicator to demonstrate that it works. It also monitors the indicator's power supply and light-emitting diode (LED) circuit. A detected fault stores a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and requests the main airbag warning light. This test identifies the affected circuit or component.
guides.why: Most faults here involve wiring or connectors. Disconnecting components changes what the RCM detects, so connector states and power sequences are part of the diagnosis. Departing from the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) procedure can cause accidental deployment and serious injury.

when.summary: Use when an RCM self-test or continuous-memory record contains B00D5:11, B00D5:12 or B00D5:13.
notes: An on-demand fault and a memory-only intermittent fault require different paths.

prepare.title: Qualified SRS work
prepare.detail: Use personnel qualified for pyrotechnic-system service. Read the linked safety, depowering and repowering procedures before testing; disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the pinpoint step directs.

prepare.title: Equipment and initial inspection
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of RCM and Restraints self-tests, a multimeter, correct probe adapters and the prescribed fused jumper. Obtain the specified wiring diagrams, inspect wiring and connectors, and verify BCM fuse 19 (5A). BCM means body control module.

steps.title: 1. Establish whether the fault is active
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test with ignition on. Route an on-demand B00D5:11 to A2, B00D5:12 to A7 and B00D5:13 to A4. An active fault cannot be cleared until corrected. A continuous-memory-only code goes to the intermittent checks in A10.

steps.title: 2. Trace B00D5:11 to ground
steps.body: Follow A2–A3: switch ignition off, disconnect the PAD indicator and test its designated control circuit. Acceptable resistance leads to confirmation at A9. Low resistance requires SRS depowering before disconnecting the RCM and repeating the measurement. A short that remains with the RCM isolated directs circuit repair.

steps.title: 3. Trace B00D5:13 through continuity and supply
steps.body: Depower and disconnect the RCM and indicator as A4 specifies, then test control-wire continuity. If it passes, repower without proving out the SRS and check indicator ignition supply. Resolve fuse or supply faults first. Only after those checks pass, perform A6's prescribed fused-jumper indicator test. Illumination leads to A9; failure directs a new indicator. Remove the jumper in either case.

steps.title: 4. Trace B00D5:12 to voltage
steps.body: A7 depowers and isolates the RCM and indicator, then repowers without prove-out for the voltage check. Voltage on the isolated control wire directs wiring repair. If absent, follow A8's depower/reconnect/repower sequence, leaving the indicator disconnected. A change from B00D5:12 to B00D5:13 shows the RCM recognizes the induced open and directs indicator replacement; otherwise continue to A9.

steps.title: 5. Confirm before condemning the RCM
steps.body: At A9, depower and inspect wiring, terminals and connector-position-assurance locks. Correct defects and reconnect all SRS components before repowering without prove-out and repeating the self-test. If the original code remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before directed RCM replacement. If it disappears, continue as intermittent without installing components.

steps.title: 6. Investigate an intermittent connection
steps.body: Follow A10's connector and harness inspection. If the self-test remains clear, attempt to reproduce the fault by flexing the harness, cycling ignition and operating other systems sharing that harness. A returning on-demand code re-enters its corresponding branch; memory alone does not justify replacement.

steps.title: 7. Finish with the full restraints check
steps.body: Follow A11 to reconnect components and repower if previously directed, without performing prove-out at that stage. Run the Restraints self-test, which retrieves results from both the RCM and occupant classification system module (OCSM). Resolve any remaining on-demand faults before completion.

watchFor.title: Unsafe probing
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors. The prescribed jumper test concerns the indicator circuit only.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails when restraint connector terminals require repair; do not repair the terminals themselves.

notes: Confirm replacement SRS part numbers in the Ford parts catalog. A physically similar component may be incompatible.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00D5:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground on the indicator LED circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3, followed by the directed repair or A9 confirmation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00D5:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to voltage on the indicator LED circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A7–A8 to distinguish harness voltage from indicator or RCM concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00D5:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Either the LED control circuit or the indicator's ignition supply may be open.
diagnostics.next: Use A4–A6; do not assume the indicator itself has failed.

verification.title: Confirm the complete system is fault-free
verification.body: Do not clear codes until all faults are resolved. Release requires a fully operational SRS and no RCM or OCSM on-demand faults at the final Restraints self-test.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the original code, whether it was active or memory-only, any deliberate fault change during A8 and the final self-test results.

procedures.purpose: Complete B00D5:11/:12/:13 indicator diagnosis, including A1–A11 circuit isolation and final restraints checks.

guides.title: Diagnose U0253:00: restraints module loses APIM communication
guides.summary: Trace missing APIM messages through network, voltage-code and audio-module checks before deciding whether APIM or restraints-module replacement is justified.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors restraint inputs and controls deployment when required. In this diagnostic path, it also expects information from the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) over the high-speed Controller Area Network (HS-CAN2). Diagnostic trouble code (DTC) U0253:00 records a missing expected APIM message. The investigation checks whether the loss is temporary, associated with voltage faults or also reported by the audio control module (ACM).
guides.why: An APIM that fails the network test needs a different investigation from one that communicates but whose messages are not reaching the RCM as expected. Checking voltage codes before comparing receiving modules avoids interpreting a communication symptom as proof of an internal module failure.
searchTerms: accessory protocol interface module communication fault

when.summary: When the RCM records U0253:00 because an expected APIM message is missing.
notes: Begin with a thorough wiring and connector inspection; a stored communication code alone does not justify replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare the scan-tool functions
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with network testing, RCM and APIM self-tests, DTC clearing and all-module self-tests. Preserve recorded results before clearing codes.

prepare.title: Keep the powered restraints module undisturbed
prepare.detail: Never handle, move or change the RCM's original horizontal mounting position while it is connected and ignition is on; accidental deployment can cause serious injury.

prepare.title: Plan any follow-on service separately
prepare.detail: Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when instructed. Have access to applicable Ford service articles and the complete replacement procedure if the diagnostic branch reaches that endpoint.

steps.title: Establish APIM network availability
steps.body: With ignition on, run a network test. If the APIM does not pass, follow Communications Network diagnosis. If it passes, continue to the RCM retest rather than treating network availability as proof that the original message-loss condition has cleared.

steps.title: Clear and repeat the RCM self-test
steps.body: With ignition on, perform the RCM self-test and preserve its results. Clear the RCM DTCs, wait 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. If U0253:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at this time; network traffic or an intermittent fault may have produced the earlier code.

steps.title: Follow the RCM voltage-code diversion when needed
steps.body: If U0253:00 returns, inspect the recorded RCM results for U3003:16 or U3003:17. Either code directs diagnosis to Pinpoint Test AU. If neither is recorded, proceed to the APIM self-test.

steps.title: Check APIM voltage-related findings
steps.body: Perform the APIM self-test and check for U3003:16 or U3003:17. If either is present, use the appropriate battery-voltage diagnostic procedure in Group 415. Without those codes, continue to the cross-module comparison.

steps.title: Compare the ACM report and check service articles
steps.body: With ignition on, perform all-module self-tests and determine whether the ACM also stores U0253:00. If it does, the diagnostic endpoint is APIM replacement through the appropriate Group 415 procedure. If it does not, the endpoint is RCM replacement. Before either action, check all applicable Ford service articles; follow a matching article instead of continuing this replacement branch.

watchFor.title: Do not broaden the comparison rule
watchFor.body: The final decision specifically asks whether the ACM records U0253:00. A different module's unrelated communication code does not satisfy that condition.

watchFor.title: Do not disturb connectors to see what changes
watchFor.body: Unscheduled SRS disconnection can create misleading diagnostic results. Keep the scan-test sequence intact.

notes: Verify replacement SRS part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physically similar components from other vehicles may be incompatible.
The diagnostic endpoint identifies the next service procedure. It does not provide removal, installation or system-restoration instructions.

diagnostics.finding: APIM fails the network test
diagnostics.meaning: Communication availability must be diagnosed before evaluating a persistent missing-message report.
diagnostics.next: Use the Communications Network route identified in the complete test.

diagnostics.finding: U0253:00 returns and the ACM also reports it
diagnostics.meaning: After the preceding checks, the prescribed decision directs attention to the APIM.
diagnostics.next: Check applicable service articles, then follow their instructions or the directed APIM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: U0253:00 returns without the ACM reporting it
diagnostics.meaning: After the preceding checks, the prescribed decision directs attention to the RCM.
diagnostics.next: Check applicable service articles before following the RCM replacement procedure.

verification.title: Confirm a fault-free restraint system
verification.body: After any directed repair, repeat the relevant diagnostic checks. Release the vehicle only when the SRS is fully operational and free of faults.

verification.title: Record the branch-defining results
verification.body: Retain APIM network status, the RCM result after the 10-second wait, both modules' voltage-code findings and whether the ACM recorded U0253:00.

procedures.purpose: Complete U0253:00 diagnosis across the listed engines, including network, voltage-code, ACM comparison and service-article branches.

guides.title: Diagnose U0140:00: the restraints module has lost BCM communication
guides.summary: Determine whether a missing body-control message reflects a network interruption, voltage fault or module fault.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) uses messages from the body control module (BCM) carried on high-speed Controller Area Network (HS-CAN2). It stores diagnostic trouble code (DTC) U0140:00 when an expected message does not arrive. This test checks communication and supporting evidence before choosing a module-replacement path.
guides.why: A missing message does not prove that its sender has failed. Network traffic, intermittent communication and supply-voltage faults must be considered first. Comparing the RCM’s result with other modules helps distinguish a concern shared by several receivers from one reported only by the RCM.
searchTerms: restraints module lost communication with BCM

when.summary: Use when the RCM reports U0140:00 for a missing BCM message.
notes: A BCM that fails the initial network test requires network diagnosis before this pinpoint path continues.

prepare.title: Provide network and module testing
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of a network test, RCM and BCM self-tests, all-module self-tests, and code recording and clearing.

prepare.title: Keep restraint components secure
prepare.detail: Review the pyrotechnic precautions. Do not move or change the RCM’s mounting position while it is connected with ignition on. Pyrotechnic service requires qualified personnel.

prepare.title: Inspect before testing
prepare.detail: Check for wiring and connector concerns. Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when the applicable procedure directs.

steps.title: Establish whether the BCM communicates
steps.body: With ignition on, run the network test. If the BCM fails, follow Communications Network diagnosis for its lack of communication. If it passes, proceed to the RCM’s stored fault. A successful network test establishes current communication, not that every expected message always arrives.

steps.title: Check whether the missing-message code returns
steps.body: Perform the RCM self-test and retain its results. Clear the RCM codes, wait 10 seconds, then repeat the self-test. If U0140:00 does not return, operation is correct at that time; heavy network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the earlier code.

steps.title: Follow the voltage-fault priorities
steps.body: If U0140:00 returns, inspect the recorded RCM results for U3003:16 or U3003:17 and follow Test AJ if present. Otherwise run the BCM self-test. The same codes in the BCM require BCM diagnosis before proceeding to the communication comparison.

steps.title: Compare reports from other receivers
steps.body: With ignition on, perform self-tests for all modules. Check specifically whether U0140:00 is set in the anti-lock braking system (ABS) module or instrument panel cluster (IPC). Their results determine the final branch; do not select a replacement from the RCM code alone.

steps.title: Apply the final branch and bulletin check
steps.body: If the ABS module or IPC also reports U0140:00, the branch points toward BCM replacement. If neither does, it points toward RCM replacement. In either case, first check Ford’s service information system for applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin instead; otherwise carry out the directed replacement through its complete service procedure.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears
watchFor.body: A successful repeat test establishes current operation; it does not identify a defective module or prove that an intermittent concern can never return.

watchFor.title: Incorrect replacement parts
watchFor.body: Verify the specified Ford part number before installation. Similar-looking SRS modules may be incompatible.

notes: Keep the network-test result separate from the individual module self-test results.

diagnostics.finding: BCM fails the network test
diagnostics.meaning: Basic communication with the BCM has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Leave this branch for Communications Network diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: U0140:00 returns after clearing and waiting
diagnostics.meaning: The missing-message concern remains reproducible.
diagnostics.next: Check voltage-related codes, then compare the ABS and IPC results.

verification.title: Record the decisive evidence
verification.body: Retain the initial and repeat RCM results, BCM self-test and ABS/IPC comparison supporting the selected branch.

verification.title: Meet the release condition
verification.body: Complete the checks required by any resulting repair procedure. Release requires a fully operational, fault-free SRS.

procedures.purpose: Complete U0140:00 missing-BCM-message diagnosis reported by the RCM.

BCM diagnosis when its self-test records voltage-related faults.

guides.title: Diagnose a parking brake that will not hold or release
guides.summary: Isolate the control, front cable, rear cables and wheel-end brakes to identify why the parking brake fails to hold or stays applied.
guides.introduction: Pulling the parking-brake handle tensions a front cable and equalizer, which pulls both rear cables and operates the rear brake actuators. Releasing the handle lets the mechanism return. This diagnosis follows that mechanical chain, using controlled disconnections to locate a restriction or lost movement before choosing a repair.
guides.why: A stiff handle, weak holding action and dragging rear wheel can arise at different points in the same linkage. Separating the cable sections shows which part is preventing movement; adjustment alone does not establish that the cables and control work correctly.
searchTerms: parking brake handle will not move
rear wheels drag after parking brake released
red brake warning light stays on

when.summary: Investigate changed handle feel, failure to hold on an incline, or dragging after the parking brake is released.
notes: Verify the complaint while it is present before using a replacement decision.

prepare.title: Provide access and assistance
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist and the capability to work safely at the equalizer and rear calipers. Have an assistant apply and release the handle while you observe cable and actuator movement.

prepare.title: Have the matching repair information ready
prepare.detail: Obtain brake thickness specifications and the applicable control, cable, caliper and adjustment procedures. Review previous repairs that could explain disconnected or incorrectly installed components.

steps.title: 1. Verify and inspect
steps.body: With the vehicle on the hoist and the control fully released, check operation and look for mechanical damage. Correct an obvious cause. Otherwise, choose Test A for failure to apply or hold, or Test B for failure to release.

steps.title: 2. Follow Test A when the handle moves
steps.body: Have the assistant operate the handle while inspecting the control, front cable, rear cables, equalizer and caliper actuators. Reconnect or replace damaged or disconnected components, test operation and adjust the cables. If everything is connected and undamaged, check rear pad and disc thickness. Only when those are within specification does this branch direct rear-caliper replacement.

steps.title: 3. Follow Test A when the handle will not move
steps.body: Disconnect the front cable from the rear equalizer and retry the handle. Continued immobility directs control/front-cable assembly replacement as necessary. If the handle now moves, disconnect the affected rear cable at its caliper. Hold the conduit and slide the inner cable: binding directs cable replacement; free movement directs inspection and repair of the affected rear brake components, followed by adjustment.

steps.title: 4. Begin Test B at the control
steps.body: Apply and release the handle. If it will not fully release, follow the control/front-cable replacement branch. If it releases, disconnect the front cable from the equalizer and check rear-wheel rotation. Wheels that now turn freely identify the control/front-cable assembly as the directed repair.

steps.title: 5. Continue Test B at the rear cables
steps.body: If drag remains, disconnect the rear cable at each affected caliper. A wheel that becomes free directs replacement of that side's rear cable. If the wheel still does not turn freely, this branch directs parking-brake cable adjustment; it does not independently establish a failed caliper.

steps.title: 6. Complete the selected repair
steps.body: Follow the corresponding removal and installation procedure, including the adjustment directed by the diagnostic branch. Test normal operation afterward rather than judging success only by a change in handle feel.

watchFor.title: Movement that stops partway along the linkage
watchFor.body: A moving handle does not prove both rear cables and actuators move. Observe the whole linkage with the assistant.

watchFor.title: Drag despite a released handle
watchFor.body: Use the staged disconnection checks to locate what remains applied instead of assuming the control has released the wheel brakes.

diagnostics.finding: Red brake warning indicator remains illuminated
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include incomplete parking-brake release, low brake fluid, wiring or a master-cylinder concern.
diagnostics.next: Follow Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes diagnosis; the lamp alone does not identify a cable fault.

verification.title: Confirm holding and release
verification.body: Check normal apply/hold operation and full release, including rear-wheel freedom on the hoist with the control released.

verification.title: Record the isolation result
verification.body: Record which disconnection changed handle movement or wheel drag, the affected side and the result after repair and any directed adjustment.

procedures.purpose: Parking-brake preliminary inspection, symptom routing, Test A for failure to hold and Test B for failure to release.
Diagnostic prerequisites, including confirming a present complaint and reviewing previous repairs.

guides.title: Replace a convertible rear quarter speaker with SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Access and replace the rear quarter speaker, then restore the loadspace trim without trapping the convertible flap or twisting the seatbelts.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter speaker converts the audio system's electrical signal into sound beside the rear seating area. It sits behind the convertible loadspace trim, so reaching it requires more work than removing the speaker itself. The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures use the same removal sequence and speaker-bolt torque.
guides.why: The access panels have clips and a rear locating tab that must be released in the correct direction. Seatbelts pass through this area, and the upper trim sits near a convertible flap. Correct reassembly preserves belt accessibility and prevents the flap from becoming caught beneath the panel.

when.summary: When a rear quarter speaker requires replacement or removal after the repair need has been established.
notes: Select the speaker procedure for the fitted audio system; a shared removal method does not establish parts interchangeability.

prepare.title: Plan the complete trim access
prepare.detail: Use the convertible loadspace-trim procedure, including its prerequisite rear seat backrest removal. The convertible top must be fully open for this access sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare for clips and small fasteners
prepare.detail: Have the capability to release the trim clips and speaker bolts without forcing the panels, and a torque wrench suitable for the speaker's low tightening specification.

steps.title: Open the roof and remove the backrest
steps.body: Fully open the convertible top. Remove the rear seat backrest through the prerequisite identified in the [loadspace-trim procedure](#/document/G1692610). This creates the starting access for the surrounding trim panels.

steps.title: Release the upper and middle trim
steps.body: Position the seatbelt guide aside, release the clips and remove the upper panel. Release the middle-panel clips, then pull forward and outward to disengage its rear tab. Move the front and rear safety belts aside and remove the middle panel.

steps.title: Expose and remove the speaker
steps.body: Release the scuff-plate clips and remove that trim, then release and remove the lower loadspace panel. Remove the speaker bolts and speaker, and disconnect its electrical connector. Follow the matching [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1694055) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1693903).

steps.title: Connect and secure the replacement
steps.body: Reverse speaker removal: connect the electrical connector, position the speaker and install its bolts. Tighten the bolts to 2.5 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the trim and belt routing
steps.body: Reverse the trim-removal sequence. Before installing the upper panel, visually inspect the convertible flap and move it aside if required so it cannot become trapped underneath. Refit the upper panel and return the seatbelt guide to position. Keep belt webbing untwisted and belts and buckles accessible as the trim and backrest are restored.

watchFor.title: Middle panel still held at the rear
watchFor.body: Release the rear tab with the specified forward-and-outward movement after releasing the clips.

watchFor.title: Flap or belt caught during assembly
watchFor.body: Reposition the convertible flap before seating the upper panel, and check belt routing as each surrounding panel is restored.

notes: The trim procedure illustrates right-hand access and a left-hand-drive vehicle; the opposite arrangements are similar.

verification.title: Check the speaker attachment
verification.body: Confirm that the electrical connector is restored and the mounting bolts have been tightened to 2.5 Nm.

verification.title: Inspect the flap and seatbelts
verification.body: Verify that the convertible flap is not caught beneath the upper trim, the seatbelt guide is back in position, and belt webbing is untwisted with belts and buckles accessible to occupants.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the convertible rear quarter speaker on vehicles with SYNC.
Remove and install the convertible rear quarter speaker on vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Remove and restore the convertible loadspace trim, including the flap and seatbelt installation precautions.

guides.title: Diagnose no-crank, slow-crank and starter-control faults on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Trace starting complaints through battery condition, start authorization, relay control, loaded cable tests and the appropriate fault-code branch.
guides.introduction: The starter turns the engine, but pressing the start button does not power it directly. The powertrain control module (PCM) checks the required inputs, then energizes the starter relay. Diagnosis therefore follows two paths: whether the vehicle authorizes cranking, and whether the motor receives usable electrical power.
guides.why: A missing start request, poor connection or seized driven component can resemble starter failure. Loaded voltage-drop tests reveal resistance that an unloaded voltage reading can miss.

when.summary: Use when cranking is absent, slow, noisy or persistent, or starting-system fault codes are present.
notes: Remote-start branches apply to automatic-transmission vehicles.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, multimeter, test light, Flex Probe Kit, appropriately fused jumper and remote starter switch. Obtain the specified wiring diagrams. Live-circuit and forced-cranking tests require competent electrical diagnosis; follow the prescribed PARK or NEUTRAL conditions.

prepare.title: Stable battery supply
prepare.detail: Check battery condition and charging-system operation. Diagnostic Methods requires charge above 70%; Test A requires voltage above 12.2 volts throughout. Do not use a charger's highest or boost setting during testing.

steps.title: 1. Establish the complaint and inspect mechanically
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, high-current connections, relevant fuses, the run/start relay and aftermarket wiring. Follow the accessory-belt procedure to remove the belt and check that the crankshaft and belt-driven components rotate without seizure or damage. Correct an obvious cause before continuing.

steps.title: 2. Follow Test A's authorization checks
steps.body: For no crank, check for NO KEY DETECTED. Move a passive key away from the interior's outer edges or far corners and retry starting; a continuing NO KEY DETECTED message requires anti-theft diagnosis. Test communication with the body control module (BCM), instrument panel cluster (IPC) and PCM, then retrieve BCM and PCM diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Follow the charts, prioritizing circuit faults.

steps.title: 3. Check the transmission-specific inputs
steps.body: On automatics, check stoplamps, brake input, the ignition-state change to Start and the transmission's out-of-gear indication in PARK and NEUTRAL. On manuals, check that clutch-bottom-of-travel data changes when fully depressed. Both branches then check engine-cranking request data. Missing inputs lead to their circuit, switch, lighting or transmission tests—not immediate starter replacement.

steps.title: 4. Separate relay control from motor supply
steps.body: Follow the verified loaded relay-control checks, relay supply, prescribed fused bypass, grounds and motor-feed checks. Successful cranking during the specified relay bypass directs relay replacement. If the path reaches the direct starter-command test, stop and obtain the confirmed command-terminal isolation and measurement setup before continuing or choosing a repair. Independent failed-clutch-input checks distinguish ground, wiring and switch faults; P0830:11 has its own disconnected-switch self-test branch. Use flex probes without forcing test-light tips into terminals.

steps.title: 5. Measure losses during slow cranking
steps.body: Fully charge the battery and perform the battery-drain check. Measure at component terminals. Positive-circuit drop of 0.5 volt or less leads to the ground test; higher loss requires cleaning and retesting, then the prescribed solenoid-versus-positive-cable comparison. Ground drop above 0.5 volt requires cleaning battery, body and starter grounds; persistent excessive loss directs negative-cable replacement. Below 0.5 volt with continued slow cranking directs starter replacement.

steps.title: 6. Isolate unusual noise with Test B
steps.body: Check starter mounting first. With ignition off, use the specified remote-switch connection to establish whether engagement causes the noise. Engagement noise leads to starter service; noise unrelated to engagement requires engine diagnosis.

steps.title: 7. Diagnose wake-up faults with Test C
steps.body: The BCM wakes the PCM before cranking so initialization can finish. C113A:11 identifies a detected short to ground; C113A:15 identifies voltage or open-circuit trouble. Disconnecting the PCM and repeating the BCM self-test selects the next branch. Harness tests with the BCM disconnected distinguish wiring faults from the subsequent BCM or PCM confirmation checks.

steps.title: 8. Diagnose P2535 with Test D
steps.body: This code reports crank-detect voltage while the engine is running. Follow voltage checks with the PCM, start-button assembly and BCM disconnected in sequence. Their results distinguish wiring, button, BCM and PCM paths. The button belongs to the front controls interface module (FCIM) and is not separately serviceable; select its touchscreen or non-touchscreen procedure.

steps.title: 9. Confirm a module conclusion
steps.body: At the directed endpoint, inspect connectors for corrosion, damage and displaced pins, repair correctly, latch connections and operate the system again. Check applicable technical service bulletins before a module decision. The PCM branch can direct replacement; the BCM branch requires the vehicle identification number for its guided routine.

watchFor.title: Cranking without a valid measurement
watchFor.body: Voltage-drop testing requires current flow and sound meter contact. A zero reading with no operation does not establish a healthy cable.

watchFor.title: Intermittent concerns
watchFor.body: Do not replace components from a pinpoint-test conclusion when its complaint is absent. Address the cause of damaged or unreliable connections.

notes: Use the complete procedure for connector locations, ignition states and thresholds. Other PCM codes route to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis; other BCM codes route to BCM diagnosis.
The direct starter-command terminal test is outside this guide’s supported checks. Do not substitute a terminal or infer a failed component when a diagnostic route reaches that gate.

diagnostics.finding: P06E9, P162F, or cranking without starting
diagnostics.meaning: P06E9 reports no detected rotation during a crank event; P162F reports excessive crank time.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for P06E9 with no crank. If it cranks, or for P162F and crank/no-start complaints, follow Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis symptom charts.

diagnostics.finding: Starter spins without turning the engine
diagnostics.meaning: Starter engagement, mounting or damaged flexplate teeth may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Inspect mounting and engagement, then the flexplate for damaged, missing or worn teeth.

diagnostics.finding: Starter remains engaged
diagnostics.meaning: The relay or a short to voltage can sustain cranking.
diagnostics.next: Follow the relay-removal check: if cranking stops, replace the relay; if it continues, repair circuit CDC25 (BN/GN) for a short to voltage.

diagnostics.finding: Remote start fails or has poor range
diagnostics.meaning: Feature settings, passive-key condition, wiring or interference may explain the complaint.
diagnostics.next: Use Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis. P1594 and P1595 forced-shutdown faults instead route to Electronic Engine Controls.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating check
verification.body: Operate the system after the directed repair or connector correction and establish whether the original complaint remains.

verification.title: Record loaded test results
verification.body: Record positive and ground voltage-drop readings, including readings after cleaning, alongside the observed cranking behavior and resulting diagnostic decision.

guides.title: Pressure-bleed the 5.2L Mustang brake system
guides.summary: Remove air using the correct wheel order, the required caliper bleeders and the additional scan-tool sequence after hydraulic control unit replacement.
guides.introduction: Brake fluid transmits pedal force through the hydraulic circuits to the calipers. Air compresses under pressure and interferes with that transfer. Pressure bleeding feeds clean fluid through the reservoir while air and old fluid leave through the caliper bleeders. A newly installed hydraulic control unit (HCU) also requires the anti-lock brake system (ABS) service-bleed routine.
guides.why: The wheel sequence differs between left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive vehicles. Multi-piston calipers require attention to both bleeders, and an integral rear parking-brake mechanism has an additional bleeding branch. Following the applicable sequence is essential; clear fluid at one screw does not establish that every required passage has been bled.

when.summary: When the brake hydraulic system requires bleeding, including after installation of a new hydraulic control unit.
notes: Identify steering position and caliper arrangement before starting.

prepare.title: Gather the bleeding equipment
prepare.detail: Use a brake/clutch pressure bleeder/filler, its correct reservoir adapter, a hose and a clean fluid container. Have enough clean, specified brake fluid for the complete operation. Obtain fluid and bleeder-tightening specifications from Brake System Specifications.

prepare.title: Provide access and scan capability
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle lifting and wheel removal using the Wheel and Tire procedure. A new HCU requires a diagnostic scan tool capable of carrying out ABS Service Bleed.

steps.title: Clean and fill the reservoir
steps.body: Clean around the master-cylinder reservoir cap before removing it. Fill with clean, specified fluid. Fit the pressure-bleeder adapter according to its manufacturer's instructions and connect the tank hose. Confirm the tank contains enough fluid to complete bleeding.

steps.title: Apply pressure and access the calipers
steps.body: Open the bleeder-tank valve and apply 207–345 kPa (30–50 psi). Remove the wheels and tires using the [wheel procedure](#/document/G1686507) to reach the bleeders.

steps.title: Follow the correct wheel order
steps.body: For left-hand drive, bleed right rear, left rear, right front, then left front. For right-hand drive, bleed left rear, right rear, left front, then right front. Left and right refer to the vehicle's sides. Complete each wheel before proceeding.

steps.title: Bleed each required screw
steps.body: Remove the screw cap if fitted. Partially fill the clean container with specified fluid, immerse the hose end and connect the other end to the bleeder. On four- or six-piston calipers, bleed the inner screw before the outer screw. Open the screw 180° and allow clear, bubble-free fluid to flow. Close it, disconnect the hose and tighten to specification. Repeat at the remaining wheel ends in order.

steps.title: Apply the integral parking-brake branch only where fitted
steps.body: For rear calipers with an integral parking-brake mechanism, apply and release the parking brake five times, then open the bleeder 180°. Close and tighten to specification when clear, bubble-free fluid flows; repeat as necessary. This branch does not apply to the SVT arrangement with separate parking-brake shoes.

steps.title: Restore the system
steps.body: Refit bleeder caps where provided. Reinstall the wheels and tires using their procedure and lower the vehicle. Close the tank valve, release pressure and remove the bleeding equipment. Fill the reservoir with clean, specified fluid and install its cap.

steps.title: Complete the additional new-HCU sequence
steps.body: If a new HCU has been installed, run the scan tool's ABS Service Bleed instructions after the initial pressure bleed. Then repeat the complete pressure-bleeding procedure and road-test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paintwork
watchFor.body: Immediately wash any affected paintwork with cold water.

watchFor.title: Bubbles still leaving a bleeder
watchFor.body: Continue the prescribed bleed at that point until the discharge is clear and bubble-free.

notes: The new-HCU scan-tool routine supplements the pressure bleed; it requires another pressure bleed afterward.

verification.title: Confirm completion at every bleed point
verification.body: Confirm bubble-free discharge at each required screw, specified screw tightening, restored caps where fitted, reservoir filling and wheel installation.

verification.title: Record the completed sequence
verification.body: Record steering configuration and completion of the applicable caliper branches. For a new HCU, also record ABS Service Bleed, the second pressure bleed and the road-test result.

guides.title: Resolve restraints-module configuration codes U2300:55 and U2300:64
guides.summary: Check configuration status, module identity and factory programming data before deciding whether an RCM or BCM needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) receives vehicle configuration from the body control module (BCM) during its first installed ignition cycle. It stores that information and compares later configuration messages against it. These tests address missing or mismatched configuration so the restraint controller can operate with the correct vehicle setup.
guides.why: Every new RCM initially carries U2300:55 until it successfully receives configuration. U2300:64 can reflect mismatched data or incomplete BCM programming rather than failed hardware. Correct part identification and programming must therefore precede a replacement decision. Once configured, an RCM cannot be transferred to another vehicle.

when.summary: Use when the RCM reports U2300:55 or U2300:64, including after module installation or programming.
notes: Distinguish an on-demand fault from a continuous-memory record before choosing the next action.

prepare.title: Provide programming and identification capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM and BCM self-tests, Log Viewer and programmable module installation (PMI). Obtain vehicle-specific As-Built data and the required build and parts-catalog records.

prepare.title: Prepare safe module access
prepare.detail: Review the safety precautions and disable remote start if fitted. Never move the connected RCM with ignition on. Disconnect SRS components only when the applicable procedure directs.

steps.title: Record the code and its current status
steps.body: With ignition on, run the RCM self-test and record all diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). An on-demand U2300 code goes to part-number checks. If present only as a continuous-memory diagnostic trouble code (CMDTC), clear it and repeat the self-test. No return permits release provided the SRS is otherwise fault-free; an on-demand return requires further diagnosis.

steps.title: Verify the fitted BCM
steps.body: Access the BCM, record its part number and compare it with the vehicle build and parts-catalog records specified in A2. If incorrect, check applicable Ford technical service bulletins first. Without an applicable bulletin, install the correct new BCM and perform PMI using As-Built data, then proceed to final testing.

steps.title: Verify the fitted RCM
steps.body: If the BCM is correct, retrieve and record the RCM part number through the scan tool’s Log Viewer. Compare it with the Ford parts catalog. An incorrect RCM requires the correct unit and PMI using As-Built data before final testing. Physical resemblance is not sufficient identification.

steps.title: Correct configuration in the prescribed order
steps.body: When both part numbers are correct, perform BCM PMI using As-Built data first. Clear codes and repeat the RCM self-test. If either U2300 code is still retrieved, perform RCM PMI using As-Built data, then continue to A4 confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm any remaining RCM fault
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test with ignition on. If the original code remains on-demand, check applicable Ford service bulletins and follow one if relevant. Otherwise install a new RCM and perform PMI using As-Built data. If the original code is absent, proceed to final testing without that replacement.

steps.title: Check both modules before finishing
steps.body: Ensure all SRS components and RCM connectors are connected, then run both RCM and BCM self-tests. Direct RCM faults to restraint-system diagnosis and BCM faults to BCM diagnosis. Do not clear unresolved RCM faults. When both tests are clear, erase continuous-memory codes and perform SRS prove-out.

watchFor.title: A previously configured RCM
watchFor.body: A controller configured to another vehicle cannot be reused as a substitute in this vehicle.

watchFor.title: A changing code status
watchFor.body: U2300:64 can be active during initial prove-out and become a memory code later in the ignition cycle if the correct message eventually arrives.

notes: As-Built data is explicitly required for the PMI operations in this test.

diagnostics.finding: U2300:55 remains on-demand
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM has not successfully received the BCM configuration message.
diagnostics.next: Check module identity and follow the programming sequence; do not replace parts solely because a new RCM carries this code.

diagnostics.finding: U2300:64 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Received configuration disagrees with stored configuration; omitted BCM PMI can also cause this code.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish current from memory status, then verify parts and configuration.

verification.title: Retain the configuration record
verification.body: Record both module part numbers, initial code status, PMI operations performed and the resulting RCM and BCM self-tests.

verification.title: Confirm the final restraint-system state
verification.body: Complete the directed memory clearing and SRS prove-out only after the final fault checks pass. Release requires a fully operational, fault-free system.

General service precautions and applicable system safety requirements.

guides.title: Diagnose U0155:00: restraints module loses instrument-cluster communication
guides.summary: Use network and module self-tests to distinguish intermittent cluster communication loss from a fault requiring further diagnosis or module replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors restraint-system inputs and commands deployment when required. It also uses messages from the instrument panel cluster (IPC) over the high-speed Controller Area Network (HS-CAN). Diagnostic trouble code (DTC) U0155:00 sets when an expected IPC message is missing for 6 seconds. This test investigates that communication loss; the code alone does not establish which module has failed.
guides.why: Network availability, battery-voltage faults and the experience of other receiving modules provide different evidence. Following that order separates a temporary missed message from a persistent problem and prevents replacing the cluster or RCM before checking the conditions that support the decision.
searchTerms: lost communication with instrument panel cluster

when.summary: When the RCM records U0155:00 for lost communication with the instrument panel cluster.
notes: A code that does not return after the specified retest can reflect network traffic or an intermittent condition.

prepare.title: Arrange the diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network testing, RCM and IPC self-tests, code clearing and all-module self-tests. Retain the recorded results needed by later decisions.

prepare.title: Apply restraint-system precautions
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic safety procedure first. Supplemental restraint system (SRS) service requires qualified personnel. Never probe airbag or deployable-device connectors or move the connected RCM with ignition on.

prepare.title: Inspect without disturbing the system
prepare.detail: Thoroughly inspect and verify wiring and connector concerns before testing. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when a prescribed step directs it.

steps.title: Check whether the cluster communicates
steps.body: With ignition on, run the network test. If the IPC fails, follow Communications Network diagnosis for its lack of communication. If it passes, continue: answering a network test does not establish that every expected message reaches the RCM.

steps.title: Determine whether the code returns
steps.body: Perform the RCM self-test, retain its results and clear its DTCs. Wait 10 seconds, then repeat the RCM self-test. If U0155:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at this time; high network traffic or an intermittent fault may explain the earlier code.

steps.title: Check the RCM's recorded voltage codes
steps.body: If U0155:00 returns, inspect the recorded RCM results for U3003:16 or U3003:17. Either code sends diagnosis to Pinpoint Test AJ. Without those codes, proceed to the cluster check.

steps.title: Check the cluster's recorded voltage codes
steps.body: Run the IPC self-test and inspect its results for U3003:16 or U3003:17. If present, follow Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes diagnosis. Otherwise, continue to compare communication reports from other modules.

steps.title: Use other modules to choose the final branch
steps.body: Run all-module self-tests. If U0155:00 is also recorded by the body control module (BCM), audio control module (ACM), or accessory protocol interface module (APIM), if equipped, the endpoint is IPC replacement. Otherwise it is RCM replacement. Before either replacement, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS; follow any matching bulletin instead. Complete replacement through the applicable installation procedure.

watchFor.title: An intermittent result is not a replacement instruction
watchFor.body: A successful retest establishes current operation, not the cause of every previous communication interruption.

watchFor.title: Similar-looking restraint parts may be incompatible
watchFor.body: Verify any replacement SRS component against the Ford parts catalog. Do not choose it solely by physical appearance.

notes: Repair restraint connector-terminal concerns with service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

diagnostics.finding: IPC fails the network test
diagnostics.meaning: The cluster is unavailable to the diagnostic network test.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose communication availability before continuing the message-loss decision tree.

diagnostics.finding: U0155:00 persists with no indicated voltage-code diversion
diagnostics.meaning: The next distinction is whether other specified modules also report losing the cluster.
diagnostics.next: Use the all-module results and bulletin check before selecting IPC or RCM replacement.

verification.title: Confirm restraint-system readiness
verification.body: After directed repairs, repeat the relevant network and self-tests. The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

verification.title: Retain the decision evidence
verification.body: Record network-test status, whether U0155:00 returned after the 10-second wait, voltage-code findings and the other modules reporting communication loss.

guides.title: Diagnose starting problems on the 3.7L Mustang
guides.summary: Separate starting authorization faults, electrical resistance and mechanical engagement problems before replacing the starter or a control module.
guides.introduction: The starter turns the engine, but pressing the start button does not power it directly. The powertrain control module (PCM) must receive the appropriate authorization and pedal or transmission inputs before operating the starter relay. This diagnostic path checks both that control chain and the high-current circuit that actually turns the motor.
guides.why: A silent starter can result from a missing start permission, while slow cranking can come from resistance in an otherwise connected cable. Checking these separately prevents a sound starter from being replaced for a wiring, battery or input fault.

when.summary: Use for no cranking, slow cranking, abnormal starter noise, continued engagement or starting-system fault codes.
notes: Diagnose a currently present concern; an intermittent history alone does not justify component replacement.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, multimeter, test light, correct flex probes, fused jumper and remote starter switch. Follow Wiring Diagrams Cells 20 and 23 and the exact test connections; this includes live circuits and commanded cranking.

prepare.title: Establish battery condition
prepare.detail: Verify charge and charging-system operation. Maintain more than 12.2 volts throughout Test A; do not use a charger's boost setting. The component tests require a fully charged battery and a battery drain check.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint and eliminate obvious causes
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, battery condition, aftermarket wiring, the run/start relay, battery junction box (BJB) connections and specified fuses. Remove the accessory belt using the 3.7L procedure and verify that the crankshaft and driven accessories are not seized or damaged. Correct an obvious cause before continuing.

steps.title: Test A: establish permission to crank
steps.body: Check for NO KEY DETECTED; move the key away from the interior’s outer edges or far corners and retry starting before following anti-theft diagnosis. Run the network test for the body control module (BCM), instrument panel cluster and PCM, then their specified self-tests. Automatic-transmission checks follow stoplamps, brake input, ignition state and Park/Neutral recognition. Manual-transmission checks follow clutch-bottom-of-travel input. Confirm that the engine-cranking parameter identification (PID), or live-data value, becomes active.

steps.title: Test A: separate relay, wiring and starter faults
steps.body: Follow the verified loaded relay-control, relay-supply and momentary fused-jumper checks, then the specified cable, grounding, mounting and voltage-drop branches. A route that reaches the direct starter-command test stops here: confirm the exact command-terminal isolation and measurement setup before continuing or choosing a repair. Other independent branches isolate relay-control shorts and opens or distinguish clutch-switch operation from wiring faults; P0830:11 has its own disconnected-switch self-test. Use flex probes rather than pushing a test-light tip into connectors.

steps.title: Measure losses during slow cranking
steps.body: With Park or Neutral selected, follow the remote-switch component tests. Measure at component terminals, not connector wire ends. Positive-side drop from battery positive to solenoid M should be 0.5 volt or less. If higher, clean connections and retest; the subsequent B-terminal measurement separates cable loss from solenoid loss. Then test starter housing to battery negative. Excessive ground drop requires cleaning and retesting before cable replacement; persistent slow cranking with the specified low ground drop leads to starter replacement.

steps.title: Test B: locate unusual starter noise
steps.body: Check mounting first. The prescribed remote-switch test then establishes whether engagement produces the noise. Engagement noise leads to starter-drive and flywheel-ring-gear inspection; noise unrelated to engagement leads to engine diagnosis.

steps.title: Test C: diagnose the PCM wake-up circuit
steps.body: The BCM wakes the PCM before cranking so initialization can finish. C113A:11 identifies a short-to-ground condition; C113A:15 identifies an open or short-to-voltage condition. Follow the appropriate branch through PCM disconnection, code clearing and self-test, then isolated wiring checks. A changed result directs module checks rather than proving a module defective.

steps.title: Test D: trace an unwanted crank-detect signal
steps.body: P2535 means the PCM detected crank-detect voltage while the engine was running. Follow sequential isolation of the PCM, front controls interface module (FCIM) and BCM to locate the voltage source. The start button is part of the FCIM and cannot be serviced separately; follow the applicable touchscreen or non-touchscreen replacement procedure.

watchFor.title: Premature module replacement
watchFor.body: At module-confirmation endpoints, inspect and repair connector faults, reconnect securely and reproduce the concern. Check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before replacement; BCM endpoints require the vehicle identification number for the guided routine.

notes: Repair corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins as directed; reconnecting a loose plug is not a complete repair if its underlying damage remains.
The direct starter-command terminal test is outside this guide’s supported checks. Do not substitute a terminal or infer a failed component when a diagnostic route reaches that gate.

diagnostics.finding: P06E9 or clutch-switch codes
diagnostics.meaning: P06E9 records absent rotation during a crank event. P0830 and P0830:11 concern clutch input.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for no cranking or clutch codes. If the engine cranks with P06E9, use Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED).

diagnostics.finding: Engine cranks but will not start, P162F, or other PCM codes
diagnostics.meaning: These require the PC/ED symptom path; P162F indicates excessive crank time disabled the starter.
diagnostics.next: Follow PC/ED. Route P1594, remote-start timeout failure, and P1595, remote-start transmission-not-in-Park failure, to 3.7L Electronic Engine Controls.

diagnostics.finding: Starter spins without engine rotation
diagnostics.meaning: Engagement, mounting or flexplate teeth may be faulty.
diagnostics.next: Inspect starter mounting and engagement, then check for damaged, missing or worn flexplate teeth.

diagnostics.finding: Starter does not disengage
diagnostics.meaning: The relay or a short to voltage may sustain cranking.
diagnostics.next: Follow the relay-removal check: stopped cranking calls for a new relay; continued cranking calls for repair of circuit CDC25 (BN/GN).

diagnostics.finding: Remote start fails or has poor range
diagnostics.meaning: Enablement, the passive key or its battery, wiring, aftermarket equipment or radio interference may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Follow Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis. Route other BCM codes through the BCM diagnostic chart.

verification.title: Repeat the affected operation
verification.body: Operate the system after repairs and connector reconnection to establish whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record loaded test results
verification.body: Record the specified cranking voltage-drop readings and repeat them after connection cleaning or cable repair.

guides.title: Diagnose U0151:00 in the occupant classification system
guides.summary: Determine whether missing restraints-module messages reflect an intermittent communication fault, another diagnostic condition or a module replacement branch.
guides.introduction: The occupant classification system module (OCSM) uses messages from the restraints control module (RCM) over high-speed Controller Area Network (HS-CAN2). The RCM also monitors occupant-classification and other sensor inputs as part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 means the OCSM did not receive an expected RCM message; it does not, by itself, establish which component failed.
guides.why: The sequence checks network access, repeatability and codes in other modules before selecting a replacement. This matters because intermittent network traffic and connection faults can resemble module failure, while unnecessary handling of restraint components creates deployment hazards.
searchTerms: lost communication with restraints control module

when.summary: When the OCSM records U0151:00 for a missing message from the restraints control module.
notes: This is a communication diagnosis; it does not authorize probing airbag or pretensioner circuits.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions before beginning. Keep the connected RCM in its original horizontal mounting position while the ignition is ON; moving it can cause unintended deployment.

prepare.title: Prepare the scan tool and inspect connections
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of network tests and module self-tests. Thoroughly inspect wiring and connectors before proceeding, but disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when a pinpoint-test step instructs it.

steps.title: Check whether the RCM communicates
steps.body: With ignition ON, run the network test. If the RCM fails, leave this branch and follow Communications Network diagnosis. If it passes, continue: successful network access does not yet establish that the OCSM receives every expected message.

steps.title: Determine whether the code returns
steps.body: Perform the OCSM self-test, clear its codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. If U0151:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at this time; high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the earlier code.

steps.title: Check the RCM's companion codes
steps.body: If U0151:00 returns, perform the RCM self-test. If U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded, follow Pinpoint Test AU before continuing this communication diagnosis. Otherwise proceed to the OCSM check.

steps.title: Check the OCSM's companion codes
steps.body: Perform the OCSM self-test and review its recorded results. U3003:16 or U3003:17 also routes to Pinpoint Test AU here. Continue only when neither code is recorded.

steps.title: Compare reports from other modules
steps.body: With ignition ON, run all-module self-tests. Determine whether U0151:00 is also set in the anti-lock braking system (ABS) module or body control module (BCM). This distinction selects the final branch.

steps.title: Follow the applicable repair decision
steps.body: Check Ford OASIS for applicable service articles and follow any that address the concern. If none applies, U0151:00 in either the ABS module or BCM directs RCM replacement. If neither records it, the test directs occupant classification system (OCS) sensor replacement. Use the replacement procedure matching seats with or without Multi-Contour equipment.

watchFor.title: Unsafe connector testing
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors. Restraint connector terminal repairs require service pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Incorrect replacement configuration
watchFor.body: Verify the correct part number in the Ford parts catalog. OCS parts are calibrated as assemblies: replace them only in their supplied configuration and protect them from contamination.

notes: A replacement decision is not a completed replacement. Follow the applicable component procedure before returning the restraint system to service.

diagnostics.finding: U0151:00 returns after the OCSM clear-and-retest sequence.
diagnostics.meaning: The expected RCM message is still being missed.
diagnostics.next: Check RCM and OCSM companion codes, then compare ABS and BCM results.

diagnostics.finding: U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded by the RCM or OCSM.
diagnostics.meaning: The communication test requires a different diagnostic branch for this recorded condition.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test AU rather than proceeding directly to module replacement.

verification.title: Preserve the repeatability result
verification.body: Record whether U0151:00 returned after the specified wait and repeated OCSM self-test. A non-returning code establishes present operation, not proof that an intermittent fault cannot recur.

verification.title: Record the selected branch
verification.body: Retain the RCM network result, both module self-tests, ABS/BCM code results and applicable service-article decision with the repair diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: U0151:00 network, repeatability and cross-module checks leading to the appropriate repair branch.

guides.title: Replace a rear brake flexible hose
guides.summary: Renew the rear flexible hose and caliper sealing washers, tighten each connection correctly, and pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The rear flexible hose carries hydraulic pressure from the rigid brake tube to the caliper while accommodating movement at the wheel. Replacing it opens the hydraulic circuit at both ends. The work therefore includes sealing the openings during removal, restoring the connections and bleeding the system after installation.
guides.why: Clean, sealed openings protect the hydraulic circuit from contamination. The caliper connection uses sealing washers that must be discarded during removal. Air admitted when the hose is disconnected must be removed through the required bleeding procedure so hydraulic pressure can operate the brake properly.

when.summary: When a rear brake flexible hose has been confirmed to require replacement.

prepare.title: Lifting and hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Provide a suitable hoist, fitting and torque tools, means to seal all open connections, and the capability to perform the complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Parts and spill precautions
prepare.detail: Have the replacement hose and new caliper sealing washers ready. If brake fluid reaches painted surfaces, wash the affected area immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and disconnect the caliper end
steps.body: Place the vehicle in Neutral and position it on the hoist using the specified lifting points. Remove the caliper flow bolt, disconnect the hose and discard the washers. Seal the open connections as work proceeds.

steps.title: Release the tube fitting and brackets
steps.body: Follow the [hose replacement procedure](#/document/G1693757). Disconnect the metal brake-tube fitting at callout 1, then remove the two hose-bracket bolts and the hose. Keep the tube opening sealed. The upper bracket bolt beside the union is callout 2; the lower bracket bolt is callout 3.

steps.title: Install the hose and new washers
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the upper bracket bolt (callout 2) to 25 Nm and the lower bolt (callout 3) to 30 Nm. Tighten the brake-tube fitting to 17.5 Nm. Use new sealing washers at the caliper and tighten the flow bolt to 47.5 Nm.

steps.title: Pressure-bleed the system
steps.body: Complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00 after installation. Follow that complete procedure for the bleeding operation; reconnecting and tightening the hose is only the mechanical portion of the repair.

watchFor.title: Different bracket torques
watchFor.body: The upper and lower bracket bolts have different tightening requirements. Match each torque to its numbered location.

watchFor.title: Unsupported access
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Use the approved lifting locations and suitable support.

verification.title: Confirm installation details
verification.body: Check that new caliper sealing washers were installed and that the flow bolt, tube fitting and both bracket bolts received their specified tightening.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm the required pressure-bleeding procedure is complete before considering the hose replacement finished.

procedures.purpose: Rear flexible-hose removal and installation, connection torques and the required pressure-bleeding handoff.
Approved lifting points and support precautions for hose access.

guides.title: Replace the fuel filler door and housing assembly
guides.summary: Replace the filler-door assembly through engine-specific filler-pipe removal, boot release and destructive access to its retaining clips.
guides.introduction: The fuel filler door covers the refuelling opening, while its housing attaches the assembly to the body. A boot connects the assembly around the opening behind it. Removing this unit involves work inside the wheel opening and removal of the fuel tank filler pipe before the housing can come free.
guides.why: Removal damages the existing assembly because access holes must be punched to reach its retaining clips. Clearance is limited, so releasing every clip before rotating the housing is central to the sequence. Have the replacement available before starting.

when.summary: When the filler-door assembly needs replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Any removed assembly requires replacement because the removal process damages it.

prepare.title: Arrange parts, tools and access
prepare.detail: Obtain a new fuel filler door assembly and a screwdriver. Plan access inside the wheel opening to release the boot.

prepare.title: Prepare for filler-pipe work
prepare.detail: Use the filler-pipe procedure matching the engine for its access, precautions and installation requirements. This prerequisite makes the job more involved than an exterior door replacement alone.

steps.title: Open the door and remove the filler pipe
steps.body: Open the fuel filler door, then remove the fuel tank filler pipe through the matching [2.3L](#/document/G1671581), [3.7L](#/document/G1671603), [5.0L](#/document/G1671615) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794943) procedure. Complete its fuel-lowering, electrical-isolation and wheel-opening access requirements before releasing the housing.

steps.title: Unseat the boot
steps.body: Work from inside the wheel opening to unseat the fuel filler door assembly boot. This releases the flexible connection before the housing is pulled away from the body.

steps.title: Release the housing clips
steps.body: Follow the indicated locations in the [assembly procedure](#/document/G1693225). Use a screwdriver to punch four access holes, then release the clips through those holes while pulling the housing away. Once all four clips have released, rotate the housing out through the limited clearance.

steps.title: Install the new assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using the new assembly: position and retain the housing, reseat the boot, then complete the engine-specific filler-pipe installation. The damaged old assembly is not suitable for refitting.

watchFor.title: A clip still holding the housing
watchFor.body: Rotation follows release of all four clips. Limited clearance does not change that order.

verification.title: Check reverse-sequence completion
verification.body: Confirm the new housing is retained by its clips, the boot is reseated and the filler pipe has been installed according to the matching engine procedure.
